title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午八月山東當鄉試
監臨御史周〔詠〕先期禮聘儒
官顧視試闈監弗稱鉅典謀
于前巡撫右副都御史姜〔廷〕
〔頤〕展拓維新士聞之思邁嘉
〔命〕烝烝然起矣至期〔之〕〔燁〕等
===
應聘至則以左布政使姚一
〔元〕左叅政楊〔繇〕司提調按察
使祁〔清〕副使潘〔允〕〔端〕司監試
〔之〕〔燁〕與教諭余〔登〕〔庸〕充考試
官學正邵〔廷〕〔臣〕劉〔繹〕〔思〕教諭
張〔源〕戰〔符〕馮〔桂〕〔芳〕周〔校〕充同
考試官諸執事咸慎簡胥命
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午八月，山東當鄉試。監臨御史周〔詠〕先期禮聘儒官，顧視試闈，監弗稱鉅典，謀于前巡撫右副都御史姜〔廷〕〔頤〕，展拓維新。士聞之，思邁嘉〔命〕，烝烝然起矣。至期，〔之〕〔燁〕等應聘至，則以左布政使姚一〔元〕、左叅政楊〔繇〕司提調，按察使祁〔清〕、副使潘〔允〕〔端〕司監試。〔之〕〔燁〕與教諭余〔登〕〔庸〕充考試官，學正邵〔廷〕〔臣〕、劉〔繹〕〔思〕，教諭張〔源〕、戰〔符〕、馮〔桂〕〔芳〕、周〔校〕充同考試官。諸執事咸慎簡，胥命
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], Shandong was due to hold its Provincial Examination. The Supervising Official, Censor Zhou Yong, formally invited educational officials in advance. On inspecting the examination compound, he found it inadequate for this great ceremony [?]. He consulted Jiang Tingyi, the former Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and had it enlarged and renovated. When the scholars heard of this, they eagerly roused themselves, aspiring to fulfill the gracious charge [?].

At the appointed time, Zhiye and the others arrived in response to the invitation. Yao Yiyuan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yang Yao, Left Administration Vice Commissioner, were assigned to serve as Proctors. Qi Qing, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Pan Yunduan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were assigned to oversee the examination. Zhiye and Yu Dengyong, an Instructor, served as Examiners. Shao Tingchen and Liu Yisi, School Rectors, and Zhang Yuan, Zhan Fu, Feng Guifang, and Zhou Xiao, Instructors, served as Associate Examiners. All the functionaries were carefully selected and together received their instructions…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
肅毖合提學副使周〔鑑〕所選
士二千二百有奇三試得士
七十五人爲錄以
獻〔之〕〔燁〕不佞諗于衆曰語云周
之士貴秦之士賤言係乎時
也若齊魯士不然方周衰時
孔門速肖七十餘人者尊六
===
經羞五霸不以時衰少自貶
至秦而孔斌田何伏勝淳于
越高堂生浮丘伯之屬各抱
遺經以自貴重孰能賤之漢
興則申孔京楊之徒並以師
說表見被徵于朝終漢之世
稱儒臣者亦七十餘人何多
punctuated: 肅毖，合提學副使周〔鑑〕所選士二千二百有奇，三試得士七十五人，爲錄以獻。〔之〕〔燁〕不佞，諗于衆曰：「語云：『周之士貴，秦之士賤。』言係乎時也。若齊魯士不然。方周衰時，孔門速肖七十餘人者，尊六經，羞五霸，不以時衰少自貶。至秦，而孔斌、田何、伏勝、淳于越、高堂生、浮丘伯之屬，各抱遺經以自貴重，孰能賤之？漢興，則申、孔、京、楊之徒，並以師說表見，被徵于朝。終漢之世，稱儒臣者亦七十餘人，何多
translation_en:
…solemn and circumspect. Altogether, more than 2,200 candidates selected by Zhou Jian, Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were assembled. Through three examination sessions, seventy-five men were selected, and a record was compiled for presentation to the throne.
We, Zhi and Ye, unworthy though we are, addressed the assembled company: “There is a saying: ‘The scholars of Zhou were honored; the scholars of Qin were despised.’ This means that their standing depended upon the times. Yet the scholars of Qi and Lu were different. When Zhou was declining, the more than seventy outstanding disciples [?] in the school of Confucius revered the Six Classics and disdained the Five Hegemons. They did not lower themselves in the slightest because their age was in decline. Under Qin, men such as Kong Bin, Tian He, Fu Sheng, Chunyu Yue, Gaotang Sheng, and Fuqiu Bo each held fast to the surviving Classics and maintained their own dignity. Who could render them base? When Han arose, men such as Shen, Kong, Jing, and Yang distinguished themselves through the teachings transmitted by their masters and were summoned to court. Over the course of the Han dynasty, those acclaimed as Confucian ministers likewise numbered more than seventy. Why were so many…”

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
齊若此山川奇秀鍾于士人
周孔之敎人人誦法是以周
不能衰秦不能賊至于今而
益盛也令夫凡山皆東屬乃
東方之山則自太行薊門遼
海島嶼碁置起爲登萊特起
爲泰岱逶迤而至滕嶧自東
===
而西屬焉
京師稱天府以有東方爲左掖
也凡水皆東注乃濟水則由
濟源伏地發於東方自東西
注又折而北焉四方輸貢
京師以有濟水轉漕也諦觀形
勢殆拱護
punctuated:
齊若此？山川奇秀，鍾于士人，周孔之敎，人人誦法，是以周不能衰，秦不能賊，至于今而益盛也。
令夫凡山皆東屬，乃東方之山，則自太行、薊門、遼海，島嶼碁置，起爲登萊，特起爲泰岱，逶迤而至滕嶧，自東而西屬焉。京師稱天府，以有東方爲左掖也。凡水皆東注，乃濟水則由濟源伏地，發於東方，自東西注，又折而北焉。四方輸貢京師，以有濟水轉漕也。諦觀形勢，殆拱護
translation_en:
…so many in Qi [?]? The extraordinary beauty of its mountains and rivers is concentrated in its scholars. Everyone recites and follows the teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. Thus the Zhou could not diminish them, nor could the Qin destroy them; down to the present they have flourished ever more abundantly.
Now [?], all mountains extend eastward in connected ranges. Yet the mountains of the eastern region, stretching from Taihang, Jimen, and the Liaohai coast, with islands scattered like pieces on a game board, rise to form Dengzhou and Laizhou, tower distinctively as Mount Tai, and wind onward to Teng and Yi, forming a connected range from east to west. The capital is called a heavenly storehouse because it has the eastern region as its left flank. All waters flow eastward, yet the Ji River, flowing underground from Jiyuan, emerges in the eastern region, flows from east to west, and then turns north. Tribute from the four quarters is transported to the capital thanks to the Ji River’s provision for grain transport. Examining the configuration of the terrain closely, one sees that it serves to encircle and protect…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
宸居以聳
億萬載無疆之業在山川且有效
忠
國家之意是以產士其間才美
博大殫猷宣力光輔我
熙朝項來尤盛山川之助多矣乃
今七十五人者宗周孔畢管
晏有速肖之風焉修明經術
曉暢世務有漢儒之指焉主
司得士如斯亦既爲
===
國家慶矣顧難逢而希遘者時
也孔門多王佐才終身不仕
即仕而爲宰僅沾一命無幾
人焉今
punctuated: 宸居，以聳億萬載無疆之業。在山川且有效忠國家之意，是以產士其間，才美博大，殫猷宣力，光輔我熙朝，項來尤盛，山川之助多矣。乃今七十五人者，宗周孔，畢管晏，有速肖之風焉；修明經術，曉暢世務，有漢儒之指焉。主司得士如斯，亦既爲國家慶矣。顧難逢而希遘者，時也。孔門多王佐才，終身不仕；即仕而爲宰，僅沾一命，無幾人焉。今
translation_en:
…the imperial residence, thereby exalting the boundless imperial enterprise for countless ages. Even the mountains and rivers seem intent on serving the state loyally. Thus they produce men of outstanding and expansive talent, who exhaust their wisdom and exert their strength to lend illustrious support to our glorious dynasty. Of late [?], such men have been especially numerous: great indeed is the contribution of these mountains and rivers.

Now these seventy-five men take the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as their models, emulate Guan Zhong and Yan Ying [?], and display a disposition to resemble these predecessors swiftly [?]. They cultivate and elucidate classical learning and thoroughly understand contemporary affairs, possessing the aims of the Han Confucian scholars. That the Examiners have obtained such men is already cause for celebration for the state. Yet what is difficult to encounter and seldom comes one's way is a favorable time. Among Confucius's disciples were many with the talent to assist a true king, yet they remained without office throughout their lives. Even those who entered service as local administrators and received a mere initial appointment were few. Now…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
主上明聖登崇儁偉抱藝之士咸
得自效邁漢代遠甚遇
主如斯而罔思策奮不前輩是程
無乃負於時乎〔之煒〕聞之岱
宗之爲宗山所宗也濟水之
爲濟濟
===
國用也諸士表樹節槩聳若岱
宗凡所展施期濟實用使人
稱曰七十五人亦速肖耳視
漢儒殆過焉主司與有榮矣
勉之哉勉之哉維時總理河
道提督軍務今兵部左侍郎
翁〔大立〕巡撫山東右僉都御
史梁〔夢龍〕巡按直隷監察御
punctuated:
主上明聖，登崇儁偉，抱藝之士咸得自效，邁漢代遠甚。遇主如斯，而罔思策奮，不前輩是程，無乃負於時乎？〔之煒〕聞之：岱宗之爲宗，山所宗也；濟水之爲濟，濟國用也。諸士表樹節槩，聳若岱宗；凡所展施，期濟實用。使人稱曰：「七十五人亦速肖耳，視漢儒殆過焉。」主司與有榮矣。勉之哉！勉之哉！
維時，總理河道提督軍務、今兵部左侍郎翁〔大立〕，巡撫山東右僉都御史梁〔夢龍〕，巡按直隷監察御
translation_en:
…Our sovereign is enlightened and sagely, elevating men of outstanding ability. All scholars possessed of learning and skill can put their talents to use, far surpassing the opportunities of the Han age. To encounter such a sovereign yet give no thought to exerting oneself, nor take one's predecessors as models—would this not be to fail one's times? I, Zhiwei 〔之煒〕, have heard this: Daizong is called the ancestral mountain because the other mountains acknowledge its primacy; the Ji River is called Ji because it supplies the state's needs. May you gentlemen establish your integrity and moral resolve, towering like Daizong; in all that you undertake, aim to meet practical needs. Let people say: “These seventy-five men, too, swiftly resemble their predecessors [?]; compared with the Han scholars, they perhaps surpass them.” The examiners will share in that honor. Strive for it! Strive for it!
At this time, those serving included Weng Dali 翁〔大立〕, Director-General of River Conservancy and Superintendent of Military Affairs, now Left Vice Minister of War; Liang Menglong 梁〔夢龍〕, Grand Coordinator of Shandong and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; and the Regional Inspecting Censor for Zhili…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
史謝〔廷傑〕蘇〔士潤〕雅尚文教
崇獎士風總理河道提督軍
務右副都御史潘〔季馴〕巡按
山東監察御史盛〔時選〕被
命維新聲猷漸布戶部員外郎程
〔文著〕主事翟〔希魯〕崔〔行可〕宋
〔豸〕工部郎中張〔純〕員外郎呂
===
〔一靜〕主事劉〔泮〕奉使東方樂
觀盛舉布政司右叅政張〔邦〕
〔士〕吳〔文華〕左叅議馮〔謙〕按察
司副使溫〔如玉〕朱〔卿〕徐〔用檢〕
孫〔應元〕劉〔有誠〕劉〔經緯〕楊〔兆〕
蔡〔可賢〕王〔維寧〕劉〔庠〕僉事蹇
〔達〕葉〔憲〕甄〔敬〕劉〔田〕王〔之弼〕宋
punctuated: 史謝〔廷傑〕、蘇〔士潤〕雅尚文教，崇獎士風。總理河道提督軍務右副都御史潘〔季馴〕、巡按山東監察御史盛〔時選〕被命維新，聲猷漸布。戶部員外郎程〔文著〕、主事翟〔希魯〕、崔〔行可〕、宋〔豸〕，工部郎中張〔純〕、員外郎呂〔一靜〕、主事劉〔泮〕奉使東方，樂觀盛舉。布政司右叅政張〔邦〕〔士〕、吳〔文華〕，左叅議馮〔謙〕，按察司副使溫〔如玉〕、朱〔卿〕、徐〔用檢〕、孫〔應元〕、劉〔有誠〕、劉〔經緯〕、楊〔兆〕、蔡〔可賢〕、王〔維寧〕、劉〔庠〕，僉事蹇〔達〕、葉〔憲〕、甄〔敬〕、劉〔田〕、王〔之弼〕、宋
translation_en:
…Censors Xie Tingjie and Su Shirun have long esteemed literary education and encouraged the scholarly ethos. Pan Jixun, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Director-General of River Conservancy and Superintendent of Military Affairs, and Sheng Shixuan, Investigating Censor on patrol in Shandong, have only recently received their appointments; their reputations and accomplishments are gradually becoming known. Cheng Wenzhu, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Zhai Xilu, Cui Xingke, and Song Zhi, Secretaries in that ministry; together with Zhang Chun, Director in the Ministry of Works, Lü Yijing, Vice Director, and Liu Pan, Secretary, have come east on official missions and are pleased to witness this grand undertaking.

Zhang Bangshi and Wu Wenhua serve as Right Administration Vice Commissioners in the Provincial Administration Commission, and Feng Qian as Left Administration Assistant Commissioner. Wen Ruyu, Zhu Qing, Xu Yongjian, Sun Yingyuan, Liu Youcheng, Liu Jingwei, Yang Zhao, Cai Kexian, Wang Weining, and Liu Xiang serve as Surveillance Vice Commissioners in the Provincial Surveillance Commission. Jian Da, Ye Xian, Zhen Jing, Liu Tian, Wang Zhibi, and Song… serve as Surveillance Assistant Commissioners.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
〔守約〕任〔彬〕吳〔一本〕都指揮使
司署都指揮僉事李〔希周〕張
〔承業〕遷秩副使羅〔良〕右叅議
顏〔鯨〕僉事徐〔炳〕先後規畫與
有勞勩錄未紀序宜紀之
浙江嘉興府儒學教授李〔之
嘩〕謹序
punctuated:
〔守約〕、任〔彬〕、吳〔一本〕，都指揮使司署都指揮僉事李〔希周〕、張〔承業〕，遷秩副使羅〔良〕、右叅議顏〔鯨〕、僉事徐〔炳〕，先後規畫，與有勞勩。錄未紀，序宜紀之。
浙江嘉興府儒學教授李〔之嘩〕謹序。
translation_en:
… Song Shouyue, Ren Bin, and Wu Yiben; Li Xizhou and Zhang Chengye, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners in the Regional Military Commission; and the officials promoted to new ranks—Vice Commissioner Luo Liang, Assistant Administration Commissioner Yan Jing, and Assistant Commissioner Xu Bing—all contributed their efforts to planning at various stages. Since the record has not noted their contributions, it is fitting to record them in this preface.
Respectfully prefaced by Li Zhihua, Professor of the Confucian School of Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年山東鄉試
監臨官
巡按山東監察御史周詠〔思養河南延津縣人 壬戌進士〕
提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使姚一元〔惟貞浙江長興縣人 甲辰進士〕
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政楊縧〔特甫應天府衛籍江西 泰和縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
山東等處提刑按察司按察使祁清〔子揚浙江山陰縣人 丁未進士〕
山東等處提刑按察司副使潘允端〔仲履直隸上海縣人 壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
浙江嘉興府儒學教授李之燁〔光甫江西廬陵縣人 戊午貢士〕
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教諭余登庸〔應徵湖廣蘄州人 辛酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南彰德府磁州儒學學正邵廷臣〔藎夫福建侯官縣籍 福清縣人甲子貢士〕
湖廣黃州府蘄州儒學學正劉繹恩〔宗文廣西靈川縣籍 臨桂縣人戊午貢士〕
湖廣武昌府咸寧縣儒學教諭張源〔以深廣西賓州人 辛酉貢士〕
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教諭戰符〔廷信湖廣蘄州人 戊午貢士〕
河南歸德府永城縣儒學教諭馮桂芳〔在培河南陳州衛籍湖 廣黃陂縣人戊午貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年山東鄉試。

監臨官。
巡按山東監察御史周詠〔思養，河南延津縣人，壬戌進士〕。

提調官。
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使姚一元〔惟貞，浙江長興縣人，甲辰進士〕。
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政楊縧〔特甫，應天府衛籍，江西泰和縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官。
山東等處提刑按察司按察使祁清〔子揚，浙江山陰縣人，丁未進士〕。
山東等處提刑按察司副使潘允端〔仲履，直隸上海縣人，壬戌進士〕。

考試官。
浙江嘉興府儒學教授李之燁〔光甫，江西廬陵縣人，戊午貢士〕。
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教諭余登庸〔應徵，湖廣蘄州人，辛酉貢士〕。

同考試官。
河南彰德府磁州儒學學正邵廷臣〔藎夫，福建侯官縣籍，福清縣人，甲子貢士〕。
湖廣黃州府蘄州儒學學正劉繹恩〔宗文，廣西靈川縣籍，臨桂縣人，戊午貢士〕。
湖廣武昌府咸寧縣儒學教諭張源〔以深，廣西賓州人，辛酉貢士〕。
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教諭戰符〔廷信，湖廣蘄州人，戊午貢士〕。
河南歸德府永城縣儒學教諭馮桂芳〔在培，河南陳州衛籍，湖廣黃陂縣人，戊午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shandong Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570).

Supervising Official

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見
子夏曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏
曰富哉言乎
敦厚以崇禮
以不忍人之心行不忍人之政治天下可
運之掌上
===
易
六爻發揮旁通情也時乘六龍以御天也
上九弗損益之无咎貞吉利有攸往得臣
无家
聖人有以見天下之賾而擬諸其形容象
其物宜是故謂之象
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有動
而不括是以出而有獲語成器而動者
也
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。」樊遲退，見子夏，曰：「鄉也吾見於夫子而問知，子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』何謂也？」子夏曰：「富哉言乎！」

敦厚以崇禮。

以不忍人之心，行不忍人之政，治天下可運之掌上。

易

六爻發揮，旁通情也；時乘六龍，以御天也。

上九：弗損益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。

聖人有以見天下之賾，而擬諸其形容，象其物宜，是故謂之象。

君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Fan Chi withdrew and went to see Zixia. He said, “Earlier I went to see the Master and asked about wisdom. The Master said, ‘Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.’ What does this mean?” Zixia said, “How rich in meaning are these words!”

Cultivate generosity and sincerity, thereby honoring ritual propriety.

With a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others, practice government that cannot bear to cause others suffering, and governing all under Heaven will be as easy as turning something in the palm of your hand.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

The six lines unfold their meaning, comprehensively revealing the circumstances they express. At the proper times, he rides the six dragons to direct the course of Heaven.

Nine at the top: Without diminishing him, increase him. No blame. Constancy brings good fortune. It is favorable to have somewhere to go. He gains a servant who has no private household.

The sages had the means to perceive the profound complexities of all under Heaven. They represented these through their forms and appearances, making images appropriate to the things represented. Hence these are called “images.”

The gentleman stores his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. How could anything be unfavorable? He acts without being constrained; thus, when he goes forth, he achieves results. This speaks of one who acts only after his capacities have been fully developed.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
書
伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
浮于濟漯達于河
今民將在祗遹乃文考紹聞衣德言往敷
求于殷先哲王用保乂民汝丕遠惟商
耇成人宅心知訓別求聞由古先哲王
用康保民
政貴有恒辭尚體要
詩
===
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播百
穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌陰
四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭
瞻彼洛矣維水泱泱君子至止福祿如茨
韎韐有奭以作六師
皇矣上帝臨下有赫監觀四方求民之莫
允文文王克開厥後
春秋
冬十有二月齊侯鄭伯盟于石門〔隱公三〕
punctuated:
書

伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞，往，欽哉！」

浮于濟、漯，達于河。

今民將在祗遹乃文考，紹聞衣德。言往敷求于殷先哲王，用保乂民。汝丕遠惟商耇成人，宅心知訓，別求聞由古先哲王，用康保民。

政貴有恒，辭尚體要。

詩

晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。

瞻彼洛矣，維水泱泱。君子至止，福祿如茨。韎韐有奭，以作六師。

皇矣上帝，臨下有赫。監觀四方，求民之莫。

允文文王，克開厥後。

春秋

冬十有二月，齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門。〔隱公三〕
translation_en:
Book of Documents

Bo [Boyi] bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long. The emperor said: “Yes. Go and attend reverently to your duties!”

They floated along the Ji and Luo rivers and reached the Yellow River.

Now, governing the people will depend on reverently following your deceased father, continuing his teachings and clothing yourself in his virtue. Go and seek widely among the wise former kings of Yin the means to protect and govern the people. You should also reflect deeply upon Shang’s aged and accomplished men, take their intentions to heart, and understand their teachings. Seek further to learn and follow the wise kings of antiquity, thereby bringing peace and protection to the people.

In government, constancy is prized; in pronouncements, substance and concision are esteemed.

Book of Odes

By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains. In the second month, they cut the ice with resounding blows; in the third month, they store it in the icehouse. Early in the fourth month, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives.

Look at the Luo River, its waters vast and flowing. The lord has arrived; blessings and emoluments cluster thick as thatch. His reddish leather knee-covering shines bright as he rouses the six armies.

August is the Lord on High, glorious as he looks down below. He surveys the four quarters, seeking repose for the people.

Truly cultivated was King Wen, able to open the way for his descendants.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In winter, in the twelfth month, the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen. 〔Duke Yin, third …〕

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
年秋七月庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于瓦
屋〔隱公八年〕
秋公會宋人齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕
秋楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋〔襄公元年〕
春公觀魚于棠〔隱公五年〕夏五月宋人及
楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕
禮記
天子之六府曰司土司木司水司草司器
司貨典司六職
大德不官大道不器大信不約大時不齊
然後聖人作爲父子君臣以爲紀綱紀綱
旣正天下大定
產萬物者聖也
===
第貳場
論
聖王脩身立政之本
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
punctuated:
年。秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱公八年〕。
秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐〔莊公二十有六年〕。
秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋〔襄公元年〕。
春，公觀魚于棠〔隱公五年〕。夏五月，宋人及楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕。
禮記
天子之六府，曰司土、司木、司水、司草、司器、司貨，典司六職。
大德不官，大道不器，大信不約，大時不齊。
然後聖人作爲父子、君臣，以爲紀綱。紀綱旣正，天下大定。
產萬物者，聖也。
第貳場
論
聖王脩身立政之本。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
translation_en:
…year. In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei made a covenant at Wawu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Yin〕
In autumn, the duke joined men of Song and Qi in attacking Xu. 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang〕
In autumn, Prince Renfu of Chu led an army to invade Song. 〔First year of Duke Xiang〕
In spring, the duke watched fishing at Tang. 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin〕 In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and Chu made peace. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan〕
Record of Rites
The Son of Heaven’s six storehouses are those administering land, timber, water, vegetation, implements, and valuables; they oversee these six functions.
Great virtue is not confined to an office; the great Way is not confined to a particular instrument; great trustworthiness requires no pledge; the great seasons are not uniform.
Then the sages established the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, to serve as the governing framework. Once that framework was properly ordered, all under Heaven enjoyed profound stability.
That which brings forth the myriad things is sageliness.
Second Session
Discourse
The foundation of sage kings’ self-cultivation and establishment of government.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting remission of half the land tax throughout the realm. 〔Second year of Emperor Wen〕

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬
聖駕大閱
賜廷臣白金文綺謝表〔隆慶三年〕
判語五條
照刷文卷
欺隱田糧
禁止迎送
辯明寃枉
盗決河防
===
第叁場
策五道
問明君以務學爲急聖學以正心爲要自
二帝三王至於漢唐宋英君誼辟未有
外心以言學者載之史冊固班班可考
也可指而言之歟夫經筵之典重矣古
人有坐講殿上而人君起敬者有反覆
開導而人主感悟者有召對之儀隆矣古
punctuated:
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕。
擬聖駕大閱，賜廷臣白金文綺謝表〔隆慶三年〕。
判語五條：照刷文卷；欺隱田糧；禁止迎送；辯明寃枉；盗決河防。

第叁場
策五道
問：明君以務學爲急，聖學以正心爲要。自二帝三王至於漢唐宋，英君誼辟，未有外心以言學者，載之史冊，固班班可考也。可指而言之歟？夫經筵之典重矣，古人有坐講殿上而人君起敬者，有反覆開導而人主感悟者。有召對之儀隆矣，古
translation_en:
Draft an appointment proclamation in the manner of the Tang court appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent (sixteenth year of Zhenguan).
Draft a memorial of thanks for the silver and figured silks bestowed upon court officials on the occasion of His Majesty’s grand military review (third year of Longqing).
Five legal judgments: auditing official documents and files; fraudulently concealing land and grain-tax liabilities; prohibiting ceremonial receptions and send-offs; establishing the truth in cases of wrongful accusation; unlawfully breaching river embankments.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: An enlightened ruler regards diligent learning as urgent; learning directed toward sagehood takes rectifying the mind as its essential task. From the Two Emperors and Three Kings down to the outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns of the Han, Tang, and Song, none discussed learning apart from the mind. The historical records contain abundant, clearly documented evidence of this. Can you identify and discuss particular examples? The institution of the Classics Colloquium is indeed weighty. In antiquity, some men lectured while seated in the palace hall and inspired reverence in their sovereigns; others offered repeated explanations and guidance, moving their rulers to understanding. There is also the solemn ceremonial of being summoned to an imperial audience [?]. In antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
人有隨事隨陳而稱上意者有議論剴
切而稱小相者史以載事也有不欲人
君自觀史者有請於禁中設起居注者
諫以弼違也有不冠不見而輙可其奏
者有以人爲鑑而疏比弦韋者其人其
說可得陳歟夫是四者裨君心關聖學
一也不知如何而可以臻實效歟洪惟
我
聖祖開基之初日晉基濂輩相與講論圖維其
實錄讜言垂炳星日所以爲萬世心法
之要者可得而鋪張揚厲之歟方今
===
皇上天縱聖神
臨御四年以來所以懋敬典學者淵以穆光且
大也而在
廷諸臣感會風雲千載一時其進講奏對紀
述陳謨亦既精白獻應矣然所以弘
啓沃于
經筵效賛襄于
punctuated: 人有隨事隨陳而稱上意者，有議論剴切而稱小相者。史以載事也，有不欲人君自觀史者，有請於禁中設起居注者。諫以弼違也，有不冠不見而輙可其奏者，有以人爲鑑而疏比弦韋者。其人其說，可得陳歟？夫是四者，裨君心、關聖學，一也。不知如何而可以臻實效歟？洪惟我聖祖開基之初，日晉基濂輩，相與講論圖維，其實錄讜言垂炳星日，所以爲萬世心法之要者，可得而鋪張揚厲之歟？方今皇上天縱聖神，臨御四年以來，所以懋敬典學者，淵以穆，光且大也。而在廷諸臣，感會風雲，千載一時，其進講奏對、紀述陳謨，亦既精白獻應矣。然所以弘啓沃于經筵，效賛襄于
translation_en:
…there were men who offered their observations as circumstances arose and satisfied the sovereign’s wishes, and men whose incisive discussions earned them the designation “little chief councillor.” History serves to record events: there were those who opposed the ruler’s personally inspecting the historical record, and those who requested that a diary of activity and repose be instituted within the palace. Remonstrance serves to correct errors: there were men whom the ruler would not receive without wearing his cap and whose memorials he readily approved, and men who took other people as a mirror and whose memorials were likened to bowstring and leather, complementary correctives to conduct. Can you set forth who these men were and what they said? These four activities alike assist the ruler’s mind and bear upon his sagely learning. How can they be made to produce actual results?
We reverently consider how, when our sagely ancestor first established the dynasty, he daily summoned men such as Ji and Lian [?], discussing and deliberating with them. The faithful records and forthright words from those occasions shine like the stars and sun for posterity. Can you fully expound and celebrate what makes them essential to the discipline of the mind for all ages?
Today His Majesty is endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom. In the four years since he assumed the throne, his efforts to cultivate reverence and apply himself constantly to learning have been profound and solemn, brilliant and great. The ministers at court, meeting their sovereign as clouds and winds converge, have encountered an opportunity that comes but once in a thousand years. In presenting lectures and answering imperial questions, recording events and offering counsel, they have already responded with the utmost purity and sincerity. Yet as to how they may extend their work of enlightening and nourishing the imperial mind at the Classics Colloquium, and render assistance at …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
召對直筆紀諸蘭臺昌言協于
彤陛由是以輔養
上德而光昭
祖烈者當必有要也諸士子行將爲
明時獻納矣試詳著於篇以觀致
君之學
問五經自孔子删述之後萬世憲章定矣
厥後談經之士往往擬作果能于聖經
有所羽翼耶慨惟古書自經秦火卒多
===
残失中或以卜筮存或以孔壁存能識
其全耶不知餘經又何賴以不失今考
之連山歸藏蓋並易矣元豐中有疑其
爲僞書者何耶至易林易通易賛易論
易緯易樞易筌古易五家皆以擬易不
知于四聖之旨何如三墳五典蓋說書
也然諸家各以意評或又有連山歸藏
之論何所取耶若九家書三家經文二
十五家書中候中文釋問演範九意皆
punctuated:
召對，直筆紀諸蘭臺，昌言協于彤陛，由是以輔養上德而光昭祖烈者，當必有要也。諸士子行將爲明時獻納矣，試詳著於篇，以觀致君之學。
問：五經自孔子删述之後，萬世憲章定矣。厥後談經之士，往往擬作，果能于聖經有所羽翼耶？慨惟古書自經秦火，卒多残失，中或以卜筮存，或以孔壁存，能識其全耶？不知餘經又何賴以不失？今考之，《連山》《歸藏》蓋並《易》矣，元豐中有疑其爲僞書者，何耶？至《易林》《易通》《易賛》《易論》《易緯》《易樞》《易筌》《古易》五家，皆以擬《易》，不知于四聖之旨何如？《三墳》《五典》蓋說《書》也，然諸家各以意評，或又有《連山》《歸藏》之論，何所取耶？若九家《書》、三家《經文》、二十五家《書》、《中候》《中文》《釋問》《演範》《九意》，皆
translation_en:
…at audiences convened by imperial summons; to record events with an upright brush in the imperial archives; and to offer sound counsel before the vermilion steps. There must surely be essential principles by which these activities can nurture His Majesty’s virtue and gloriously illuminate his ancestors’ achievements. You candidates will soon be presenting counsel in this enlightened age. Set this out in detail in your essays, so that we may assess your learning concerning how to bring the ruler to the highest attainment.
Question: After Confucius edited and transmitted the Five Classics, authoritative standards were established for all ages. Scholars discussing the classics thereafter frequently composed works in imitation of them. Could these really supplement and support the sages’ classics? Regrettably, after the Qin book burning, ancient writings suffered much damage and loss. Some survived because they concerned divination, others because they were preserved within the walls of Confucius’s house. Can their complete contents be known? And upon what did the other classics depend for their survival? Now, on examination, the Linked Mountains (Lianshan) and Return to the Hidden (Guicang) were apparently counterparts of the Changes. Why did some people in the Yuanfeng era suspect them of being spurious books? As for the Forest of Changes, Comprehensive Interpretation of the Changes, Praise of the Changes, Discourse on the Changes, Apocrypha of the Changes, Pivot of the Changes, Elucidation of the Changes, and the five schools of the Ancient Changes [?], all were composed in imitation of the Changes. How do they accord with the purport of the Four Sages? The Three Ancient Records (Sanfen) and Five Canons (Wudian) apparently expound the Documents. Yet the various scholars each assess them according to their own views, and some also discuss the Linked Mountains and Return to the Hidden. What should we accept from these accounts? As for the nine schools of the Documents, the three schools of the Canonical Text, the twenty-five schools of the Documents, the Central Observations (Zhonghou), Central Text (Zhongwen), Explanation of Questions (Shiwen), Elaboration of the Great Plan (Yanfan), and Nine Meanings (Jiuyi) [the grouping and titles are uncertain], all …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
以擬書不知于典謨之旨何如有義駁
八卷奏事一卷問難二卷箋傳是非二
卷雜問七卷擬詩誰最爲近有或刪爲
八十五篇或刪爲四十六篇或合爲四
十九篇或傳十七篇擬禮誰最爲眞春
秋聖人筆削然猶有四家二十三家春
秋是卽孔子所脩耶抑前別有春秋耶
左氏公羊穀梁皆傳春秋先儒各加評
議是耶非耶何氏五始三科九旨七等
===
六輔二類之義于三子何所宗信圖緯
繁露調人諸作于春秋何所發明凡諸
作者多當時名賢其大旨載在典籍中
可考諸士子能一一掇拾復我耶窮經
致用迺學術之大有能發其藴者異日
卽能大有造者也
問書曰一德一心言心也又曰學古入官
言學也是心之貴一而學之貴正自古
尚之矣心一則純二則雜學誠則正僞
punctuated:
以擬《書》，不知于典謨之旨何如？有《義駁》八卷、《奏事》一卷、《問難》二卷、《箋傳是非》二卷、《雜問》七卷，擬《詩》，誰最爲近？有或刪爲八十五篇，或刪爲四十六篇，或合爲四十九篇，或傳十七篇，擬《禮》，誰最爲眞？《春秋》，聖人筆削，然猶有四家、二十三家《春秋》，是卽孔子所脩耶？抑前別有《春秋》耶？左氏、公羊、穀梁皆傳《春秋》，先儒各加評議，是耶非耶？何氏五始、三科、九旨、七等、六輔、二類之義，于三子何所宗信？《圖緯》、《繁露》、《調人》諸作，于《春秋》何所發明？凡諸作者，多當時名賢，其大旨載在典籍中可考。諸士子能一一掇拾復我耶？窮經致用，迺學術之大，有能發其藴者，異日卽能大有造者也。

問：《書》曰：「一德一心。」言心也。又曰：「學古入官。」言學也。是心之貴一，而學之貴正，自古尚之矣。心一則純，二則雜；學誠則正，僞
translation_en:
…were modeled on the Book of Documents; how do they accord with the purport of its Canons and Counsels? There are eight juan of Refutations of Interpretations (Yibo), one juan of Memorials on Affairs (Zoushi), two juan of Questions and Challenges (Wennan), two juan of Merits and Errors of the Annotations and Commentaries (Jianzhuan shifei), and seven juan of Miscellaneous Questions (Zawen). Among these works modeled on the Book of Odes, which comes closest to it? Some abridged the rites texts to eighty-five chapters, some to forty-six; some combined them into forty-nine chapters, while others transmitted seventeen. Among these versions of the rites texts, which is most authentic? The Spring and Autumn Annals underwent the Sage’s editorial additions and deletions, yet there are also Annals associated with four schools and with twenty-three schools. Are these the very work Confucius edited, or were there other Annals before it? Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang all supplied commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and earlier scholars offered their respective assessments: were these right or wrong? In Master He’s interpretations of the Five Beginnings, Three Categories, Nine Purports, Seven Ranks, Six Supports, and Two Classes, which of these three masters did he follow and trust? What light do such works as the Charts and Apocrypha (Tuwei), Luxuriant Dew (Fanlu), and Mediating Men (Diaoren) [?] shed on the Spring and Autumn Annals? Most of these authors were renowned worthies of their times, and the main purport of their writings is recorded in texts that can be consulted. Can you candidates gather these points one by one and answer me? To investigate the Classics exhaustively and put them to practical use is the great undertaking of scholarship. Those who can disclose their underlying meaning will one day be capable of great achievements.

Question: The Book of Documents says, “One in virtue and one in mind.” This speaks of the mind. It also says, “Study antiquity and enter office.” This speaks of learning. Thus unity of mind and correctness of learning have been esteemed since antiquity. When the mind is single, it is pure; when divided, it is mixed. When learning is sincere, it is correct; when false …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
則邪所謂二者豈必拂禮背義出檻紓
籌者流耶所謂僞者豈必離經畔道歸
楊附墨者流耶要之懷一念之私不可
對人言不可與天知者皆二也投一時
之好炫奇說異飾貌文奸者皆僞也式
稽往牒君子之有益人國有裨聖道者
若阿衡佐命若篤棐輔德若丹書矢戒
若典學沃心其心術之純學術之正固
光盎聲施千古奇絕矣嗣是而後有始
終爲韓有感激馳驅有心事青白有精
忠貫日心術正矣不知于學術純焉否
也有下帷發憤有原道詆佛有鳴道淶
水有力復古文學術偉矣不知其心術
正焉否也可得而尚論歟夫有純心必
有正學而學術不正則心術從可窺也
國家明道正心崇文啓學二百餘年凡在菁
莪棫樸涵育
聖神之化者率能以正大光明之心而爲純粹
punctuated: 則邪。所謂二者，豈必拂禮背義、出檻紓籌者流耶？所謂僞者，豈必離經畔道、歸楊附墨者流耶？要之，懷一念之私，不可對人言、不可與天知者，皆二也；投一時之好，炫奇說異、飾貌文奸者，皆僞也。式稽往牒，君子之有益人國、有裨聖道者，若阿衡佐命，若篤棐輔德，若丹書矢戒，若典學沃心，其心術之純、學術之正，固光盎聲施，千古奇絕矣。嗣是而後，有始終爲韓，有感激馳驅，有心事青白，有精忠貫日，心術正矣，不知于學術純焉否也？有下帷發憤，有原道詆佛，有鳴道淶水，有力復古文，學術偉矣，不知其心術正焉否也？可得而尚論歟？夫有純心必有正學，而學術不正，則心術從可窺也。國家明道正心，崇文啓學，二百餘年。凡在菁莪棫樸、涵育聖神之化者，率能以正大光明之心，而爲純粹
translation_en:
…then it is deviant. Must those described as divided in purpose necessarily belong to the sort who flout ritual propriety, betray righteousness, emerge from confinement, and unfold their schemes [?]? Must those described as false necessarily belong to the sort who abandon the classics, turn against the Way, and adhere to Yang Zhu and Mo Di? In essence, anyone who harbors even a single selfish thought that cannot be spoken before others or made known to Heaven is divided in purpose. Anyone who panders to passing tastes, displays startling ideas and expounds strange doctrines, or adorns his outward appearance to cloak wickedness is false.

Consult the records of the past. Among gentlemen who benefited their states and furthered the Way of the sages were those exemplified by the Aheng assisting the reception of Heaven’s mandate, by devoted support in nurturing virtue, by the admonitions set forth in the Vermilion Writing, and by constant attention to learning that nourished the ruler’s mind. The purity of their moral intentions and the correctness of their learning shone abundantly and spread their fame: they were extraordinary exemplars for all ages.

Thereafter, some remained devoted to Han from beginning to end; some exerted themselves tirelessly out of gratitude; some had intentions as clear as the blue sky and white sun; and some possessed perfect loyalty that reached the sun. Their moral intentions were correct, but was their learning pure? Some lowered their study curtains and applied themselves with determination; some traced the origins of the Way and denounced Buddhism; some proclaimed the Way at Laishui; and some vigorously restored ancient-style prose. Their learning was impressive, but were their moral intentions correct? Can we discuss and assess these figures of the past? A pure heart necessarily entails correct learning; where learning is incorrect, one can thereby discern the character of the heart.

For more than two hundred years, our dynasty has elucidated the Way and rectified hearts, honored literary culture and fostered learning. All those nurtured under the sage sovereigns’ transforming influence—in the cultivation of talent celebrated by the Odes’ luxuriant southernwood and flourishing oaks—have generally been able, with upright, magnanimous, and enlightened hearts, to pursue pure…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
精微之學其卓然彪炳於
皇明名臣錄與理學名臣錄者固皆後學師資
也可槩其人歟抑亦有所宗法歟然鏡
往所以昭來察言可以觀行是立心者
又懋學之基也爾多士精白一心學于
古訓素矣盍各紓爾蘊主司者將據今
日之心學而卜他日之功業焉
問士產斯鄉必懷枌榆棘念居其地必切
門庭隱憂姑以山東最急者與諸士商
===
之自井牧廢而屯營興墾資農力租裕
官儲議者謂厚民富國之要圖也許下
河中之蹟尚矣而如置營田務於唐鄧
襄三州置營田使於河北東西路可搽
而行之於今與自阡陌開而水利起灌
溉之疏瀦洩之備議者謂真居裕食之
急務也決口滑河之濬尚矣如修蕭何
之故堰而廢土變爲沃壤築信臣之舊
隄而巨洋復爲腴業可考而準之於今
punctuated:
精微之學。其卓然彪炳於《皇明名臣錄》與《理學名臣錄》者，固皆後學師資也。可槩其人歟？抑亦有所宗法歟？然鏡往所以昭來，察言可以觀行，是立心者又懋學之基也。爾多士精白一心，學于古訓素矣，盍各紓爾蘊？主司者將據今日之心學而卜他日之功業焉。
問：士產斯鄉，必懷枌榆棘念；居其地，必切門庭隱憂。姑以山東最急者與諸士商之。自井牧廢而屯營興，墾資農力，租裕官儲，議者謂厚民富國之要圖也。許下、河中之蹟尚矣，而如置營田務於唐、鄧、襄三州，置營田使於河北東西路，可搽而行之於今與？自阡陌開而水利起，灌溉之疏，瀦洩之備，議者謂真居裕食之急務也。決口滑河之濬尚矣，如修蕭何之故堰而廢土變爲沃壤，築信臣之舊隄而巨洋復爲腴業，可考而準之於今
translation_en:
…learning of purity and subtle refinement. Those whose distinction shines forth in the Records of Eminent Ministers of the August Ming and the Records of Eminent Ministers of the Learning of Principle are indeed all teachers and exemplars for later students. Can you give an account of these men? Are there particular men whom you take as your models? Reflecting on the past illuminates the future, and examining words allows one to discern conduct. Thus, establishing the proper disposition of the mind is also the foundation for diligent learning. You candidates have long devoted yourselves with pure and single-minded purpose to studying the teachings of antiquity. Why not each set forth what you have within you? Those presiding over the examination will use your present cultivation of the mind to judge your future achievements.
Question: Scholars born in this region must cherish an urgent concern for their native place [?]; those living here must feel deeply its troubles as concerns at their very doors. Let us therefore discuss with you scholars the most pressing matters in Shandong. Since the abolition of the well-field and pastoral land system and the rise of agricultural garrisons, reclamation has depended on farmers’ labor, while rents have replenished government stores. Commentators call this an essential means of enriching the people and the state. The precedents at Xuxia and Hezhong go far back. But could such measures as establishing agricultural colony offices in the three prefectures of Tang, Deng, and Xiang, and appointing agricultural colony commissioners for the Eastern and Western Hebei Circuits, be adopted [?] and put into practice today?
Since fields were opened along intersecting boundaries, water management has developed: keeping irrigation channels clear and providing fully for water storage and drainage. Commentators call these urgent tasks for securing people’s dwellings [?] and ensuring abundant food. The dredging associated with Juekou and the Hua River [?] goes far back. As for repairing Xiao He’s ancient weir so that abandoned land became fertile soil, and rebuilding Xinchen’s old embankment so that a vast expanse of water again became productive farmland, could these precedents be examined and taken as models today…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
與夫山東地多鹵薄民輕逃徙汶泗之
河屢決濟漯之源久湮營田水利不可
不講也廼者千里蓁蕪四望蕭艾招撫
徙辦于文移經畫卒滋于浮議司牧者
其秦越之心乎茲欲召募貧民而與闢
曠土穀種芻糧牛犋農器官可給與計
畝分川貸征蠲役法可常與夫以流離
遷徙之民今年耕之明年顧而之他恐
國賦未必益民利未必興又將何術以
===
馭之求其便民宜俗勿弃于豪梁勿漁
于壟斷而可為永遠之猷者果安在邪
魚臺汎漲衛河溢流沿大小之清河亘
青濟而巨浸治農者其隣壑之謀乎茲
欲殺濟兗之上流而避其衝濬清源之
下流而導其勢不知黃衛二河之流可
永無汎濫之虞乎東築小清分漯水一
半而入于海西開柳塘分漯水一半而
歸于河不知大小二清之水可保無淤
punctuated:
與？夫山東地多鹵薄，民輕逃徙，汶泗之河屢決，濟漯之源久湮，營田水利不可不講也。廼者千里蓁蕪，四望蕭艾，招撫徙辦于文移，經畫卒滋于浮議。司牧者，其秦越之心乎？茲欲召募貧民而與闢曠土，穀種芻糧、牛犋農器，官可給與？計畝分川，貸征蠲役，法可常與？夫以流離遷徙之民，今年耕之，明年顧而之他，恐國賦未必益，民利未必興，又將何術以馭之？求其便民宜俗，勿弃于豪梁，勿漁于壟斷，而可為永遠之猷者，果安在邪？
魚臺汎漲，衛河溢流，沿大小之清河，亘青濟而巨浸。治農者，其隣壑之謀乎？茲欲殺濟兗之上流而避其衝，濬清源之下流而導其勢，不知黃衛二河之流，可永無汎濫之虞乎？東築小清，分漯水一半而入于海；西開柳塘，分漯水一半而歸于河。不知大小二清之水，可保無淤
translation_en:
…could they?
Much of Shandong’s land is saline and barren, and its people readily flee and migrate. The Wen and Si rivers repeatedly breach their banks, while the sources of the Ji and Ta have long been silted up. Agricultural settlement and water management therefore demand consideration. Recently, a thousand li have lain overgrown, with wormwood everywhere in sight. Efforts to recruit and settle people have been confined to official correspondence [?], while planning has ultimately produced still more empty discussion. Do those charged with shepherding the people regard their plight with the indifference of Qin toward Yue? If we now wish to recruit poor people and help them open up waste land, can the government provide seed grain, fodder and provisions, teams of oxen, and farm implements? Can arrangements for allotting fields by acreage, deferring tax collection, and remitting labor service be maintained permanently? These displaced and wandering people may cultivate a place this year, only to turn away and go elsewhere the next. We fear that state tax revenues may not increase and the people’s welfare may not improve. By what means, then, can they be governed? Where indeed is a lasting plan that benefits the people, suits local customs, prevents the land from being abandoned to powerful men [?], and keeps monopolists from exploiting it?
Floodwaters rise at Yutai, and the Wei River overflows. Along the Greater and Lesser Qing rivers, vast inundations stretch across Qingzhou and Jinan. Are those administering agriculture planning merely to make their neighbors’ land a drainage basin? We now wish to reduce the upstream flow in Jinan and Yanzhou to avert its impact, and dredge the downstream channel at Qingyuan to guide its force. Yet can the Yellow and Wei rivers thereby be made forever free from the danger of flooding? To the east, embank the Lesser Qing, diverting half the Ta’s water into the sea; to the west, open Liutang, diverting the other half into the river. Yet can the waters of the Greater and Lesser Qing be guaranteed freedom from silting…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
溺之患乎夫以兗東青齊之民方悲赤
地之災復罹洪水之變恐衡決相尋居
食鮮計將何法以治之求其一勞永逸
復水道固民居而可以底平成之績者
將安歸邪夫二者所關于
國家民事非細也諸士子負俊傑之望其所
得于長老先生者久矣願悉爲執事者
告也
===
問豐荒者天行之數拯捄者人事之紀荒
政不可一日不講也君子曰捄荒無奇
策豈上之人坐視而不爲之所耶吾於
周禮見先王子惠庶民之至而捄荒一
事則甚略也大司徒荒政自散利之外
曰薄征曰緩刑曰青禮皆用之以治荒
者而不專爲捄荒計也司民牧者可知
已後之議者或爲濟有無或謂權輕重
或創平糴常平或爲社倉義倉或遏河
南而矯制發粟或守青州而區畫賑貸
punctuated:
溺之患乎？夫以兗東青齊之民，方悲赤地之災，復罹洪水之變，恐衡決相尋，居食鮮計，將何法以治之？求其一勞永逸，復水道，固民居，而可以底平成之績者，將安歸邪？夫二者所關于國家民事非細也。諸士子負俊傑之望，其所得于長老先生者久矣，願悉爲執事者告也。

問：豐荒者，天行之數；拯捄者，人事之紀。荒政不可一日不講也。君子曰：「捄荒無奇策。」豈上之人坐視而不爲之所耶？吾於《周禮》見先王子惠庶民之至，而捄荒一事則甚略也。大司徒荒政，自散利之外，曰薄征，曰緩刑，曰青禮，皆用之以治荒者，而不專爲捄荒計也。司民牧者可知已。後之議者，或爲濟有無，或謂權輕重，或創平糴常平，或爲社倉義倉，或遏河南而矯制發粟，或守青州而區畫賑貸。
translation_en:
…the danger of inundation? The people of Yan, Dong, Qing, and Qi, already grieving over the calamity of parched fields, have again suffered the disaster of flooding. We fear that breaches and overflowing waters will follow one another, leaving them few means of securing shelter and food. By what methods should this be remedied? Where should we turn for measures that, through one effort, secure lasting relief, restore the waterways, safeguard people’s homes, and achieve the accomplishment of bringing the waters and land into order? These two matters have no small bearing on the state and the people’s affairs. You examination candidates bear a reputation for outstanding talent and have long benefited from the teachings of elders and learned masters. We ask you to tell those charged with these affairs all that you know.

Question: Abundance and famine belong to the patterns of Heaven’s operation; rescue and relief belong to the ordering of human affairs. Famine administration must not go undiscussed for even a day. A gentleman has said, “There is no extraordinary strategy for famine relief.” Could those in authority therefore sit watching without making provision for it? In the Rites of Zhou, I see the utmost care of the former kings for the common people as their children, yet its treatment of famine relief is very brief. Among the famine measures of the Minister of Education, apart from distributing resources, are reducing levies, relaxing punishments, and “qing rites” [?]. All are measures used to govern during famine, rather than plans specifically devised to provide famine relief. Those responsible for shepherding the people should understand this.

Later thinkers proposed various measures: balancing supplies between those who had them and those who lacked them; adjusting the relative values of goods; establishing equitable grain purchasing and ever-normal granaries; or setting up community granaries and charitable granaries. Others went to Henan [?] and issued grain on falsely claimed imperial authority, or governed Qingzhou and devised arrangements for relief distributions and loans…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
或觀察宣歙不抑米價或任糶州諭民
平糶其人與政可指而言與往歲東南
水旱頻仍災沴相繼而齊魯尤甚
皇上軫念元元俯從臺臣之請至出
帑儲遣使周行賑卹萬民踴躍鼓舞眞若更
生間者秋穫旣登民賴安堵誠可上紓
宵旰之憂而俯全億萬烝民之命矣然時難必
於常豐政不可以無備議者謂先時為
義倉社倉之建或疑濟有未徧臨期為
===
常平通濟之規民未必其盡周發粟賑
貸權宜之策也果及于老稚之顛連乎
均市平糶調停之法也果行于陬壤之
遐僻乎一民失所咎將誰歸而思患之
防宜有以預桑土之圖矣必何如而可
諸士子夙抱經時之略幸盡言之司
國計者採焉
punctuated: 或觀察宣歙，不抑米價；或任糶州，諭民平糶。其人與政，可指而言與？往歲東南水旱頻仍，災沴相繼，而齊魯尤甚。皇上軫念元元，俯從臺臣之請，至出帑儲，遣使周行賑卹，萬民踴躍鼓舞，眞若更生。間者秋穫旣登，民賴安堵，誠可上紓宵旰之憂，而俯全億萬烝民之命矣。然時難必於常豐，政不可以無備。議者謂先時為義倉社倉之建，或疑濟有未徧；臨期為常平通濟之規，民未必其盡周。發粟賑貸，權宜之策也，果及于老稚之顛連乎？均市平糶，調停之法也，果行于陬壤之遐僻乎？一民失所，咎將誰歸？而思患之防，宜有以預桑土之圖矣。必何如而可？諸士子夙抱經時之略，幸盡言之，司國計者採焉。
translation_en:
… Some, while serving as Surveillance Commissioners in Xuan and She, refrained from suppressing rice prices; others, while holding office in Tiaozhou [?], urged the people to sell grain at moderate prices. Can you identify these men and explain their measures?

In past years, floods and droughts repeatedly afflicted the southeast, with calamities following one another; Qi and Lu suffered especially severely. His Majesty, deeply concerned for the common people, graciously accepted the request of the censorial officials, going so far as to release treasury reserves and dispatch envoys throughout the affected regions to provide relief. The people leapt and danced for joy, truly as though they had been given new life. Recently, the autumn harvest has been gathered, enabling the people to live securely. This can indeed relieve the worries that keep His Majesty occupied from before dawn until late at night, and preserve the lives of his countless subjects. Yet the seasons cannot be counted upon always to yield abundant harvests, and government must not be without preparations.

Those discussing the matter propose establishing charitable and community granaries in advance, though some doubt whether their relief would reach everyone. If arrangements for Ever-Normal Granaries and general relief are made only when the need arises, they may not adequately provide for all the people. Distributing grain and making relief loans are expedients, but do they truly reach the elderly and the young in their distress? Regulating markets and selling grain at moderate prices are methods of adjustment, but are they actually implemented in remote and secluded places? If even one person loses the means of subsistence, upon whom will the blame fall? In guarding against anticipated troubles, we should make preparations beforehand, like securing a nest with mulberry roots before a storm. What, precisely, should be done?

You examination candidates have long cherished plans for governing in response to the needs of the times. Please set them forth fully, so that those responsible for the state's resources may draw upon them.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直樊遲退見
子夏曰鄉也吾見於夫子而問知子曰
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直何謂也子夏
曰富哉言乎
張　鉦
同考試官教諭張　批〔體格嚴整詞氣精潔得聖賢問荅語意〕
考試官教諭余　批〔發明仁知合一之理精當詳明是亦有養可以式矣〕
===

甚矣聖人一言盡仁知之道也子夏因樊遲之
問而嘆之殆獨契其深者乎且夫仁知之道異
用而同歸夫子之言貫通于一理者也想因遲
之未達而告之曰知人愛人子疑其相悖乎觀
於用人可知矣彼人有直者焉吾知之吾舉之
punctuated:
第壹場

translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said, “Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.” Fan Chi withdrew and, seeing Zixia, said, “Earlier I had an audience with the Master and asked about wisdom. The Master said, ‘Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.’ What does this mean?” Zixia said, “How rich these words are!”

Zhang Zheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The structure is rigorous and orderly, and the language and tone refined and clear. It captures the meaning of the questions and answers exchanged by the sage and his worthy disciples.”

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: “It elucidates the principle that benevolence and wisdom are one, precisely and aptly, with thoroughness and clarity. This too shows cultivation and may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Its understanding of principle is clear and incisive, and its phrasing lucid and orderly. An excellent composition. [Unclear wording concerning a scholar and recording or selecting the essay: 之士錄之, ?].”

The sage’s teaching that benevolence and wisdom are one puzzled a worthy disciple, yet a fellow disciple grasped it.

How fully the sage exhausts the Way of benevolence and wisdom in a single utterance! Zixia marveled at it upon hearing Fan Chi’s question: was he perhaps alone in grasping its profundity? Now, the ways of benevolence and wisdom differ in their application but converge upon the same end. The Master’s words unite them through a single principle. We may imagine that, because Chi had not yet understood, he told him: “Knowing others and loving others—do you suspect that these conflict? You can understand by observing the employment of men. Among them are upright men: I recognize them, and I raise them up …”

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
而旌淑之惟明有枉者焉吾知之吾錯之而別
慝之不爽將見用舍當而激勸昭凡遺於所舉
者自易惡以至中若或使之也甄別行而觀感
速凡在于所錯者自改行而率德莫或禦之也
是夫子一言而仁知之理無餘蘊矣何逢之猶
未悟也退而述之于子夏焉蓋徒知舉錯之爲
知而不知化枉之爲仁也子夏則深契其旨者
迺嘆之曰富哉言乎意以道涵于聖心本一理
之渾然而言發乎聖蘊實廣大而悉備舉直知
===
也而不直者化焉則有出於知之外矣其諸旨
遠詞文而包涵盡天下之道者乎錯枉知也而
枉者直焉則非知之所能限矣其諸言近指遠
而易簡得天下之理者乎吁夫子一言而仁知
相須之理以明子夏一言而仁知相悖之疑以
釋遲也可以繹思矣雖然夫子之言雖因樊遲
以發而帝王致治之要寔不外此考之唐虞黜
陟法行而庶績遂熙即三苗至頑且分北焉知
以行仁此非明徵乎故曰知人則哲能官人安
punctuated: 而旌淑之惟明；有枉者焉，吾知之，吾錯之，而別慝之不爽。將見用舍當而激勸昭，凡遺於所舉者，自易惡以至中，若或使之也；甄別行而觀感速，凡在于所錯者，自改行而率德，莫或禦之也。是夫子一言而仁知之理無餘蘊矣，何逢之猶未悟也？退而述之于子夏焉，蓋徒知舉錯之爲知，而不知化枉之爲仁也。子夏則深契其旨者，迺嘆之曰：「富哉言乎！」意以道涵于聖心，本一理之渾然，而言發乎聖蘊，實廣大而悉備。舉直，知也，而不直者化焉，則有出於知之外矣，其諸旨遠詞文而包涵盡天下之道者乎？錯枉，知也，而枉者直焉，則非知之所能限矣，其諸言近指遠而易簡得天下之理者乎？吁！夫子一言而仁知相須之理以明，子夏一言而仁知相悖之疑以釋，遲也可以繹思矣。雖然，夫子之言雖因樊遲以發，而帝王致治之要寔不外此。考之唐虞，黜陟法行而庶績遂熙，即三苗至頑，且分北焉。知以行仁，此非明徵乎？故曰：「知人則哲，能官人，安
translation_en:
…and clearly honor the good. When there are crooked men, I recognize them and set them aside, unerringly distinguishing the wicked. Then appointments and dismissals will be appropriate, and their power to encourage improvement will be manifest. All those left outside the ranks of the promoted will of themselves abandon evil and attain the mean, as though someone were directing them. Discrimination between men will take effect, and the response to their example will be swift. All those set aside will of themselves reform their conduct and follow virtue, with nothing holding them back. Thus, in a single utterance, the Master left none of the principles of benevolence and wisdom unexplained. Why, then, had [Fan Chi?] still not understood? He withdrew and recounted it to Zixia. For he understood only that promoting and setting aside men constituted wisdom; he did not understand that transforming the crooked constituted benevolence. Zixia, however, deeply grasped the purport and therefore exclaimed: “How rich these words are!”

His meaning was that the Way contained within the sage’s mind is fundamentally one undivided principle, while the words issuing from the sage’s inner understanding are truly vast and comprehensive. Promoting the upright is wisdom; yet when those who are not upright are transformed, something extends beyond wisdom itself. Are these not words profound in meaning and refined in expression, encompassing the whole Way of the world? Setting aside the crooked is wisdom; yet when the crooked become upright, this cannot be confined within the bounds of wisdom. Are these not words whose language is accessible but whose import reaches far, apprehending the principles of the world through ease and simplicity?

Ah! With one utterance, the Master clarified the principle that benevolence and wisdom depend upon each other; with one utterance, Zixia dispelled the doubt that benevolence and wisdom conflict. Chi could now ponder this fully. Nevertheless, although the Master’s words were prompted by Fan Chi, the essentials by which emperors and kings achieve good government truly extend no further than this. Consider the ages of Tang and Yu: when the rules for demotion and promotion were put into practice, all undertakings flourished. Even the Sanmiao, stubborn in the extreme, were separated and driven away. Is this not clear evidence of wisdom being used to carry out benevolence? Hence it is said: “To know men is to be wise, enabling one to appoint men to office; to bring peace …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
民則惠黎民懷之要之知人者又安民之本也
然則夫子之言豈獨為樊遲告哉
敦厚以崇禮
朱鴻謨
同考試官教諭馮　批〔敦崇二字作者類多膚滯獨此發〕
明精微錄之
考試官教諭佘　批〔造理淵邃搆思俊逸殆深於性學者〕
考試官教授李　批〔純正典雅結尤有見〕
===
君子凝道之功篤其已能者而充之也夫德性
本厚而禮所以節文之者也敦之崇之而德脩
矣道其有不凝乎中庸明人道之意謂夫道一
而已矣自充足于德性也謂之厚而所以培秩
敘之基者此也自散見于儀文也謂之禮而所
以裕德性之用者此也厚之不敦則禮不虛行
而禮有不崇厚者漓矣非脩德凝道之全功也
惟君子操存篤於匪懈而時保其真純之懿持
養懋於勿忘而益培乎渾朴之體厚之原於天
者粹然其完固焉而成性之存存殆與峻極之
punctuated:
民則惠，黎民懷之。要之，知人者又安民之本也。然則夫子之言，豈獨為樊遲告哉？

敦厚以崇禮
朱鴻謨
同考試官教諭馮批〔敦崇二字，作者類多膚滯，獨此發〕明精微，錄之。
考試官教諭佘批〔造理淵邃，搆思俊逸，殆深於性學者。〕
考試官教授李批〔純正典雅，結尤有見。〕

君子凝道之功，篤其已能者而充之也。夫德性本厚，而禮所以節文之者也。敦之崇之，而德脩矣，道其有不凝乎？《中庸》明人道之意，謂夫道一而已矣。自充足于德性也，謂之厚，而所以培秩敘之基者此也；自散見于儀文也，謂之禮，而所以裕德性之用者此也。厚之不敦，則禮不虛行；而禮有不崇，厚者漓矣。非脩德凝道之全功也。惟君子操存篤於匪懈，而時保其真純之懿；持養懋於勿忘，而益培乎渾朴之體。厚之原於天者，粹然其完固焉，而成性之存存，殆與峻極之
translation_en:
…bringing peace to the people constitutes benevolence, and the common people cherish him. In sum, knowing people is also the foundation of bringing peace to the people. Were the Master's words, then, addressed to Fan Chi alone?

“Deepen Substantiality in Order to Honor Ritual Propriety”
By Zhu Hongmo

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: “In treating the two words ‘deepen’ and ‘honor,’ most writers are superficial and constrained. This essay alone elucidates their subtle meaning. Include it.”
Examiner She, Instructor, comments: “Its exploration of principle is profound, and its conception outstanding and free-flowing. The author seems deeply versed in the learning of human nature.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “Pure and correct, refined and elegant; the conclusion is especially insightful.”

The gentleman's work of giving firm embodiment to the Way consists in strengthening what he is already capable of and extending it to the full. Moral nature is inherently substantial, while ritual propriety regulates and gives patterned expression to it. By deepening the former and honoring the latter, virtue is cultivated. How could the Way then fail to become firmly embodied? In explaining the meaning of the human Way, the Doctrine of the Mean holds that the Way is simply one. Insofar as it is fully present within moral nature, it is called substantiality: this is what nurtures the foundation of ordered relationships. Insofar as it appears variously in ceremonial forms, it is called ritual propriety: this is what enriches the functioning of moral nature. If substantiality is not deepened, ritual cannot operate on an empty foundation; and if ritual is not honored, substantiality becomes diluted. This falls short of the complete work of cultivating virtue and giving firm embodiment to the Way.

Only the gentleman is steadfast and unremitting in grasping and preserving it, constantly safeguarding the excellence of its genuine purity. He diligently sustains and nourishes it without forgetting, further nurturing its integral simplicity. The substantiality that originates in Heaven thus remains pure, intact, and secure; and the ceaseless preservation of his fully realized nature comes close to joining with the loftiness of …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
而相爲渾淪矣厚之統於物者純然其保合焉
而真機之亹亹殆與發育之妙相爲化醇矣然
又擴其固有之能而持循於中正之典充其積
中之厚而率履於品式之常經焉三百欽翼以
奉之而凡盡制盡倫以綱維乎人道者合之盡
其大也典禮之會通而良能有不益固也哉曲
焉三千秪肅以承之而凡中規中矩以經緯乎
人文者析之極其精也致禮以治躬而德性有
不益堅也哉夫心存於敦厚而學禮有以豫其
===
基知致於崇禮而德性有以踐其實斯道之所
以凝也歟抑聞諸夫子曰克己復禮爲仁夫已
克乃所以復禮而非禮不動卽所以涵養德性
也中庸顧以内外言者何與噫此交養互發之
功也蓋厚者禮之原而禮者厚之著無二理也
故曰忠信之人可以學禮又曰動容周旋中禮
者盛德之至也學者合而觀之始得
以不忍人之心行不忍人之政治天下可
運之掌上
punctuated:
而相爲渾淪矣。厚之統於物者，純然其保合焉，而真機之亹亹，殆與發育之妙相爲化醇矣。然又擴其固有之能，而持循於中正之典；充其積中之厚，而率履於品式之常。經焉三百，欽翼以奉之，而凡盡制盡倫以綱維乎人道者，合之盡其大也。典禮之會通，而良能有不益固也哉？曲焉三千，秪肅以承之，而凡中規中矩以經緯乎人文者，析之極其精也。致禮以治躬，而德性有不益堅也哉？夫心存於敦厚，而學禮有以豫其基；知致於崇禮，而德性有以踐其實，斯道之所以凝也歟？抑聞諸夫子曰：「克己復禮爲仁。」夫已克，乃所以復禮，而非禮不動，卽所以涵養德性也。《中庸》顧以内外言者，何與？噫！此交養互發之功也。蓋厚者禮之原，而禮者厚之著，無二理也。故曰：「忠信之人，可以學禮。」又曰：「動容周旋中禮者，盛德之至也。」學者合而觀之，始得。

以不忍人之心，行不忍人之政，治天下可運之掌上。
translation_en:
…and together form an undivided whole [?]. As for the substantial goodness that unites all things, its integrity is preserved in purity; the ceaseless activity of its genuine impulse becomes thoroughly fused with the wondrous workings of generation and nurture. Yet one must also extend one’s inherent capacities and abide by standards of centrality and correctness, bringing to fullness the substantial goodness accumulated within and following the enduring norms of prescribed forms. The three hundred principal rules of ritual are to be upheld with reverence and care. All that fulfills institutions and human relationships, thereby maintaining the framework of the human Way, is brought together to encompass its full scope. When canonical rites are comprehensively understood, how could innate moral capacity fail to become more firmly established? The three thousand detailed rules are to be received with reverence and solemnity. All that accords with the compass and square, thereby ordering human culture, is distinguished and examined to the utmost refinement. When ritual is fully realized in governing oneself, how could moral nature fail to become more steadfast?

When the mind rests in substantial goodness, studying ritual provides for its foundation in advance; when knowledge is brought to fulfillment in honoring ritual, moral nature has the means to realize its substance in practice. Is this not how the Way becomes firmly established? Moreover, we have heard the Master say: “To overcome oneself and return to ritual is benevolence.” Overcoming oneself is precisely the means of returning to ritual, while making no movement contrary to ritual is precisely the means of nurturing moral nature. Why, then, does the Doctrine of the Mean speak in terms of the inner and the outer? Ah! This is the work of mutual nourishment and reciprocal development. Substantial goodness is the source of ritual, and ritual is the manifestation of substantial goodness: they do not constitute two separate principles. Thus it is said: “A person of loyalty and trustworthiness can learn ritual.” It is also said: “For one’s bearing and every movement to accord with ritual is the culmination of abundant virtue.” Only by considering these together can learners attain understanding.

With a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others, practice government that cannot bear their suffering: governing all under Heaven can then be as easy as turning something in the palm of one’s hand.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:

聖王有因心之政而措之天下無難矣夫心者
萬化之原也聖王因心以達政而於治天下也
===
何有哉孟子之意若曰人之有是不忍人之心
也存之爲天地立心發之爲生民立命者也不
能推之者固無望于治矣惟先王有不忍人之
心斯有不忍人之政焉則惻怛所溢有政以達
之而先天下以周其慮經綸所布由心以推之
而合天下以廣其仁有是心也非徒善也行是
政也非徒法也以是而治天下有不裕如也哉
吾知美意資良法以相成而達順之機莫禦純
政寄純心以時出而丕冒之化自弘紀綱法度
punctuated:
王象乾

聖王有因心之政，而措之天下無難矣。夫心者，萬化之原也。聖王因心以達政，而於治天下也何有哉？孟子之意若曰：人之有是不忍人之心也，存之爲天地立心，發之爲生民立命者也。不能推之者，固無望于治矣。惟先王有不忍人之心，斯有不忍人之政焉。則惻怛所溢，有政以達之，而先天下以周其慮；經綸所布，由心以推之，而合天下以廣其仁。有是心也，非徒善也；行是政也，非徒法也。以是而治天下，有不裕如也哉？吾知美意資良法以相成，而達順之機莫禦；純政寄純心以時出，而丕冒之化自弘。紀綱法度，

Wang Xiangqian 王象乾

Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor, comments: 〔The first two clauses of this topic carry forward the preceding passage and set aside what follows; their rhetorical emphasis does not call for extended exposition. Moreover, treatments generally base their argument on educating and nourishing the people, which seems especially stale and rigid. This composition alone is lucid and distinguished, and should be recorded as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Shao, School Instructor, comments: 〔The language and tone are composed and fluent, and the implications of its principles are deep and abundant. It also entirely clears away convoluted expression [?], making the topic’s meaning shine forth. An excellent composition.〕
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear, fluent, and elegant.〕
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔The language conveys its meaning fully, and the ideas are harmoniously integrated.〕

The sage kings possessed a government that followed their hearts, and putting it into practice throughout All-under-Heaven presented no difficulty. The heart is the source of all transformation. When the sage kings followed their hearts to give expression to government, what difficulty could there be in governing All-under-Heaven? Mencius’s meaning might be expressed thus: The heart that cannot bear the suffering of others, which human beings possess, when preserved establishes the heart of Heaven and Earth; when expressed, it establishes the destiny of the people. Those unable to extend it certainly have no hope of achieving good government. Because the former kings possessed hearts that could not bear the suffering of others, they consequently possessed governments that could not bear the suffering of others. Thus, the outpouring of their compassion found expression in government, and they took thought ahead of everyone under Heaven, making their concern comprehensive. The ordering of affairs that they put into practice proceeded by extension from their hearts, and they embraced everyone under Heaven to broaden their benevolence. Possessing this heart was not merely a matter of good intentions; implementing this government was not merely a matter of laws. Could governing All-under-Heaven by these means be anything but effortless? I know that fine intentions draw upon good laws, each bringing the other to fulfillment, so that nothing can obstruct the workings of pervasive harmony. Pure government rests upon a pure heart and emerges as circumstances require, so that its all-encompassing transforming influence naturally expands. The guiding principles, laws, and institutions…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
治之經也舉斯心以加彼而愷悌之周流推之
何所不準禮樂刑政治之章也出乎身以加民
而予惠之洋溢動之何所不化雖天下至大也
然以其先得乎斯民者而運量焉民胞物與之
懷殆舉斯世而甄陶之者乎雖治天下至難也
然以其同然乎斯民者而廣運焉乾父坤母之
量殆合四海而涵育之者乎謂之曰治天下可
運之掌上信乎掌之運也近取諸身而自足治
之運也反求諸心而有餘噫吾觀先王而知治
===
天下之易易也雖然不忍之心所謂赤子之心
也惟聖人不失其心故能達之於政而天下治
焉如天好生由此其選也苟不得之心而徒泥
之政則新之井田秦之周官于治奚補哉噫此
必有關雎麟趾之意而後周官之法度可行也
易
六爻發揮旁通情也時乘六龍以御天也
朱鴻謨
同考試官教諭馮　批〔此題於旁通御天處易涉浮泛獨此作〕
punctuated:
治之經也。舉斯心以加彼，而愷悌之周流，推之何所不準？禮樂刑政，治之章也。出乎身以加民，而予惠之洋溢，動之何所不化？雖天下至大也，然以其先得乎斯民者而運量焉，民胞物與之懷，殆舉斯世而甄陶之者乎！雖治天下至難也，然以其同然乎斯民者而廣運焉，乾父坤母之量，殆合四海而涵育之者乎！謂之曰「治天下可運之掌上」，信乎！掌之運也，近取諸身而自足；治之運也，反求諸心而有餘。噫！吾觀先王而知治天下之易易也。雖然，不忍之心，所謂赤子之心也。惟聖人不失其心，故能達之於政，而天下治焉。如天好生，由此其選也。苟不得之心，而徒泥之政，則新之井田、秦之周官，于治奚補哉？噫！此必有《關雎》《麟趾》之意，而後《周官》之法度可行也。
易
六爻發揮，旁通情也；時乘六龍，以御天也。
朱鴻謨
同考試官教諭馮，批〔此題於旁通御天處易涉浮泛，獨此作〕
translation_en:
…are the enduring framework of governance. Extend this heart to others, and kindly affection will circulate everywhere: where would its application fail to accord with what is right? Rites, music, punishments, and administration are the outward forms of governance. Proceeding from oneself and extending to the people, beneficence overflows: whom would its influence fail to transform? Though all under Heaven is vast indeed, one manages it through what one has grasped before the people have. Does not the spirit that regards the people as siblings and other creatures as companions embrace and mold this entire world? Though governing all under Heaven is difficult indeed, one extends one's activity through what one shares with the people. Does not the capaciousness that regards Heaven as father and Earth as mother embrace and nurture all within the Four Seas? How true the saying, “Governing all under Heaven can be like turning something in one's palm”! For movement in the palm, what lies close at hand in one's own body is sufficient; for the workings of government, searching within one's own heart yields more than enough. Ah! In contemplating the former kings, I understand how very easy governing all under Heaven can be. Nevertheless, the heart that cannot bear others' suffering is what is called the heart of a newborn child. Only the sage never loses this heart; thus he can express it in government, and all under Heaven is well governed. To cherish life as Heaven does: herein lies the basis of that choice [?]. If one does not grasp this in the heart but merely clings to governmental arrangements, what benefit to governance could come from the Xin dynasty's well-field system or Qin's Offices of Zhou [?]? Ah! Only when there is the spirit of “The Ospreys Cry” (Guanju) and “The Qilin's Hoofs” (Linzhi) can the institutions of the Offices of Zhou be put into practice.

Book of Changes

“The six lines unfold their meaning, comprehensively communicating the circumstances; at the appropriate times, he mounts the six dragons to ride through Heaven.”

Zhu Hongmo

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “On this topic, discussion of ‘comprehensively communicating’ and ‘riding through Heaven’ readily becomes vague and superficial. This composition alone…”

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
明切瑩澈殆深於易者取冠多士允宜
考試官教諭余　批〔詞氣春雅發揮御天處尤見筆力〕
考試官教授李　批〔不事浮詞而意獨到有養士也〕
易畫備闡乎天德而聖人體之于治焉甚矣天
德之妙也易畫闡其藴而聖人體之于治也夫
豈有二乎哉文言復申彖傳之意至此若曰乾
之爲道固極其大矣然非易則無以該其藴而
非聖則無以體其全是故四德貫乎流行而至
精入于無朕情之溢于天載者若是乎其難盡
===
矣惟六爻之已畫也純陽至健之體旣以昭布
于法象之陳而貞悔乘承之形有以通極乎神
明之德總觀乎一卦而一元之統體者合之曲
盡乎其大也徧觀乎六爻而一元之分布者析
之曲盡乎其詳也蓋不必觀象于天而四德之
精盡于易則致治之本裕于易矣聖人有見于
六龍之變皆天也皆天則皆時也由是奉帝則
以周旋而見之敷布者允協夫化裁之用述天
理以時措而運之經緯者不失其張弛之宜將
punctuated:
明切瑩澈，殆深於易者，取冠多士允宜。
考試官教諭余，批〔詞氣春雅，發揮御天處尤見筆力。〕
考試官教授李，批〔不事浮詞而意獨到，有養士也。〕
易畫備闡乎天德，而聖人體之于治焉。甚矣，天德之妙也！易畫闡其藴，而聖人體之于治也，夫豈有二乎哉？文言復申彖傳之意，至此若曰：乾之爲道，固極其大矣，然非易則無以該其藴，而非聖則無以體其全。是故四德貫乎流行，而至精入于無朕，情之溢于天載者，若是乎其難盡矣。惟六爻之已畫也，純陽至健之體，旣以昭布于法象之陳，而貞悔乘承之形，有以通極乎神明之德。總觀乎一卦，而一元之統體者，合之曲盡乎其大也；徧觀乎六爻，而一元之分布者，析之曲盡乎其詳也。蓋不必觀象于天，而四德之精盡于易，則致治之本裕于易矣。聖人有見于六龍之變，皆天也；皆天，則皆時也。由是奉帝則以周旋，而見之敷布者，允協夫化裁之用；述天理以時措，而運之經緯者，不失其張弛之宜。將
translation_en:
…clear, incisive, luminous, and penetrating. The writer must have a profound understanding of the Book of Changes; it is entirely fitting to rank him first among the candidates.

Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: “The diction and spirit are refined [?]; the exposition of ‘riding upon Heaven’ particularly displays the strength of his writing.”

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “He avoids empty phrases and achieves distinctive insights: he is a scholar of cultivated character.”

The lines of the Book of Changes fully elucidate Heaven’s virtue, and the sage embodies it in government. How profound is the subtlety of Heaven’s virtue! The lines of the Changes elucidate what it contains, while the sage embodies it in government: how could these be two different things? Here the Commentary on the Words of the Text further develops the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments, as though saying: The Way of Qian is indeed supremely great. Yet without the Changes there would be no means to encompass its inner riches, and without the sage there would be no means to embody its entirety. Thus the four virtues pervade its ceaseless operation, while its utmost essence enters the realm without perceptible traces. How difficult it is to exhaust the true workings that overflow in Heaven’s activity!

Once the six lines have been drawn, the substance of pure yang and supreme strength is clearly displayed in the array of patterns and images. The configurations of the inner and outer trigrams, and of lines riding upon or supporting one another, provide the means to penetrate fully the virtue of spiritual intelligence. Viewed comprehensively as a single hexagram, the unified substance of the primal origin is brought together, exhaustively expressing its greatness in every aspect. Viewed throughout its six lines, the differentiated manifestations of that primal origin are analyzed, exhaustively expressing their particulars in every aspect. There is thus no need to observe the images in Heaven: the essence of the four virtues is fully contained in the Changes, and the foundation for achieving good government is abundantly provided there.

The sage perceives that the transformations of the six dragons are all Heaven’s workings. Since all are Heaven’s workings, all accord with their proper times. Accordingly, he conducts himself in obedience to the Supreme Lord’s standards, and what he manifests in his enactments truly accords with the function of transforming and regulating. He follows Heaven’s principles and applies them at the proper times, and in ordering affairs he never departs from the appropriate balance of tightening and relaxing. He is about to…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
有爲焉而本無爲以妙其施凡所以順乎其治
者卽所以藴乎其畫者也而於穆之微自此兼
體于一身矣時乎動焉而本無動以神其化凡
所以經乎其政者卽所以顯乎其卦者也而化
育之精至此盡見于推行矣是其始也天道通
于易畫是易一天也其旣也天道體于聖人聖
亦一天也由之雲雨沛而天下平元亨配天之
功其至矣噫乾之大也不其深乎雖然易聖人
所作也而御天之功猶必本諸易焉何哉蓋易
===
書者理之寓而聖心者理之藏也聖心之理寄
於易故體天之治自不能外易而有行耳若其
神明默成以心會易于意言象數之表而六爻
之塵跡不與焉噫此固聖人作易之本心所以
屬望天下後世者豈其微哉善學者當自得之
聖人有以見天下之賾而擬諸其形容象
其物宜是故謂之象
劉一相
同考試官敎諭馮　批〔伏羲精意獨顯于易學者類難言之惟〕
punctuated:
有爲焉，而本無爲以妙其施，凡所以順乎其治者，卽所以藴乎其畫者也，而於穆之微自此兼體于一身矣。時乎動焉，而本無動以神其化，凡所以經乎其政者，卽所以顯乎其卦者也，而化育之精至此盡見于推行矣。是其始也，天道通于易畫，是易一天也；其旣也，天道體于聖人，聖亦一天也。由之雲雨沛而天下平，元亨配天之功其至矣。噫！乾之大也，不其深乎？雖然，易聖人所作也，而御天之功猶必本諸易焉，何哉？蓋易書者，理之寓，而聖心者，理之藏也。聖心之理寄於易，故體天之治自不能外易而有行耳。若其神明默成，以心會易于意言象數之表，而六爻之塵跡不與焉。噫！此固聖人作易之本心，所以屬望天下後世者，豈其微哉？善學者當自得之。
聖人有以見天下之賾，而擬諸其形容，象其物宜，是故謂之象。
劉一相
同考試官敎諭馮　批〔伏羲精意獨顯于易，學者類難言之，惟〕
translation_en:
…act, yet take nonaction as the basis for making their application wondrous. All that brings their governance into accord with Heaven is precisely what is contained in the lines of the diagrams; thus the subtle workings of Heaven’s profound stillness are embodied together in a single person. They move when the time calls for movement, yet take nonmovement as the basis for making their transformations numinous. All that orders their administration is precisely what is manifested in the hexagrams; thus the essential workings of transformation and nurture are fully revealed in their practical implementation. At the outset, the Way of Heaven permeates the diagrams of the Changes: the Changes is itself a Heaven. Subsequently, the Way of Heaven is embodied in the sage: the sage, too, is a Heaven. Through this, clouds gather, rain falls abundantly, and all under Heaven is at peace. The achievement of matching Heaven in primal greatness and unimpeded success reaches its utmost extent. Ah! Is not the greatness of Qian profound?
Nevertheless, the Changes was made by the sages. Why, then, must their achievement in governing in accord with Heaven still be rooted in the Changes? The book of Changes is the lodging place of principle, while the sage’s mind is its repository. The principle within the sage’s mind is lodged in the Changes; thus governance that embodies Heaven naturally cannot operate outside the Changes. As for their numinous understanding and silent accomplishment, they comprehend the Changes with their minds beyond ideas, words, images, and numbers, without involvement in the merely outward traces of the six lines. Ah! This was indeed the original intention of the sages in making the Changes, and the hope they placed in all under Heaven and in later generations. Could its significance be slight? Those who learn well should apprehend it for themselves.
“The sages had the means to perceive the profound complexities of all under Heaven. They represented these through their forms and appearances, imaging what was appropriate to each thing; hence these were called ‘images.’”
Liu Yixiang 劉一相
Comment by Associate Examiner Feng 馮, Instructor: 〔Fuxi’s essential intent is uniquely revealed in the Changes, yet scholars generally find it difficult to articulate. Only…〕

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之此作發明詳盡可以式矣
考試官教諭余　批〔講謂之象處精透迥出衆作〕〔須得聖心者〕
考試官教授李　批〔詞氣昌徤〕
知象之所由立則知象之所由名矣盖象以像
乎理也聖人見天下之賾而象始立焉易豈強
作者哉且先天聖人嘗立象以盡意矣象果何
所自哉蓋物類盈于兩間其紛然不一者何至
賾也而莫非陰陽之變也聖人則自其神明于
心者而仰觀俯察旁通其散殊之迹由其默成
===
于内者而遠求近取踈觀其不一之情所以啓
易畫之原預于此矣於是隨其至賾之所著者
以擬其形容之似陰也陽也與夫陰陽之雜也
無不比擬於心目之間由是即其擬議之所及
者以象其物理之宜陽以奇象也陰以偶象也
與夫陰陽之雜也而以奇偶之雜者象之也有
以曲盡其摸寫之真若此者不謂之象乎吾知
未畫之先象非本無也形容寓于紛紜之内而
萬象森然之已具既畫之後象非始有也物宜
punctuated:
之此作發明詳盡，可以式矣。

考試官教諭余，批〔講謂之象處精透，迥出衆作〕〔須得聖心者〕。

考試官教授李，批〔詞氣昌徤〕。

知象之所由立，則知象之所由名矣。盖象以像乎理也。聖人見天下之賾，而象始立焉，易豈強作者哉？且先天聖人嘗立象以盡意矣，象果何所自哉？蓋物類盈于兩間，其紛然不一者何至賾也！而莫非陰陽之變也。聖人則自其神明于心者，而仰觀俯察，旁通其散殊之迹；由其默成于内者，而遠求近取，踈觀其不一之情，所以啓易畫之原，預于此矣。於是隨其至賾之所著者，以擬其形容之似，陰也，陽也，與夫陰陽之雜也，無不比擬於心目之間。由是即其擬議之所及者，以象其物理之宜。陽以奇象也，陰以偶象也，與夫陰陽之雜也，而以奇偶之雜者象之也。有以曲盡其摸寫之真，若此者不謂之象乎？吾知未畫之先，象非本無也，形容寓于紛紜之内，而萬象森然之已具；既畫之後，象非始有也，物宜
translation_en:
…This composition elucidates it thoroughly and may serve as a model. [The opening 之 is unclear in context.]

Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of “therefore they are called images” is penetrating and precise, far surpassing the other compositions.〕〔This requires someone who has grasped the sage’s mind.〕

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔The language and its spirit are flourishing and vigorous.〕

If one understands how the images came to be established, one understands how they came to be named. For images represent principles. The sage perceived the intricate mysteries of all under Heaven, and only then were the images established. Could the Changes have been an arbitrary creation? Moreover, the sage of Former Heaven once established images to express his meaning fully. Where, then, did these images originate? The myriad kinds of things fill the space between Heaven and Earth: how profoundly intricate is their bewildering diversity! Yet none is other than a transformation of yin and yang. Drawing upon the spiritual illumination within his mind, the sage looked upward and examined downward, comprehensively apprehending their varied manifestations. Drawing upon what silently came to fruition within, he sought afar and took examples close at hand, surveying their diverse conditions [?]. The source from which the lines of the Changes would emerge was already prepared in this.

Accordingly, following the manifestations of these profound intricacies, he fashioned likenesses of their forms and appearances. Yin, yang, and the intermingling of yin and yang—all were compared and represented within his mind’s eye. Then, drawing upon what his comparisons and deliberations encompassed, he represented what was appropriate to the principles of things. Yang was represented by an odd number, yin by an even number; the intermingling of yin and yang was represented by combinations of odd and even numbers. Thus he could render their true character with exhaustive fidelity in every detail. Should representations such as these not be called images?

I know that, before the lines were drawn, the images were not originally absent. Forms and appearances inhered within the bewildering multiplicity of things, and the myriad images were already fully arrayed. After the lines were drawn, the images did not only then begin to exist. What was appropriate to things…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
著于探索之精而法象昭然其畢陳其稱名于
卦者其取類于賾者也理本無形借此以爲形
心欲言之而未盡者至此示之而有餘矣其模
寫于畫者其醜類于物者也道本無象假此以
爲象意欲陳之而未悉者自此彰之而莫掩矣
不謂之象而何哉吁知象之所由立則知聖人
之意所由盡而尚象之學不容已矣夫人其可
無擬議之功耶抑易象自伏羲而始畫已非得
已之情至文周益以言而擬議言動又望人以
尚詞之學每惓惓焉無乃愈失其初乎時使然
爾要之假象以明理者聖人之善教因象而識
心者君子之善學苟徒象是泥而曰易在是焉
豈聖人之心哉而况於言乎噫見乎此者謂之
見易
===
書
伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
張　鉦
同考試官教諭張　批〔此題作者率塵俗可厭獨此清暢典則模〕
punctuated:
著于探索之精，而法象昭然其畢陳。其稱名于卦者，其取類于賾者也。理本無形，借此以爲形；心欲言之而未盡者，至此示之而有餘矣。其模寫于畫者，其醜類于物者也。道本無象，假此以爲象；意欲陳之而未悉者，自此彰之而莫掩矣。不謂之象而何哉？吁！知象之所由立，則知聖人之意所由盡，而尚象之學不容已矣。夫人其可無擬議之功耶？抑易象自伏羲而始畫，已非得已之情；至文周益以言，而擬議言動，又望人以尚詞之學，每惓惓焉，無乃愈失其初乎？時使然爾。要之，假象以明理者，聖人之善教；因象而識心者，君子之善學。苟徒象是泥，而曰易在是焉，豈聖人之心哉？而况於言乎？噫！見乎此者，謂之見易。

書
伯拜稽首，讓于夔龍。帝曰：「俞，往欽哉！」
張　鉦
同考試官教諭張　批〔此題作者率塵俗可厭，獨此清暢典則，模〕
translation_en:
…become manifest through the refinement of inquiry, and the exemplary images are all clearly displayed. The names assigned to the hexagrams draw their analogies from the intricacies of things. Principle itself has no form; these lend it form. What the mind wishes to express in words but cannot fully convey is here shown with more than sufficient fullness. What is depicted in the lines corresponds to the kinds of things. The Way itself has no image; these lend it an image. What one wishes to set forth but cannot fully explain is thereby made manifest and cannot remain concealed. What could these be called, if not images?

Ah! To understand how the images were established is to understand how the sages’ meaning was fully expressed; thus the study that esteems images cannot be neglected. Can anyone dispense with the work of comparison and deliberation? Yet when Fuxi first drew the images of the Changes, even this arose from a necessity he could not avoid. When King Wen and the Duke of Zhou added words, so that people might compare and deliberate upon their speech and actions, they also earnestly and repeatedly urged people toward a study that esteems the verbal statements. Did this not depart still further from the original intent? The times made it so. Ultimately, borrowing images to illuminate principle is the sages’ excellence in teaching; following images to understand the mind is the gentleman’s excellence in learning. If one merely clings to the images and says that the Changes resides in them, how could this accord with the sages’ intent? How much more does this apply to words! Ah! To perceive this is what it means to perceive the Changes.

Book of Documents

“Bo bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Kui and Long. The emperor said: ‘Yes. Go and be reverent!’”

Zhang Zheng

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
寫虞廷氣象宛然宜錄以式多士
考試官教諭余　批〔氣勢閎暢格局清整〕
考試官教授李　批〔立意簡切造語精練〕
大臣敬遜典禮之任聖君勑之以敬職焉蓋敬
以典禮伯夷固其選也乃不自任焉此帝舜勑
勉之歟且國之大事在祀而交神之本主敬虞
廷重秩宗之官既選于衆而咨伯矣乃伯則不
敢當也承君命之嚴重而謙退未遑特拜手以
致敬仰天威之咫尺而恭敬不寧載稽首以盡
禮讓于夔焉眞見夫夔之賢愈于已首舉以自
代也讓于龍焉又見夫已之賢不如龍並舉以
俟擇也此固伯夷敬愼之心而帝則申其成命
曰俞往欽哉意以夔龍之賢讓以典禮汝言是
哉固非一人之私顧秩宗之任詢謀僉同汝尚
往哉欽承三禮之命以祀上下朕將對越天地
惟汝是典焉則匪懈于夙夜以端昭格之原者
汝其愼乃攸司可也而何以讓爲耶以承宗廟
朕欲克享鬼神惟汝是主焉則勉力于寅直以

寫虞廷氣象宛然，宜錄以式多士。

大臣敬遜典禮之任，聖君勑之以敬職焉。蓋敬以典禮，伯夷固其選也，乃不自任焉，此帝舜勑勉之歟？且國之大事在祀，而交神之本主敬。虞廷重秩宗之官，既選于衆而咨伯矣，乃伯則不敢當也。承君命之嚴重，而謙退未遑，特拜手以致敬；仰天威之咫尺，而恭敬不寧，載稽首以盡禮。讓于夔焉，眞見夫夔之賢愈于已，首舉以自代也；讓于龍焉，又見夫已之賢不如龍，並舉以俟擇也。此固伯夷敬愼之心，而帝則申其成命曰：「俞，往欽哉！」意以夔龍之賢，讓以典禮，汝言是哉！固非一人之私。顧秩宗之任，詢謀僉同，汝尚往哉！欽承三禮之命，以祀上下，朕將對越天地，惟汝是典焉。則匪懈于夙夜，以端昭格之原者，汝其愼乃攸司可也，而何以讓爲耶？以承宗廟，朕欲克享鬼神，惟汝是主焉。則勉力于寅直，以
translation_en:
…vividly depicts the atmosphere of the court of Yu. It deserves inclusion as a model for the many candidates.
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔Its force is expansive and fluent; its structure lucid and orderly.〕
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔Its conception is concise and pertinent; its phrasing precise and polished.〕
A great minister reverently declined responsibility for directing the rites, and the sage ruler admonished him to discharge that office with reverence. For directing the rites reverently, Bo Yi was indeed the fitting choice; yet he would not take the responsibility upon himself. Was this why Emperor Shun admonished and encouraged him?
Now the great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice, and reverence is the foundation of communion with the spirits. The court of Yu attached great importance to the office of Minister of Ancestral Rites. Having selected Bo Yi from among the assembled ministers, the emperor addressed him; yet Bo Yi dared not accept. Receiving his sovereign’s weighty command, he scarcely had time to express his humility and withdrawal, but bowed with his hands joined to convey his reverence. Looking up at the imperial majesty so close at hand, he was uneasy in his respectful awe and further bowed his head to the ground to fulfill the rites. He yielded to Kui because he truly considered Kui’s worth superior to his own, naming him first as his replacement. He yielded to Long because he likewise considered his own worth inferior to Long’s, naming him as well for consideration.
This was indeed Bo Yi’s reverent and cautious disposition. The emperor, however, reaffirmed the command he had already issued, saying: “Yes. Go, and be reverent!” His meaning was: “In view of Kui’s and Long’s worthiness, you would yield to them the direction of the rites. Your words are right! They certainly do not arise from personal self-interest. Yet consultation concerning the office of Minister of Ancestral Rites has produced unanimous agreement. Go, then! Reverently receive the command concerning the three categories of rites, to offer sacrifice to those above and below. I shall reverently serve Heaven and Earth, and you alone shall direct these rites. Thus, in remaining diligent morning and night, to set right the source through which the spirits are manifestly brought into our presence, you need only attend carefully to your charge. Why should you decline? In serving the ancestral temples, I wish to offer sacrifices acceptable to the spirits, and you alone shall preside over them. Therefore, exert yourself in reverence and uprightness, so as to…”

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
立感通之本者汝其敬爾有官可也而可徒退
讓耶吁于伯夷見推賢之誠于帝舜見任賢之
專有虞君臣之氣象藹然可想矣抑明德恤祀
非有二也舜命秩宗曰寅曰欽不一而足豈不
以敬者無體之禮舍敬則禮文皆虛耳故曰禮
云禮云玉帛云乎哉舜之主祭而百神享蓋不
在類禋望徧之儀文也後世封祀郊雍殆不知
敬爲何物旨哉明德惟馨之訓此虞周之所以
爲至治也
===
政貴有恒辭尚體要
張中鴻
同考試官教諭張　批〔講有恒體要處一洗繁庸之詞獨發實字〕
尚字意見超脫亦文之有體者可錄
考試官教諭余　批〔意精詞雅格整氣暢〕
考試官教授李　批〔莊腴典則逈邁諸作〕
賢王示大臣政令之體可謂知所重矣夫久于
其道而令不煩焉政令之體敦矣欲化殷者舍
是奚以哉康王命畢公保釐東郊至此意謂君
punctuated:
立感通之本者，汝其敬爾有官可也，而可徒退讓耶？」吁！于伯夷見推賢之誠，于帝舜見任賢之專，有虞君臣之氣象藹然可想矣。抑明德恤祀，非有二也。舜命秩宗，曰寅，曰欽，不一而足，豈不以敬者無體之禮，舍敬則禮文皆虛耳？故曰：「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？」舜之主祭而百神享，蓋不在類禋望徧之儀文也。後世封祀郊雍，殆不知敬爲何物。旨哉，「明德惟馨」之訓！此虞周之所以爲至治也。

政貴有恒，辭尚體要。
張中鴻

translation_en:
…to establish the foundation for spiritual communion, you need only discharge your office reverently. How could you merely withdraw and decline?” Ah! In Bo Yi we see sincerity in recommending worthy men; in Emperor Shun we see single-mindedness in entrusting responsibility to the worthy. We can readily imagine the harmonious spirit of the ruler and ministers of Yu. Moreover, manifesting virtue and attending to sacrifices are not two separate things. When Shun appointed the Minister of Ancestral Rites, he repeatedly enjoined attentiveness and reverence. Was this not because reverence is ritual without outward form, and without reverence all ritual forms are empty? Thus it is said: “Ritual, ritual—is it merely jade and silk?” That the hundred spirits accepted Shun’s offerings when he presided over sacrifices surely did not depend upon the ceremonial forms of the lei sacrifice, the yin sacrifice, the distant sacrifices, and the comprehensive offerings. Later generations performed sacrifices of enfeoffment and worship at Yong [?], yet scarcely knew what reverence was. How profound the teaching, “Only luminous virtue is fragrant”! This is why Yu and Zhou attained the utmost order.

“In government, constancy is prized; in language, substance and concision are esteemed.”
By Zhang Zhonghong.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔In explaining “constancy” and “substance and concision,” he sweeps away verbose, commonplace language and brings out the single idea of substance.〕 His interpretation of “esteemed” rises above the ordinary. This, too, is writing with substance and deserves selection.
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔The ideas are refined and the language elegant; the structure is orderly and the vital force flows freely.〕
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔Dignified and rich, classical and well regulated, it far surpasses the other compositions.〕

When one remains constant in one’s way and commands are not burdensomely numerous, the essential character of government and commands is firmly established. How could anyone wishing to transform the people of Yin accomplish it apart from this? King Kang charged the Duke of Bi with safeguarding and governing the eastern suburbs.
