Thus he discussed the Book of Changes in Baihu Hall and the Book of Documents in Wuying Hall; reading the Analects, he commended its essentials for governing the state…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
讀孟子究仁義之旨而
聖學光昭者莫非始終典學之要焉蓋其心之
存也瑩然如水之澄而無纖芥也空然如
鑑之明而無遺照也粹然如良玉之潤而
純潔無瑕也融然如精金之耀而光彩奪
目也是以達之政也如天覆地載而無弗
被也如日照月臨而無弗見也如甘雨湛
露而無弗涵濡霑足也如風行雷動而無
弗披拂鼓舞也盛德大業至矣哉所以衍
千聖之心傳開萬世之太平以為
===
聖子
神孫之法程者善矣美矣我
皇上躬睿哲之資撫恭隆之運
臨御以來四年于玆講幄弘開忠讜彙進
紀元一詔而海宇覃恩
尊親一詔而孝思維則以至
幸大學親
郊廟秉耒耜閱營兵拔擢遺英褒奬忠直廣言
punctuated:
讀《孟子》，究仁義之旨，而聖學光昭者，莫非始終典學之要焉。蓋其心之存也，瑩然如水之澄而無纖芥也，空然如鑑之明而無遺照也，粹然如良玉之潤而純潔無瑕也，融然如精金之耀而光彩奪目也。是以達之政也，如天覆地載而無弗被也，如日照月臨而無弗見也，如甘雨湛露而無弗涵濡霑足也，如風行雷動而無弗披拂鼓舞也。盛德大業至矣哉！所以衍千聖之心傳，開萬世之太平，以為聖子神孫之法程者，善矣美矣！
我皇上躬睿哲之資，撫恭隆之運，臨御以來四年于玆，講幄弘開，忠讜彙進。紀元一詔而海宇覃恩，尊親一詔而孝思維則，以至幸大學，親郊廟，秉耒耜，閱營兵，拔擢遺英，褒奬忠直，廣言
translation_en:
…He read the Mencius to fathom the purport of benevolence and righteousness. The brilliance of his sagely learning invariably rested on the essential principle of constant devotion to learning from beginning to end. His mind was lucid, like clear water without the slightest speck; open, like a bright mirror whose reflection omits nothing; pure, like the luster of fine jade, immaculate and flawless; and radiant, like refined gold whose brilliance dazzles the eye. Thus, when expressed in government, it was like Heaven covering and Earth bearing all things, leaving nothing outside its care; like the sun shining and the moon looking down, leaving nothing unseen; like timely rain and abundant dew, leaving nothing unmoistened or unsatisfied; and like wind sweeping forth and thunder stirring, leaving nothing untouched or unanimated. How consummate his flourishing virtue and great achievements! How excellent and splendid the means by which he perpetuated the transmission of the sages’ mind, inaugurated peace for ten thousand generations, and established a model for his sagely sons and divine grandsons!
Our Emperor, endowed with penetrating wisdom, presides over an age of reverence and prosperity [?]. Four years have now passed since he ascended the throne. He has opened wide the imperial lecture chamber, and loyal, forthright counsel has poured in. With a single edict inaugurating his reign era, he extended his benevolence throughout the realm; with a single edict honoring his parents, he made filial devotion a model. Furthermore, he has visited the Imperial University, personally performed the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices, taken up the plow, inspected the garrison troops, promoted overlooked men of talent, commended the loyal and upright, and broadened the avenues of remonstrance…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
路以通耳目恤災困以賑饑荒教稼
宵勤憂蝗
露禱其敷
帝德塞
皇猷八埏九域蒸蒸洋洋遠邁帝王而近符
烈祖者淵以穆光且大也執事猶欲於進講奏
對紀述陳謨期以弘
啓沃效賛襄肆蘭臺之直筆揮
彤陛之昌言愚有以知盛心矣夫
===
皇天眷命猶亹儆戒之謨萬邦作乂不廢幾康
之弼人臣愛君之心固無已也敢以輔養
聖德而光昭
祖烈之四事爲
今日獻焉一曰肅進講之規夫鳴玉
龍墀殫思
鳳閣淸華之選備矣而錦帙牙籤非不日侍
經筵也然尚未副望道之懷何歟愚以爲講
畢進規
punctuated:
路以通耳目，恤災困以賑饑荒，教稼宵勤，憂蝗露禱。其敷帝德、塞皇猷，八埏九域，蒸蒸洋洋，遠邁帝王而近符烈祖者，淵以穆，光且大也。執事猶欲於進講奏對、紀述陳謨，期以弘啓沃，效賛襄，肆蘭臺之直筆，揮彤陛之昌言，愚有以知盛心矣。夫皇天眷命，猶亹儆戒之謨；萬邦作乂，不廢幾康之弼。人臣愛君之心，固無已也。敢以輔養聖德而光昭祖烈之四事，爲今日獻焉。
一曰：肅進講之規。夫鳴玉龍墀，殫思鳳閣，淸華之選備矣；而錦帙牙籤，非不日侍經筵也。然尚未副望道之懷，何歟？愚以爲講畢進規，
translation_en:
…avenues for speech to keep his eyes and ears informed; he has relieved those distressed by disasters and alleviated famine, labored into the night over instruction in farming, and, anxious about locusts, prayed beneath the open sky. In spreading imperial virtue and fulfilling his sovereign designs throughout the eight limits and nine regions of the realm, his influence flourishes and flows abundantly. Far surpassing the emperors and kings of antiquity and closely matching his illustrious forebears, his achievements are profound and august, radiant and great. Yet you gentlemen still seek, through lectures and responses to the throne, historical accounts and the presentation of counsel, to broaden the instruction that nourishes the sovereign’s mind and contribute your assistance: to wield the candid brush of the Orchid Terrace and voice excellent counsel before the vermilion steps. I can thus discern your lofty intentions. Even when August Heaven bestows its favor and mandate, admonitory counsel must still be diligently offered; even when the myriad states are well governed, assistance in bringing all affairs to good order must not cease. A minister’s love for his sovereign indeed knows no end. I venture to submit today four measures for nurturing His Majesty’s sagely virtue and making manifest the glorious achievements of his ancestors.
First: make the procedures for presenting lectures more rigorous. With jade pendants sounding upon the dragon-adorned steps, and minds exerted to the utmost in the phoenix pavilion, the chosen men of distinguished scholarly standing are all assembled. Nor do they fail to attend daily at the Classics Colloquium with brocade-wrapped volumes and ivory book labels. Yet they have still not fulfilled His Majesty’s longing for the Way. Why is this? In my humble opinion, after the lecture is concluded, admonitions should be presented…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
先朝有之矣請一法之凡時政之得失人才之
進退不厭煩瀆務求聽納如程頥賢哉田
也之章真足以格君心可也二曰復
召對之規夫寒極靡涯隱伏無盡休戚之關
大矣而連篇累牘非不日請
召對也然尚未見施行之實何歟愚以爲
先朝行之矣請遂復之凡軍國之利害人品之
御門論政
邪正每日奏對務竭忠猷如韓琦相爭如
虎之事真足以裨實政可也三曰備史紀
之官出入起居君德惟彰左右前後鑒觀
攸係史職之不可不備也審矣
高廟嘗設起居注矣永樂間始罷之亦
朝家故事也愚請倣唐宋柱下史日輪一人
起居禁中隨事輙記而他日之實錄稽焉
不必更設其官即專屬之瑣闥之臣可也
四曰重諫諍之職從諫克聖古有明徵朝
無諍臣則不知過諫官之不可不重也明
punctuated:
先朝有之矣，請一法之。凡時政之得失、人才之進退，不厭煩瀆，務求聽納，如程頥「賢哉田也」之章，真足以格君心可也。
二曰復召對之規。夫寒極靡涯，隱伏無盡，休戚之關大矣。而連篇累牘，非不日請召對也，然尚未見施行之實，何歟？愚以爲先朝行之矣，請遂復之。凡軍國之利害、人品之御門論政邪正，每日奏對，務竭忠猷，如韓琦相爭如虎之事，真足以裨實政可也。
三曰備史紀之官。出入起居，君德惟彰；左右前後，鑒觀攸係。史職之不可不備也，審矣。高廟嘗設起居注矣，永樂間始罷之，亦朝家故事也。愚請倣唐宋柱下史，日輪一人，起居禁中，隨事輙記，而他日之實錄稽焉。不必更設其官，即專屬之瑣闥之臣可也。
四曰重諫諍之職。從諫克聖，古有明徵；朝無諍臣，則不知過。諫官之不可不重也，明
translation_en:
…There was such a practice under former reigns; I ask that it be taken as a model. Concerning successes and failures in current government and the advancement or dismissal of talented men, let repeated representations cause no impatience, and make every effort to hear and accept them. Follow Cheng Yi’s exposition of the passage “How worthy Tian is!” [?; apparently “How worthy Hui is!”]. Such counsel should truly suffice to rectify the ruler’s heart.
Second, restore the practice of summoning officials to audience. The cold reaches are boundless [?], and hidden matters are inexhaustible; their bearing on well-being and distress is great. Memorials pile up, and requests for audiences are indeed submitted daily. Yet why have we still seen no actual implementation? In my humble view, former reigns followed this practice; I ask that it now be restored. Concerning the advantages and dangers in military and state affairs, and the depravity or uprightness of men’s character, let officials report and answer questions daily, fully offering their loyal counsel. [The words “discuss government at the imperial gate” appear here in a disrupted position in the transcription.] Follow the example of Han Qi’s “contending like a tiger” [?], so that this may truly benefit practical government.
Third, provide a full complement of officials to record history. In the ruler’s movements and daily activities, his virtue is displayed; those around him, on every side, bear upon the scrutiny of his conduct. It is therefore certain that the historiographical offices must be fully staffed. The founding emperor once established the office of Imperial Diarist; it was abolished only during the Yongle reign. This too is a precedent of our dynasty. I humbly request that, following the court historiographers of the Tang and Song, one man serve in rotation each day within the palace precincts, recording events as they occur, so that the Veritable Records compiled in later days may consult these accounts. There need be no additional office: this duty may be assigned exclusively to the supervising secretaries.
Fourth, give weight to the duty of remonstrance. Antiquity offers clear proof that accepting remonstrance enables a ruler to become a sage. If the court has no ministers who remonstrate, the ruler will not know his faults. That remonstrating officials must be accorded weight is clear…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
矣頃年以來言路開矣而報章稠疊實用
則踈也愚請
祖宗設官初意專精其任知之必言言之必聽
而昌時之政治頼焉務使誠心直道不徒
事於章奏之文可也夫然則衆思集而忠
益弘我
皇上所以懋純心之學弘法
祖之烈而遠紹帝王心學之統者或可仰禆萬
一矣雖然有本焉
===
君心是也尤願我
聖天子凝神宥密澄慮靜觀察理欲於幾微敦
培養而匪懈使虛明之地一疵不存化理
之原萬用攸裕然後善言觸而江河若決
心學純而德業兼隆凡
經筵
召對無善弗庸史職諫臣有言必入而
聖神文武之德廣運於無窮翼翼爲明聽之賢周
知而不爽殆與
punctuated: 矣。頃年以來，言路開矣，而報章稠疊，實用則踈也。愚請祖宗設官初意，專精其任，知之必言，言之必聽，而昌時之政治頼焉。務使誠心直道，不徒事於章奏之文，可也。夫然，則衆思集而忠益弘。我皇上所以懋純心之學，弘法祖之烈，而遠紹帝王心學之統者，或可仰禆萬一矣。雖然，有本焉：君心是也。尤願我聖天子凝神宥密，澄慮靜觀，察理欲於幾微，敦培養而匪懈，使虛明之地一疵不存，化理之原萬用攸裕。然後善言觸而江河若決，心學純而德業兼隆。凡經筵、召對，無善弗庸；史職、諫臣，有言必入。而聖神文武之德廣運於無窮，翼翼爲明聽之賢，周知而不爽，殆與
translation_en:
… is clear. In recent years, the channels for remonstrance have been opened, yet responses to memorials pile up while practical implementation remains scant. I humbly request that the original intention of the imperial ancestors in establishing these offices [be followed?]: let their holders devote themselves fully to their duties, invariably speak of what they know, and invariably receive a hearing when they speak. The governance of a flourishing age depends upon this. Ensure that they act with sincere hearts and upright principles, rather than merely attending to the literary form of their memorials. This would suffice. Then the thinking of many would be brought together, and the benefits of loyal counsel would increase. This might contribute, however slightly, to Your Majesty’s efforts to advance the learning that purifies the mind, magnify the achievements of emulating the imperial ancestors, and carry forward the ancient transmission of the learning of the mind among emperors and kings. Yet there is a foundation for all this: the ruler’s mind.

Above all, I wish that our sagely Son of Heaven would concentrate his spirit in profound stillness, clarify his thoughts through quiet contemplation, discern heavenly principle from selfish desire in their subtlest beginnings, and diligently foster self-cultivation without slackening. Thus, not a single blemish would remain in the mind’s open clarity, and the source of transformative governance would amply sustain its myriad applications. Then, when good counsel touches the mind, its response would be like great rivers bursting forth; the learning of the mind would become pure, and virtue and achievement would flourish together. In the Classics Colloquium and in summoned audiences, no good counsel would go unused; whenever the historiographers and remonstrating officials spoke, their words would be accepted. Your Majesty’s sagely, spiritual, civil, and martial virtues would extend their influence without limit. Reverently attentive, possessing the worthiness of discerning hearing [?], comprehensively informed and free from error, you would perhaps, together with …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
祖同符而與天為一者矣書曰始終惟一時乃
日新又曰視乃烈祖無時豫怠此固
聖天子法
祖建中之盛而緝熙聖學之原也執事以為然
否
第二問
傅光宅
同考試官教諭戰　批〔經學不明本以諸儒多言所晦所以千載無真儒百世無善治此耳是作發明經學明晦之由而折衷於宋儒卓有定見其能〕
===
〔開示來學使知趨向其裨益於世教弘矣錄之〕
同考試官學正邵　批〔以五經為聖人不得已之言而以多言陋漢儒以躬行心得開來學可謂灼見道體矣子其有造者耶〕
考試官教諭余　批〔妨經病道每以古今儒者虛談之故子剖析諸儒闊論而末歸重於躬行可以與言經者〕
考試官教授李　批〔議論有根據引援有蘊藉剖斷有識見不凡之士也〕
聖人之經所以明道也而萬世之心學以
開諸儒之談經所以立言也而五經之眞
源始晦夫道何有于言哉天地之初道且
punctuated:
祖同符而與天為一者矣。《書》曰：「始終惟一，時乃日新。」又曰：「視乃烈祖，無時豫怠。」此固聖天子法祖建中之盛，而緝熙聖學之原也。執事以為然否？

第二問
傅光宅

同考試官教諭戰批〔經學不明，本以諸儒多言所晦，所以千載無真儒，百世無善治，此耳。是作發明經學明晦之由，而折衷於宋儒，卓有定見。其能開示來學，使知趨向，其裨益於世教弘矣。錄之。〕
同考試官學正邵批〔以五經為聖人不得已之言，而以多言陋漢儒，以躬行心得開來學，可謂灼見道體矣。子其有造者耶？〕
考試官教諭余批〔妨經病道，每以古今儒者虛談之故。子剖析諸儒闊論，而末歸重於躬行，可以與言經者。〕
考試官教授李批〔議論有根據，引援有蘊藉，剖斷有識見，不凡之士也。〕

聖人之經，所以明道也，而萬世之心學以開；諸儒之談經，所以立言也，而五經之眞源始晦。夫道何有于言哉？天地之初，道且
translation_en:
…accords with his ancestor and is one with Heaven. The Book of Documents says: “Be constant from beginning to end, and thus renew yourself daily.” It also says: “Look to your illustrious ancestors; never indulge in ease or indolence.” This indeed is the splendor of the sage Son of Heaven’s emulating his ancestors and establishing the mean, and the source of his continuing to illuminate sagely learning. Do you, sir, consider this correct?

Second Question
Fu Guangzhai

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhan, Instructor: 〔Classical learning is unclear fundamentally because the excessive words of the scholars have obscured it. This alone explains why a thousand years have passed without a true Confucian and a hundred generations without good government. This composition elucidates the causes of clarity and obscurity in classical learning, taking the Song Confucians as its standard of judgment, and displays outstandingly firm convictions. It can enlighten future students and show them what direction to take; its contribution to moral instruction in the world is great. Include it in the record.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔You regard the Five Classics as words the sages uttered only because they had no alternative, and judge the Han Confucians deficient for their excessive words. By personal practice and understanding gained in the heart, you enlighten future students. This may indeed be called a penetrating perception of the substance of the Way. Are you perhaps one who has attained it?〕

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: 〔Obstruction of the Classics and injury to the Way repeatedly arise from the empty talk of Confucians, past and present. You analyze the scholars’ sweeping pronouncements and ultimately place the greatest weight on personal practice. You are someone with whom one can discuss the Classics.〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: 〔Your arguments have a foundation, your citations have depth and reserve, and your analyses and judgments show discernment. You are a man of uncommon ability.〕

The sages’ Classics serve to illuminate the Way, thereby opening up the learning of the mind for all generations. The scholars’ discussions of the Classics serve to establish their own pronouncements, and with these the true source of the Five Classics begins to be obscured. What has the Way to do with words? At the beginning of Heaven and Earth, the Way still…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
無名也而何有于言惟風氣日開道體爲
裂則時之變矣聖人深憂之不容於無言
也於是乎五經出焉於是乎刪述定焉苟
以明吾道已耳不得已而然者也而豈其
心哉後世諸儒之談經也不然焉可已而
不已者也或發於意見或激於辨駁立言
以成一家其詞非不精而終爲輪轅之飾
其理非不粹而不免步驟之私吁道本無
言而強言之已非聖人心而至於紛紛多
===
言焉又至於純駁相參焉則道體於是乎
愈裂而五經真源於是乎晦而不可尋矣
吁愈多愈晦吾固憂其所終也夫六經不
明天地閉塞所關不小請因執事下詢而
陳之粤惟未始有物之前亦未始無物之
後有伏羲堯舜禹湯文武周孔之爲聖易
書詩禮記春秋之爲經所以發天地之秘
而立民命開太平者至矣然所以垂法萬
世與天地相爲始終者惟孔子集羣聖之
punctuated:
無名也，而何有于言？惟風氣日開，道體爲裂，則時之變矣。聖人深憂之，不容於無言也。於是乎五經出焉，於是乎刪述定焉，苟以明吾道已耳，不得已而然者也，而豈其心哉？後世諸儒之談經也不然焉，可已而不已者也。或發於意見，或激於辨駁，立言以成一家。其詞非不精，而終爲輪轅之飾；其理非不粹，而不免步驟之私。吁！道本無言，而強言之，已非聖人心；而至於紛紛多言焉，又至於純駁相參焉，則道體於是乎愈裂，而五經真源於是乎晦而不可尋矣。吁！愈多愈晦，吾固憂其所終也。夫六經不明，天地閉塞，所關不小。請因執事下詢而陳之。
粤惟未始有物之前，亦未始無物之後，有伏羲、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周、孔之爲聖，《易》、《書》、《詩》、《禮記》、《春秋》之爲經，所以發天地之秘而立民命、開太平者至矣。然所以垂法萬世，與天地相爲始終者，惟孔子集羣聖之
translation_en:
…was nameless; how, then, could there have been words? Only as the temper of the age progressively unfolded and the substance of the Way became fragmented did circumstances change. The sages were deeply troubled by this and could not remain silent. Thus the Five Classics appeared; thus their editing and exposition were settled. This was merely to make our Way clear, something undertaken because there was no alternative. How could it have been their heart’s desire? Later scholars’ discussions of the classics were otherwise: they could have stopped, yet did not. Some arose from personal opinions, others were provoked by disputation and refutation; they formulated doctrines to establish schools of their own. Their language was certainly refined, yet ultimately amounted to ornamenting wheels and shafts; their principles were certainly subtle, yet could not escape the partiality of their own chosen paths. Alas! The Way originally had no words, and forcing it into words already departed from the sages’ intent. When this went so far as a welter of proliferating words, and further still to an intermingling of the pure and the impure, the substance of the Way became ever more fragmented, and the true source of the Five Classics became obscured beyond recovery. Alas! The more words, the greater the obscurity. I have good reason to fear where this will end. When the Six Classics are not understood, Heaven and Earth are closed off: what is at stake is no small matter. Allow me to set this forth in response to your gracious inquiry.
Now, before things had ever begun to exist, and likewise after things had never been absent [?], there were such sages as Fuxi, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius, and such classics as the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, the Book of Odes, the Record of Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals. Their means of revealing the mysteries of Heaven and Earth, securing the people’s livelihood, and ushering in great peace were consummate. Yet, as for transmitting models for ten thousand generations, enduring from beginning to end with Heaven and Earth, it was Confucius alone who brought together the achievements of all the sages…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
大成精刪定之心法易張十翼以黜誕禮
樂正五紀以黜僭詩書列四始四代以黜
不雅春秋著五例以黜不王六經之道又
一開闢也譬諸爐天地工日月以爲洪鍾
豈錚錚細響者飾聽哉當是時也顏曾思
孟獨得其宗而七十子各有所受以傳於
諸侯之國易有子木而授於衛馬詩有卜
商而授於西河焉春秋有左丘明而衍爲
國語焉南宮敬叔伋各有以授於魯宋焉
===
道在六經是又當陽爝火其光同炳也何
啻一日佚其緒哉厥後秦火烈焰六經沉
寒易幸以卜筮存矣而猶失說卦三篇其
後得之於河內能皆其全文乎書幸以孔
壁存矣而猶失泰誓一篇其後得之於河
南能皆其原旨乎詩以諷詠得全而觀素
絢棠棣之逸其散失者衆矣禮以尊君得
采而觀考工記之補其附會者多矣一時
編簡存者無幾泯泯紛紛無所攷據豈非
punctuated: 大成，精刪定之心法：易張十翼以黜誕，禮樂正五紀以黜僭，詩書列四始四代以黜不雅，春秋著五例以黜不王。六經之道，又一開闢也。譬諸爐天地、工日月以爲洪鍾，豈錚錚細響者飾聽哉？當是時也，顏曾思孟獨得其宗，而七十子各有所受，以傳於諸侯之國。易有子木而授於衛馬，詩有卜商而授於西河焉，春秋有左丘明而衍爲國語焉，南宮敬叔、伋各有以授於魯宋焉。道在六經，是又當陽爝火，其光同炳也，何啻一日佚其緒哉？厥後秦火烈焰，六經沉寒。易幸以卜筮存矣，而猶失說卦三篇，其後得之於河內，能皆其全文乎？書幸以孔壁存矣，而猶失泰誓一篇，其後得之於河南，能皆其原旨乎？詩以諷詠得全，而觀素絢棠棣之逸，其散失者衆矣。禮以尊君得采，而觀考工記之補，其附會者多矣。一時編簡存者無幾，泯泯紛紛，無所攷據，豈非
translation_en:
…the grand synthesis, perfecting the guiding principles of deletion and definitive arrangement: for the Changes, he set forth the Ten Wings to reject the fantastic; for rites and music, he rectified the five ordering principles to reject usurpation; for the Odes and Documents, he arranged the four beginnings and the four dynasties to reject what was improper; and for the Spring and Autumn Annals, he established the five precedents to reject departures from true kingship. The Way of the Six Classics thus underwent another creation of heaven and earth. It was as though heaven and earth were the furnace and the sun and moon the craftsmen casting a great bell. Could mere tinkling sounds embellish what one heard? At that time, Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mencius alone grasped its essential teaching, while the seventy disciples each received something to transmit to the feudal states. For the Changes, there was Zimu, who transmitted it to Wei Ma [?]; for the Odes, there was Bu Shang, who taught at Xihe; for the Spring and Autumn Annals, there was Zuo Qiuming, who expanded it into the Discourses of the States. Nangong Jingshu and Ji each had teachings to transmit in Lu and Song. The Way resided in the Six Classics: this was again like torchlight in the presence of the sun, their radiance shining together. How could its thread have been lost for even a single day [?]?

Thereafter, the fierce flames of Qin's book burning left the Six Classics submerged in cold obscurity. Fortunately, the Changes survived because of its use in divination, yet the three chapters including Explaining the Trigrams were still lost. When they were later recovered in Henei, could they all have been complete texts? Fortunately, the Documents survived within the wall of Confucius's house, yet the chapter Great Declaration was still lost. When it was later recovered in Henan, could it have preserved its original purport throughout? The Odes were preserved intact through recitation and singing; yet, considering the lost passages concerning the plain ground and ornamentation, and the cherry tree's blossoms [?], much had been scattered and lost. The Rites gained acceptance because it honored the ruler; yet, considering its supplementation with the Record of Artificers, much had been added through forced association. At that time, very few bound sets of bamboo slips survived. Amid obscurity and confusion, there was nothing on which to base verification. Was this not…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
斯文之一厄而世道之不幸歟自今考之
連山歸藏以並易矣然成言乎艮而連山
以艮爲首義何所取乾統八卦而歸藏以
坤爲首乾何所列其象山出雲氣堯二女
之說尤爲怪誕唐州僞書之疑似未始無
見也至若焦贛之易林十六卷洼丹之易
通七篇鄭玄之易緯易賛易論三首李見
之易樞十卷阮逸之易筌六卷古易則呂
大防晁說之王雎陽呂祖謙周璠五家皆
===
以擬易然不過象數之詞耳於四聖之旨
何補雖五家援經立論不出易道本旨而
改更次序各以師承自難信矣况其他乎
三墳五典以說書矣然山墳氣墳形墳之
傳各以象明連山歸藏坤乾之屬各以意
定其三皇三墳五帝五典之說尤覺玄遠
太史不雅之稱似未爲無指也至若歐陽
夏侯等之九家書劉向之校三家經文鄭
玄之尚書中候劉陶傳之中文尚書王粲
punctuated:
斯文之一厄，而世道之不幸歟？自今考之，《連山》《歸藏》以並《易》矣。然「成言乎艮」，而《連山》以艮爲首，義何所取？乾統八卦，而《歸藏》以坤爲首，乾何所列？其象山出雲氣、堯二女之說，尤爲怪誕。唐州僞書之疑，似未始無見也。至若焦贛之《易林》十六卷、洼丹之《易通》七篇、鄭玄之《易緯》《易賛》《易論》三首、李見之《易樞》十卷、阮逸之《易筌》六卷，《古易》則呂大防、晁說之、王雎陽、呂祖謙、周璠五家，皆以擬《易》。然不過象數之詞耳，於四聖之旨何補？雖五家援經立論，不出《易》道本旨，而改更次序，各以師承，自難信矣，况其他乎？

《三墳》《五典》以說《書》矣。然《山墳》《氣墳》《形墳》之傳，各以象明；《連山》《歸藏》《坤乾》之屬，各以意定。其三皇三墳、五帝五典之說，尤覺玄遠。太史不雅之稱，似未爲無指也。至若歐陽、夏侯等之九家《書》、劉向之校三家經文、鄭玄之《尚書中候》、劉陶傳之《中文尚書》、王粲
translation_en:
…a calamity for this cultural tradition, and a misfortune for the moral order of the world? Examining them from our present standpoint, the Linked Mountains (Lianshan) and the Return to the Hidden (Guicang) have been placed alongside the Book of Changes. Yet the Changes says, “Completion is spoken of in Gen,” while the Linked Mountains places Gen first: on what principle is this based? Qian governs the eight trigrams, yet the Return to the Hidden places Kun first: where, then, does it place Qian? Its accounts of images of mountains sending forth clouds and vapor, and of Yao’s two daughters, are especially bizarre. The suspicion that the text from Tangzhou was a forgery seems not to have been without insight.

As for Jiao Gan’s Forest of Changes, in sixteen juan; Wa Dan’s Comprehensive Account of the Changes, in seven sections; Zheng Xuan’s Apocrypha of the Changes, Praise of the Changes, and Discourse on the Changes, three works; Li Jian’s [?] Pivot of the Changes, in ten juan; and Ruan Yi’s Guide to the Changes, in six juan—as well as the Ancient Changes associated with the five scholars Lü Dafang, Chao Shuozhi, Wang Juyang [?], Lü Zuqian, and Zhou Fan—all were intended to emulate the Changes. Yet they amount merely to discussions of images and numbers: what do they add to the purport of the four sages? Although the five scholars cite the classic in establishing their arguments and remain within the fundamental meaning of the Way of the Changes, they alter its sequence, each following his own lineage of instruction. They are thus difficult to trust; how much more so the others!

The Three Tombs (Sanfen) and Five Canons (Wudian) have been used to explain the Book of Documents. Yet the transmitted accounts of the Mountain Tomb, Breath Tomb, and Form Tomb each explain matters through images, while such categories as the Linked Mountains, Return to the Hidden, and Kun and Qian are each determined by interpretation. The claim that the Three Tombs belong to the Three Sovereigns and the Five Canons to the Five Emperors seems especially obscure and remote. The Grand Historian’s description of such material as lacking refinement seems not to have been without a specific target. As for the nine schools of the Documents, including those of Ouyang and Xiahou; Liu Xiang’s collation of the texts of three schools; Zheng Xuan’s Central Observations on the Book of Documents; the Central Text of the Book of Documents [?] transmitted by Liu Tao; and Wang Can …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之釋問崔良佐之演範楊繪元素之九意
摩則謝沈王肅范甯李顒姜道盛等二十
五家皆以擬書然不過訓詁之詞耳於典
謨之旨何益雖劉向傳經刋誤不出中古
本法而所傳五行即多乖戾不可傳矣況
其餘乎擬詩者王肅毛詩則義駁八卷奏
事一卷問難一卷劉璠則箋傳是非二卷
韋昭朱育則答雜問七卷非不各有意見
而取舍各殊即非逆志之得夫詩自魯申
===
公立訓而轅固韓嬰各加傳疏當時皆善
說詩者而已病其非本義矣況王韋輩又
其支流者耶擬禮者大戴則刪古禮爲八
十五篇戴聖則刪大戴爲小戴爲四十六
篇馬融則足月令明堂樂記爲四十九篇
高堂生傳士禮十七篇非不各有攷訂而
詳略互異恐非會通之觀夫禮自河間獻
王始得而劉歆校理遂加著錄當時尚去
古不遠而已苦其多缺逸矣況德聖輩又
punctuated:
之《釋問》，崔良佐之《演範》，楊繪元素之《九意》《摩則》，謝沈、王肅、范甯、李顒、姜道盛等二十五家，皆以擬《書》，然不過訓詁之詞耳，於典謨之旨何益？雖劉向傳經刋誤，不出中古本法，而所傳《五行》即多乖戾，不可傳矣，況其餘乎？擬《詩》者，王肅《毛詩》則《義駁》八卷，《奏事》一卷，《問難》一卷；劉璠則《箋傳是非》二卷；韋昭、朱育則《答雜問》七卷。非不各有意見，而取舍各殊，即非逆志之得。夫《詩》自魯申公立訓，而轅固、韓嬰各加傳疏，當時皆善說《詩》者，而已病其非本義矣，況王、韋輩又其支流者耶？

擬《禮》者，大戴則刪古禮爲八十五篇，戴聖則刪大戴爲小戴，爲四十六篇，馬融則足《月令》《明堂》《樂記》爲四十九篇，高堂生傳《士禮》十七篇。非不各有攷訂，而詳略互異，恐非會通之觀。夫《禮》自河間獻王始得，而劉歆校理，遂加著錄，當時尚去古不遠，而已苦其多缺逸矣，況德、聖輩又
translation_en:
…his Explanations of Questions; Cui Liangzuo’s Elucidation of the Great Plan; Yang Hui, styled Yuansu’s Nine Meanings and Models [?]; and the twenty-five schools represented by Xie Chen, Wang Su, Fan Ning, Li Yong, Jiang Daosheng, and others—all sought to emulate the Book of Documents. Yet these are merely verbal glosses: what benefit do they bring to understanding the purport of its canons and counsels? Although Liu Xiang, in transmitting the classic and correcting its errors, kept within the original methods of middle antiquity, the Five Phases material he transmitted already contained many inconsistencies and could not be handed down as authoritative. How much more so the others!

Among those who sought to emulate the Book of Poetry, Wang Su’s writings on the Mao Poetry included eight juan of Refutations of Interpretations, one juan of Memorials on Affairs, and one juan of Questions and Challenges; Liu Fan wrote two juan of Merits and Faults of the Annotations and Commentary; and Wei Zhao and Zhu Yu wrote seven juan of Answers to Miscellaneous Questions. It is not that they lacked views of their own, but their choices of what to accept and reject differed, and thus they failed to apprehend the poets’ intentions. After Master Shen of Lu established his glosses on the Poetry, Yuan Gu and Han Ying each added commentaries and explanations. All were skilled interpreters of the Poetry in their day, yet their interpretations were already criticized for departing from its original meaning. How much more so Wang, Wei, and their fellows, who were merely offshoots of those traditions!

Among those who sought to emulate the ritual classics, the Elder Dai abridged the ancient ritual texts into eighty-five chapters; Dai Sheng abridged the Elder Dai’s collection into the Younger Dai’s, comprising forty-six chapters; and Ma Rong supplemented it with the Monthly Ordinances, Hall of Enlightenment, and Record of Music, making forty-nine chapters. Gaotang Sheng transmitted seventeen chapters of the Rites of the Shi. It is not that each lacked textual investigation and correction, but their degrees of detail differed, and I fear they lacked a comprehensive understanding of how the material fit together. The ritual texts were first recovered by Prince Xian of Hejian; Liu Xin then collated and arranged them and entered them in the bibliographical record. At that time antiquity was still not far distant, yet scholars already lamented the many omissions and losses. How much more so when Dai De, Dai Sheng, and their fellows also …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
多𥿄附者耶春秋自經聖筆遂列於經然
攷於前古經外傳等有二十三家矣公羊
穀梁等有四家矣是孔子之前不已有春
秋之名耶而感時垂戒特託其書以存王
迹焉耳故曰其義則丘竊取之以此左氏
傳二十公羊傳十二穀梁傳十五皆依經
辨理各成條段先儒有或誣或短或俗之
譏矣要之則左氏義嚴君父其主爲正賈
逵作長義以別之不亦公乎郗萌圖緯五
===
十篇董仲舒繁露十七篇劉兆調人萬餘
言皆錯經合異各有指趨先儒有失眞辨
譏之詆矣要之則仲舒義引宏博其學爲
醇史記卽著文以推之不亦正乎何休五
始三科九旨七等六輔二類不過謂元年
春王正月公卽位等之凡例耳初無深意
晁說之譏其持負公羊之學豈非有厭其
紛紛耶噫天地聖人之秘盡於五經而垂
憲之功成於夫子至矣盡矣無以加矣而
punctuated: 多𥿄附者耶？《春秋》自經聖筆，遂列於經。然攷於前古，《經外傳》等有二十三家矣，《公羊》《穀梁》等有四家矣，是孔子之前不已有《春秋》之名耶？而感時垂戒，特託其書以存王迹焉耳。故曰：「其義則丘竊取之。」以此，《左氏傳》二十，《公羊傳》十二，《穀梁傳》十五，皆依經辨理，各成條段。先儒有或誣、或短、或俗之譏矣。要之，則左氏義嚴君父，其主爲正。賈逵作《長義》以別之，不亦公乎？郗萌《圖緯》五十篇，董仲舒《繁露》十七篇，劉兆《調人》萬餘言，皆錯經合異，各有指趨。先儒有失眞辨譏之詆矣。要之，則仲舒義引宏博，其學爲醇。《史記》卽著文以推之，不亦正乎？何休五始、三科、九旨、七等、六輔、二類，不過謂「元年春王正月，公卽位」等之凡例耳，初無深意。晁說之譏其持負公羊之學，豈非有厭其紛紛耶？噫！天地聖人之秘，盡於《五經》，而垂憲之功成於夫子，至矣，盡矣，無以加矣，而
translation_en:
…were they not also responsible for many extraneous additions [?]? Once the Spring and Autumn Annals had passed through the sage’s brush, it was ranked among the Classics. Yet an investigation of earlier antiquity reveals twenty-three schools or works, including the Outer Commentary on the Classic, and four including Gongyang and Guliang. Did the title Spring and Autumn Annals not therefore already exist before Confucius? Responding to his times and transmitting admonitions to posterity, he merely used this book to preserve the traces of true kingship. Thus he said: “As for its meaning, I, Qiu, have ventured to take responsibility for it.” Accordingly, the Zuo Commentary in twenty chapters, the Gongyang Commentary in twelve, and the Guliang Commentary in fifteen all explicated principles by reference to the Classic, each arranging its material into sections. Earlier scholars criticized them respectively as unreliable, inadequate, or vulgar. In sum, however, the Zuo Commentary’s interpretation upholds strict reverence for ruler and father, and its guiding position is correct. Was it not fair of Jia Kui to write Superior Interpretations to distinguish its merits?

Xi Meng’s Charts and Apocrypha in fifty chapters, Dong Zhongshu’s Luxuriant Dew in seventeen chapters, and Liu Zhao’s Mediator in over ten thousand words all interweave the Classics and reconcile divergent interpretations, each with its own purport. Earlier scholars reproached them for departing from the truth and for their disputation and criticism [?]. In sum, however, Zhongshu’s interpretations draw on broad and extensive learning, and his scholarship is sound. Was it not right that the Records of the Grand Historian devoted a passage to commending him? He Xiu’s five beginnings, three categories, nine principles, seven grades, six auxiliaries, and two classes are merely general interpretive rules concerning such phrases as “In the first year, in spring, in the king’s first month, the duke assumed his position.” There was originally no profound meaning in them. When Chao Shuozhi criticized his reliance on Gongyang learning [?], was this not because he found its profusion tiresome?

Alas! The mysteries of Heaven, Earth, and the sages are fully contained in the Five Classics, and the achievement of transmitting enduring standards was completed by the Master. It is consummate and exhaustive; nothing can be added. Yet…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
後世散於百家蕩於末流溺於學者見聞
之外若此其浩博焉將欲明道適以生岐
矣將欲翼經適以增障矣昔堯之授舜曰
執中而舜復益之以精一夫精一之於執
中未遠也而中之渾淪者離矣孔之授參
曰一貫而參復益之以忠恕夫忠恕之於
一貫未遠也而一之渾淪者離矣故聖賢
兢兢焉惟恐其言多而病道其曰精一曰
忠恕不得已而言者也孔子曰予欲無言
===
言且欲無況多耶精一忠恕四字耳且離
道況載籍累累耶予故曰諸儒立言而經
始晦者此也嗚呼夫子沒而微言絕七十
子喪而大義乖聖賢懿訓與旨僅得一二
于煨燼之餘其枝鳴蹊唱且不暇責之至
如中公切躬行而僅談巡狩轅固譏曲學
而緘口罷歸珍名而砆質也夏侯垂意青
紫而以明皇極爲梯航匡衡溺情阿附而
以陳關雎爲壟斷設樊而攘鄰也兒寬以
punctuated:
後世散於百家，蕩於末流，溺於學者見聞之外，若此其浩博焉。將欲明道，適以生岐矣；將欲翼經，適以增障矣。昔堯之授舜曰「執中」，而舜復益之以精一。夫精一之於執中未遠也，而中之渾淪者離矣。孔之授參曰「一貫」，而參復益之以忠恕。夫忠恕之於一貫未遠也，而一之渾淪者離矣。故聖賢兢兢焉，惟恐其言多而病道。其曰精一、曰忠恕，不得已而言者也。孔子曰：「予欲無言。」言且欲無，況多耶？精一、忠恕四字耳，且離道，況載籍累累耶？予故曰，諸儒立言而經始晦者，此也。
嗚呼！夫子沒而微言絕，七十子喪而大義乖。聖賢懿訓與旨，僅得一二于煨燼之餘，其枝鳴蹊唱，且不暇責之。至如中公切躬行而僅談巡狩，轅固譏曲學而緘口罷歸，珍名而砆質也。夏侯垂意青紫而以明皇極爲梯航，匡衡溺情阿附而以陳關雎爲壟斷，設樊而攘鄰也。兒寬以
translation_en:
…In later ages, it became dispersed among the hundred schools, drifted into derivative currents, and sank beyond the range of scholars’ experience and learning—so vast had it become. Intended to illuminate the Way, it instead created divergent paths; intended to support the Classics, it instead added obstructions. Long ago, Yao instructed Shun to “hold fast to the mean,” and Shun further added refinement and single-mindedness. Refinement and single-mindedness are not far removed from holding fast to the mean, yet the undivided wholeness of the mean was thereby split apart. Confucius instructed Zeng Shen that “one thread runs through it,” and Shen further added doing one’s utmost for others and sympathetic understanding. These are not far removed from that single thread, yet the undivided wholeness of the one was thereby split apart. Thus the sages and worthies were ever cautious, fearing only that too many words would impair the Way. When they spoke of refinement and single-mindedness, or of doing one’s utmost and sympathetic understanding, they spoke only because they could not avoid doing so. Confucius said, “I wish to speak no words.” If he wished even to dispense with words, how much less would he wish for many! Refinement, single-mindedness, doing one’s utmost, and sympathetic understanding amount to only four written characters, yet even these depart from the Way. How much more so the accumulated volumes of writings! This, I therefore say, is why the Classics began to be obscured when the various scholars set forth their doctrines.
Alas! When the Master died, his subtle words ceased; when the seventy disciples passed away, the great principles became distorted. Of the admirable teachings and intentions of the sages and worthies, only a little was recovered from the ashes. As for the chirping from branches and singing along bypaths—their peripheral pronouncements—there is scarcely time even to reproach them. Take Zhonggong [?], who stressed personal practice yet merely discoursed on royal inspection tours, or Yuan Gu, who condemned distorted learning yet closed his mouth and withdrew from office: theirs was the reputation of precious jade but the substance of common stone. Xiahou set his heart on the blue and purple insignia of high office and used his exposition of the “Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard” as a ladder and ferry to advancement. Kuang Heng indulged his inclination to flatter and attach himself to the powerful, using his exposition of “Guanju” (“The Ospreys”) to secure a commanding position for private gain. They erected fences and encroached upon their neighbors. Er Kuan, by means of…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
術良而贊封禪之誅歐陽歆以世書而不
救多贓之敗張禹以帝師而不抑外戚之
權其口聖而腹魘者乎鄭夾漈曰秦人焚
書而書存漢儒窮經而經絕豈盡謂其學
之訛舛哉是故漢無經也唐尚詞賦去經
遠矣暨宋儒學術純正五經中興至今宗
之然語曰醴酒之美明水釀之文綺之麗
素絲織之貴其始耳向非漢儒掇拾六經
於前千載之下宋人孰從而考之哉此漢
===
儒未可深疵惟在窮經者知經所以明晦
耳學者誠能由宋儒開示之端以尋五經
之緒由五經已言之象以會羣聖無言之
眞而又反之吾心以求根本體之躬行以
驗實得如嫉奸權之專而必知幾于吉凶
如格藩主之非而必不事於縱闔出遊諫
矣書必行於致主法戒陳矣而詩必用於
拾遺訓釋註矣而言不遷於顧問則進退
語默皆經也其不有以翼五經之明哉故
punctuated:
術良而贊封禪之誅，歐陽歆以世書而不救多贓之敗，張禹以帝師而不抑外戚之權，其口聖而腹魘者乎？鄭夾漈曰：「秦人焚書而書存，漢儒窮經而經絕。」豈盡謂其學之訛舛哉？是故漢無經也。唐尚詞賦，去經遠矣。暨宋儒學術純正，五經中興，至今宗之。然語曰：「醴酒之美，明水釀之；文綺之麗，素絲織之。」貴其始耳。向非漢儒掇拾六經於前，千載之下，宋人孰從而考之哉？此漢儒未可深疵，惟在窮經者知經所以明晦耳。

學者誠能由宋儒開示之端，以尋五經之緒；由五經已言之象，以會羣聖無言之眞；而又反之吾心以求根本，體之躬行以驗實得：如嫉奸權之專，而必知幾于吉凶；如格藩主之非，而必不事於縱闔；出遊諫矣，書必行於致主；法戒陳矣，而詩必用於拾遺；訓釋註矣，而言不遷於顧問。則進退語默皆經也，其不有以翼五經之明哉？故
translation_en:
…though accomplished in his learning, he assisted in the wrongdoing associated with the feng and shan sacrifices [?]. Ouyang Xin, despite his family's hereditary study of the Book of Documents, could not avert his downfall through extensive corruption; Zhang Yu, despite being the emperor's teacher, did not restrain the power of the imperial consorts' relatives. Were these men sagely in speech but sinister within [?]? Zheng Jiajī said: “The men of Qin burned the books, yet the books survived; the scholars of Han exhaustively studied the Classics, yet the Classics were extinguished.” Could he have meant only the errors in their scholarship? Thus Han had no Classics. Tang prized literary compositions and rhapsodies and was far removed from the Classics. With the purity and correctness of Song scholars' learning, the Five Classics enjoyed a revival, and their interpretations remain authoritative today. Yet a saying runs: “Sweet wine owes its excellence to the clear water with which it is brewed; patterned silk owes its beauty to the plain threads from which it is woven.” This values their beginnings. Had Han scholars not first gathered up the Six Classics, what could Song scholars, a thousand years later, have consulted in their investigations? In this respect, Han scholars should not be censured too severely. What matters is that those who study the Classics exhaustively understand what makes their meaning clear or obscure.

If scholars can truly follow the openings disclosed by Song scholars to trace the threads of the Five Classics; use the images expressed in the Five Classics to apprehend the unspoken truth of the many sages; and then turn back to their own hearts to seek the foundation, embodying it in personal conduct to test what they have actually attained—then their learning will bear fruit. Thus, when abhorring the monopolization of power by treacherous men, they must discern the first signs of good and ill fortune; when correcting a regional prince's faults, they must not engage in political maneuvering. Having remonstrated against excursions, they must put the Book of Documents into practice in bringing their ruler to perfection; having presented models and warnings, they must use the Book of Odes to remedy omissions; having supplied glosses and explanations, they must not alter their words when consulted by the ruler. Then their advancing and withdrawing, speaking and remaining silent, will all embody the Classics. Would this not help illuminate the Five Classics? Therefore…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
日窮經以道會道以心吾心有時中公正
和敬之道而易詩書禮樂春秋之原渾如
也所以管轄百家筌蹄六籍上下乎千百
載之間而無古今者特有此心焉耳否則
約焉則翦叏經傳博焉則決裂義理未見
其少得於巳措間也故曰學不窮經則妄
經不求心則浮惟執事進而教之
第三問
王見賓
===
同考試官教諭馮　批〔心術學術相須爲用而心爲本是篇揭擢所　以辨析精微求復以盡心致聖人者尤爲喫緊此必心𨻶純不詭流俗者他日立〕
朝功業可豫占矣主司者不勝慶賴焉
考試官敎諭佘　批〔心學大明場中類能言之而直行素履自　待以古人誠不多得有士如此咸當退讓三舍矣高鳶何忝〕
考試官教授李　批〔剖析心學幾微精詳想必刻而識見卓絶遠　詞高古佳士佳士〕
萬化原於心也君子純其心而大本斯立
萬理會於學也君子正其學而大用斯弘
punctuated:
日：窮經以道，會道以心。吾心有時中、公正、和敬之道，而易、詩、書、禮、樂、春秋之原渾如也。所以管轄百家，筌蹄六籍，上下乎千百載之間而無古今者，特有此心焉耳。否則，約焉則翦叏經傳，博焉則決裂義理，未見其少得於巳措間也。故曰：學不窮經則妄，經不求心則浮。惟執事進而教之。
第三問
王見賓
同考試官教諭馮，批〔心術、學術相須爲用，而心爲本。是篇揭擢所，以辨析精微，求復以盡心致聖人者，尤爲喫緊。此必心𨻶純、不詭流俗者，他日立〕朝，功業可豫占矣。主司者不勝慶賴焉。
考試官敎諭佘，批〔心學大明，場中類能言之，而直行素履、自待以古人，誠不多得。有士如此，咸當退讓三舍矣。高鳶何忝？〕
考試官教授李，批〔剖析心學幾微精詳，想必刻，而識見卓絶遠，詞高古。佳士！佳士！〕
萬化原於心也，君子純其心而大本斯立；萬理會於學也，君子正其學而大用斯弘。
translation_en:
…It is said: Investigate the classics through the Way, and comprehend the Way through the heart-mind. Our heart-minds possess the Way of timely equilibrium, impartial rectitude, harmony, and reverence; the sources of the Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites, Music, and Spring and Autumn Annals are united within it. What enables one to encompass the hundred schools, use the Six Classics as instruments for apprehending meaning, and range through hundreds and thousands of years without distinguishing ancient from modern is simply this heart-mind. Otherwise, seeking concision leads to cutting up the classics and their commentaries [?], while seeking breadth leads to sundering their principles. I have yet to see even a little gained in putting them into practice [?]. Thus it is said: Learning that does not thoroughly investigate the classics is misguided; studying the classics without seeking the heart-mind is superficial. I respectfully ask you, sir, to offer further instruction.
Third Policy Question
Wang Jianbin
Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔The cultivation of the heart-mind and scholarly learning depend upon one another in their operation, but the heart-mind is fundamental. This essay brings this out [?], distinguishing subtle points with precision. Its pursuit of a return to the original heart-mind, so as to develop it fully and attain sagehood, is especially urgent and pertinent. This must be someone whose heart-mind is pure [?] and who does not conform deceitfully to prevailing fashions. When he takes his place〕 at court in days to come, his achievements can already be foretold. Those presiding over the examination cannot contain their joy and confidence in him.
Examiner She, Instructor, comments: 〔Learning of the heart-mind has been greatly elucidated, and most candidates here can speak of it. Yet upright conduct, an unassuming course of life, and holding oneself to the standards of the ancients are truly uncommon. Before a scholar such as this, all ought to retreat three stages in deference. How could he disgrace the lofty kite [?]?〕
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔His analysis of the subtleties of learning of the heart-mind is precise and detailed. His thought is surely penetrating [?], and his insight exceptionally far-reaching. His language is elevated and antique. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕
The myriad transformations originate in the heart-mind: the gentleman purifies his heart-mind, and thereby the great foundation is established. The myriad principles converge in learning: the gentleman rectifies his learning, and thereby its great application is expanded.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
夫心者學之本也天下固未有心術不純
而可以語學術之正者也學者心之著也
天下亦未有學術之正而不本於心術之
純者也古之人惟其立心也至一而不二
可以質鬼神盟天地而純乎無所於雜故
其爲學也務實而無僞可以植世教淑人
心而粹然一出於正窮則以道自守而不
爲枉尺直尋之謀達則以道致君而必成
光明俊偉之業此固心術與學術相符而
===
全體與大用交暢德則爲君子之盛德業
則爲君子之大業寧非世道之攸賴耶且
夫心術學術之辨何昉也書曰惟聖罔念
作狂惟狂克念作聖夫聖狂遠矣罔念則
聖可爲狂克念則狂可爲聖卽所謂一則
純二則雜也而心術不辨於此乎孔子語
子夏曰汝爲君子儒無爲小人儒夫君子
小人遠矣爲巳則爲君子爲人則爲小人
卽所謂誠則正僞則邪也而學術不辨於
punctuated:
夫心者，學之本也。天下固未有心術不純而可以語學術之正者也。學者，心之著也。天下亦未有學術之正而不本於心術之純者也。古之人惟其立心也至一而不二，可以質鬼神、盟天地，而純乎無所於雜，故其爲學也務實而無僞，可以植世教、淑人心，而粹然一出於正。窮則以道自守，而不爲枉尺直尋之謀；達則以道致君，而必成光明俊偉之業。此固心術與學術相符，而全體與大用交暢，德則爲君子之盛德，業則爲君子之大業，寧非世道之攸賴耶？
且夫心術、學術之辨何昉也？《書》曰：「惟聖罔念作狂，惟狂克念作聖。」夫聖狂遠矣，罔念則聖可爲狂，克念則狂可爲聖，卽所謂一則純、二則雜也，而心術不辨於此乎？孔子語子夏曰：「汝爲君子儒，無爲小人儒。」夫君子、小人遠矣，爲巳則爲君子，爲人則爲小人，卽所謂誠則正、僞則邪也，而學術不辨於
translation_en:
The mind is the foundation of learning. There has surely never been anyone whose disposition of mind was impure yet whose approach to learning could be called correct. Learning is the manifestation of the mind. Nor has there ever been a correct approach to learning that was not rooted in purity of mind. The ancients established their minds in perfect unity, without division: they could submit themselves to the judgment of spirits and pledge themselves before Heaven and Earth, remaining pure and free of admixture. Thus, in learning they pursued substance without falsity; they could uphold moral teaching in the world and improve people’s hearts, proceeding wholly from what was correct. In obscurity, they guarded themselves through the Way and would not scheme to bend a foot in order to straighten eight feet—to compromise their principles for greater gain. In prominence, they guided their ruler through the Way and invariably accomplished illustrious and outstanding deeds. Here, indeed, the disposition of mind and the approach to learning accorded with one another, while the complete substance and its great functioning flowed freely together. Their virtue was the flourishing virtue of the gentleman; their achievements were the great achievements of the gentleman. Was this not what the moral order of the world depended upon?
Now, where does the distinction concerning the disposition of mind and the approach to learning originate? The Book of Documents says: “A sage who fails to reflect becomes a madman; a madman who can reflect becomes a sage.” Sage and madman are far apart indeed. Yet without reflection, a sage can become a madman; with reflection, a madman can become a sage. This is precisely what is meant by unity bringing purity and division bringing admixture. Is not the distinction concerning the disposition of mind made clear here? Confucius told Zixia: “Be a gentlemanly scholar, not a petty scholar.” Gentleman and petty man are far apart indeed. Learning for oneself makes one a gentleman; learning for the regard of others makes one a petty man. This is precisely what is meant by sincerity bringing correctness and falsity bringing deviation. And is not the distinction concerning the approach to learning made clear in …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
此乎然孟子謂鄉愿自是之心卽不可與
入堯舜之道程伯子謂多識爲玩物喪志
卽爲已爲人之分是心術之純雜學術之
邪正其幾亦甚微矣故不必拂禮背義出
檻紆籌者而後爲心術之疵凡懷一念之
私不可對人言不可與天知者皆罔念也
皆狂之類也不必離經畔道歸楊附墨者
而後爲學術之僞凡投一時之好炫奇說
異飾貌文奸者皆爲人也皆小人之心也
===
謹其微而後心術可純充其類而後學術
可正審若是則心術學術果有二致乎哉
要之事心卽所以爲學而心術又學術之
本也心術純則學術自正不能純其心術
而謂學術之能正者否也不能正其學術
而謂心術之獨純者亦否也求之於古純
其心以爲學者伊傅周呂其選也自今觀
之阿衡左右之績隆矣而樂道必嚴於一
介舟楫鹽梅之烈盛矣而啓沃惟本於一
punctuated: 此乎？然孟子謂鄉愿自是之心，卽不可與入堯舜之道；程伯子謂多識爲玩物喪志，卽爲已爲人之分。是心術之純雜、學術之邪正，其幾亦甚微矣。故不必拂禮背義、出檻紆籌者，而後爲心術之疵；凡懷一念之私，不可對人言、不可與天知者，皆罔念也，皆狂之類也。不必離經畔道、歸楊附墨者，而後爲學術之僞；凡投一時之好、炫奇說異、飾貌文奸者，皆爲人也，皆小人之心也。謹其微而後心術可純，充其類而後學術可正。審若是，則心術學術果有二致乎哉？要之，事心卽所以爲學，而心術又學術之本也。心術純則學術自正；不能純其心術而謂學術之能正者，否也；不能正其學術而謂心術之獨純者，亦否也。求之於古，純其心以爲學者，伊傅周呂其選也。自今觀之，阿衡左右之績隆矣，而樂道必嚴於一介；舟楫鹽梅之烈盛矣，而啓沃惟本於一
translation_en:
…in this, too? Yet Mengzi said that village worthies, with their self-satisfied minds, cannot be brought into the Way of Yao and Shun. Master Cheng the Elder said that extensive knowledge could amount to toying with things and losing one’s resolve: here lies the distinction between learning for oneself and learning for others’ approval. Thus the incipient distinctions between purity and admixture in the workings of the mind, and between deviation and correctness in learning, are exceedingly subtle.

Faults in the workings of the mind need not await conduct that violates ritual and turns its back on righteousness, goes beyond bounds, and devises tortuous schemes [?]. Any private, selfish thought that one cannot speak of to others or allow Heaven to know constitutes a failure of moral mindfulness and belongs to the category of folly. Nor need falsity in learning await a departure from the Classics and the Way, or allegiance to Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Catering to the tastes of the moment, flaunting strange ideas and propounding novelties, or embellishing outward appearances to disguise wickedness—all are done for others’ approval and all express the mind of the petty person.

Only by attending carefully to these subtle beginnings can the workings of the mind become pure; only by extending this discernment to all things of the same kind can learning become correct. If this is indeed so, can the workings of the mind and the practice of learning really lead in two different directions? In essence, tending the mind is precisely how one pursues learning, and the workings of the mind are the foundation of learning. When the workings of the mind are pure, learning naturally becomes correct. To claim that learning can be correct without purifying the workings of the mind is wrong; to claim that the workings of the mind alone can remain pure without correcting one’s learning is also wrong.

If we seek among the ancients those who purified their minds in pursuing learning, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Lü Shang are the foremost examples. Viewed from our own day, Yi Yin’s achievements in assisting his sovereign as A-heng were great; yet his delight in the Way required strictness even over the smallest thing he accepted or gave. Fu Yue’s accomplishments as his sovereign’s boat and oars, salt and plums were magnificent; yet his opening and enriching his sovereign’s mind rested solely upon a single…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
心爲渠王家其精誠足以動天地丹書入
告其訓戒足以炳古今伊傅周呂之心至
純而不雜也至誠而不欺也至正而無邪
也所謂無不可與天知無不可與人言者
也心術既純則學術事功皆出於正其所
以光益商周聲施後世者豈無自哉嗣是
而後心術與學術岐而爲二伊傅周呂之
業始不可復覩矣是故始終爲韓留侯所
以善藏其用也而孔明感激馳驅其出師
===
一表慷慨之節迄今可想心事青白希文
所以自任之重也而文山精忠貫日其正
氣一歌誦之凜然猶有生氣之四子者心
術可謂正矣然四皓之招疑於智誘而勢
劫劉璋之取疑於離經以用權君子猶有
遺憾焉若夫先憂後樂之志待時而動甘
荼如飴之操視死如歸非有得於學問之
功不能也又豈可以例論哉下帷發憤仲
舒可謂銳志經術矣而昌黎作原道以詆
punctuated:
心。爲渠王家，其精誠足以動天地；丹書入告，其訓戒足以炳古今。伊傅周呂之心，至純而不雜也，至誠而不欺也，至正而無邪也，所謂無不可與天知、無不可與人言者也。心術既純，則學術事功皆出於正。其所以光益商周、聲施後世者，豈無自哉？嗣是而後，心術與學術岐而爲二，伊傅周呂之業始不可復覩矣。
是故始終爲韓，留侯所以善藏其用也；而孔明感激馳驅，其《出師》一表，慷慨之節迄今可想。心事青白，希文所以自任之重也；而文山精忠貫日，其《正氣》一歌，誦之凜然猶有生氣。之四子者，心術可謂正矣。然四皓之招，疑於智誘而勢劫；劉璋之取，疑於離經以用權。君子猶有遺憾焉。若夫先憂後樂之志，待時而動；甘荼如飴之操，視死如歸：非有得於學問之功不能也，又豈可以例論哉？
下帷發憤，仲舒可謂銳志經術矣；而昌黎作《原道》以詆
translation_en:
…heart. In serving as a leader of the royal house [?], his utter sincerity was sufficient to move Heaven and Earth; in presenting the Cinnabar Writing to the ruler, his admonitions were sufficient to illuminate past and present. The hearts of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Lü Shang were utterly pure and unmixed, utterly sincere and without deception, utterly upright and without perversity. They exemplified what is meant by having nothing that Heaven could not be allowed to know and nothing that could not be told to others. Once the disposition of the heart is pure, learning and practical achievements alike issue from rectitude. Could their enhancement of the glory of Shang and Zhou, and the transmission of their renown to later generations, have been without a foundation? Thereafter, the cultivation of the heart and scholarly learning diverged into two separate paths, and achievements such as those of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Lü Shang could no longer be seen.
Thus, by remaining devoted to Han from beginning to end, the Marquis of Liu, Zhang Liang, showed his skill in concealing his capacities. Kongming, Zhuge Liang, for his part, exerted himself tirelessly out of gratitude: his single Memorial on Dispatching the Army still enables us to envision his generous and resolute integrity. Purity in the heart’s concerns was the basis of the weighty responsibilities Xiwen, Fan Zhongyan, assumed for himself. Wenshan, Wen Tianxiang, displayed a pure loyalty that pierced the sun: reciting his Song of Righteous Spirit still inspires awe, as though his living spirit remained. These four men may indeed be said to have possessed upright dispositions. Yet the recruitment of the Four Hoary Elders raises suspicions of enticement through cunning and coercion through superior influence; the seizure of Liu Zhang’s territory raises suspicions of departing from constant principles to employ expedient measures. The gentleman still finds grounds for regret in these matters. But as for the resolve to be first in anxiety and last in enjoyment, awaiting the proper time to act, and the integrity that takes bitter herbs as sweet malt and regards death as a homecoming—these are impossible without attainment through scholarly cultivation. How, then, could they be judged indiscriminately by the same standard?
Lowering his study curtains and applying himself with determination, Dong Zhongshu may be said to have devoted himself ardently to classical learning. And Changli, Han Yu, wrote An Inquiry into the Way to denounce…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
佛辭而闢之不遺餘力嗚道涑水溫公可
謂究心正學矣而歐陽氏力復古文挺軋
之體條焉釐革之四子者學術可謂偉矣
然蓋簡之答貽求售之羞濮安之議取誚
君之誚君子深有不滿焉若夫明道正誼
之論度越乎諸儒天若祚宋之言近於終
條理非有得於事心之功不能也又豈可
以並觀哉要之學有未正者必其心有弗
純而純心固正學之本也洪惟我
===
朝
列聖相承道化旁洽講學明道之士紀載於
皇明名臣錄與理學名臣錄者後先相望夫既
班班可考矣然求其以純心而崇之爲正
學者亦不多得章溢學主於誠而以廉恥
勵風俗黃福學根於正而以剛直激人心
立教不同要之皆有本之學也李時勉以
道淑諸人而封事屢上胡居仁衛道任諸
已而屋漏無愧出處不同要之皆經濟之
punctuated:
佛辭，而闢之不遺餘力。嗚道涑水溫公，可謂究心正學矣；而歐陽氏力復古文，挺軋之體，條焉釐革之。四子者，學術可謂偉矣。然蓋簡之答，貽求售之羞；濮安之議，取誚君之誚，君子深有不滿焉。若夫明道正誼之論，度越乎諸儒；天若祚宋之言，近於終條理，非有得於事心之功不能也，又豈可以並觀哉？要之，學有未正者，必其心有弗純，而純心固正學之本也。
洪惟我朝列聖相承，道化旁洽，講學明道之士，紀載於《皇明名臣錄》與《理學名臣錄》者，後先相望。夫既班班可考矣，然求其以純心而崇之爲正學者，亦不多得。章溢學主於誠，而以廉恥勵風俗；黃福學根於正，而以剛直激人心。立教不同，要之皆有本之學也。李時勉以道淑諸人，而封事屢上；胡居仁衛道任諸已，而屋漏無愧。出處不同，要之皆經濟之
translation_en:
…Buddhist teachings, sparing no effort in refuting them. Duke Wen of Sushui, Sima Guang, who proclaimed the Way [?], may be said to have devoted his mind to orthodox learning; and Ouyang Xiu strove to revive ancient-style prose, systematically reforming its contorted forms [?]. These four masters may be said to have been outstanding in their learning. Yet the reply to Gai Jian brought the shame of seeking to sell one’s services, while the deliberation concerning Pu’an [?] incurred criticism for censuring the ruler. Gentlemen find much in these matters deeply unsatisfactory. As for the argument for illuminating the Way and rectifying righteousness, it surpassed those of other Confucian scholars; and the words “If Heaven grants good fortune to the Song” came close to bringing the whole into its proper completion. Such achievements would have been impossible without gains from the work of tending the mind. How, then, could these men all be regarded alike? In essence, wherever learning is not yet correct, there must be some impurity in the mind; a pure mind is indeed the foundation of orthodox learning.
We reverently reflect that, in our dynasty, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, and the transforming influence of the Way has spread everywhere. Scholars who expounded learning and illuminated the Way, recorded in the Record of Eminent Ministers of the August Ming and the Record of Eminent Ministers of the Learning of Principle, have appeared in succession. Their achievements are clearly documented and open to examination. Yet those who, through purity of mind, elevated their learning into orthodox learning are not easily found. Zhang Yi grounded his learning in sincerity and used integrity and a sense of shame to improve prevailing customs. Huang Fu rooted his learning in rectitude and used firmness and uprightness to stir people’s hearts. Their ways of teaching differed, but both, in essence, possessed learning with a sound foundation. Li Shimian used the Way to make others better and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials. Hu Juren took responsibility for defending the Way upon himself and had nothing to be ashamed of even in the privacy of his own chamber. They differed in serving in office or remaining in retirement, but, in essence, both possessed learning for ordering the world and aiding its people…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
學也乃若可以爲師資之宗者非薛文清
其誰與歸踐履篤實抗志浩然威勢不怵
其心去就不違其義卓然以明道自期其
心庶乎不雜而其學庶乎粹然者矣玆又
非傑出於名臣之中而爲諸子之所揖讓
者乎愚竊慨夫理學未嘗不明於天下而
學者竊其名以自欺也記曰言從而行之
則言不可飾也行從而言之則行不可飾
也聖人之道貴實而賤飾蓋如此後世以
===
學術名者吾惑焉雍然非不著有道氣象
也剴然非不闡有道議論也軒然非不以
有道自高人亦非不以有道尊之信之也
然而見利則動遇勢則惕臨死生禍福之
際將有茫然喪其所守者斯亦奚取於學
術哉甚者詞襲老莊而言知性術用管商
而曰識治矯情鎮物而曰雅量倨傲鮮腆
而曰養高假恬退以階仕進事遲鈍以謀
速化示朴野之形以藏其機械之巧立孤
punctuated:
學也。乃若可以爲師資之宗者，非薛文清，其誰與歸？踐履篤實，抗志浩然，威勢不怵其心，去就不違其義，卓然以明道自期，其心庶乎不雜，而其學庶乎粹然者矣。玆又非傑出於名臣之中，而爲諸子之所揖讓者乎？
愚竊慨夫理學未嘗不明於天下，而學者竊其名以自欺也。《記》曰：「言從而行之，則言不可飾也；行從而言之，則行不可飾也。」聖人之道貴實而賤飾，蓋如此。後世以學術名者，吾惑焉。雍然非不著有道氣象也，剴然非不闡有道議論也，軒然非不以有道自高，人亦非不以有道尊之信之也。然而見利則動，遇勢則惕，臨死生禍福之際，將有茫然喪其所守者，斯亦奚取於學術哉？甚者，詞襲老莊而言知性，術用管商而曰識治，矯情鎮物而曰雅量，倨傲鮮腆而曰養高，假恬退以階仕進，事遲鈍以謀速化，示朴野之形以藏其機械之巧，立孤
translation_en:
…learning. As for someone who might serve as the foremost model for teachers and students, to whom could we turn but Xue Wenqing 薛文清? Earnest and steadfast in practice, lofty and expansive in resolve, he was not intimidated by power and authority, nor did his decisions to enter or withdraw from office violate righteousness. Standing firm, he set himself the task of illuminating the Way. His mind approached freedom from admixture, and his learning approached purity. Was he not outstanding even among eminent ministers, one before whom the other masters would respectfully yield precedence?
I humbly lament that learning concerning principle has never failed to shine forth in the world, yet students of it appropriate its name to deceive themselves. The Record of Rites says: “When words are followed by putting them into practice, words cannot be mere embellishment; when conduct is followed by speaking of it, conduct cannot be mere embellishment.” Such is the sages’ Way: it prizes substance and disdains embellishment. I am perplexed by those of later ages who win renown for their learning. With dignified composure, they certainly display the bearing of those who possess the Way; with incisive speech, they certainly expound arguments befitting those who possess the Way. With an air of superiority, they certainly exalt themselves as possessors of the Way, and others likewise honor and trust them as such. Yet the sight of profit stirs them, and encounters with power make them fearful. Confronted with life and death, calamity and good fortune, they may lose their bearings and abandon what they uphold. What value, then, is there in their learning? Worse still, they borrow the language of Laozi and Zhuangzi yet claim to understand human nature; employ the methods of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang yet claim to understand government; suppress their true feelings to overawe others yet call this magnanimity; behave arrogantly and with scant shame yet call this cultivating lofty character. They feign tranquil retirement to climb the ladder of official advancement, practice seeming slowness and dullness to seek rapid advancement [?], display a plain and rustic exterior to conceal their ingenious scheming, and cultivate a solitary…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
狷之行以濟其貪婪之欲倡公平之說以
行其攻訐之私崇詭激之節以肆其傾陷
之毒此又學術之大蠹而飾名者之滋其
弊也噫豈獨其學術之僞哉由心術之不
純也茲執事之所隱憂也然則欲正其學
術者宜何如先正其心而已孔子曰臣事
君以忠夫忠者無他純心之謂也無所爲
而爲者也故天下有借其事之公以濟其
心之私者是其心爲私也非純也忠臣苟
===
利社稷遑恤其私必絕其一念之私而後
謂之純心有成天下之事而欲享其名者
是其心爲名也非純也忠臣事專報主何
有於名必祛其徼名之念而後謂之純心
人君所可知所可見而盡瘁以圖之者是
其心爲君之知見也亦非純也忠臣誠一
不二何間隱顯必泯其爲知見之心而後
謂之純心心純則其學必正心雜則其學
必邪唯在上者早辨之耳寶鏡之於姸媸
punctuated: 狷之行，以濟其貪婪之欲；倡公平之說，以行其攻訐之私；崇詭激之節，以肆其傾陷之毒。此又學術之大蠹，而飾名者之滋其弊也。噫！豈獨其學術之僞哉？由心術之不純也。茲執事之所隱憂也。然則欲正其學術者，宜何如？先正其心而已。孔子曰：「臣事君以忠。」夫忠者無他，純心之謂也，無所爲而爲者也。故天下有借其事之公，以濟其心之私者，是其心爲私也，非純也。忠臣苟利社稷，遑恤其私？必絕其一念之私，而後謂之純心。有成天下之事而欲享其名者，是其心爲名也，非純也。忠臣事專報主，何有於名？必祛其徼名之念，而後謂之純心。人君所可知、所可見，而盡瘁以圖之者，是其心爲君之知見也，亦非純也。忠臣誠一不二，何間隱顯？必泯其爲知見之心，而後謂之純心。心純則其學必正，心雜則其學必邪，唯在上者早辨之耳。寶鏡之於姸媸
translation_en:
…conduct of rigid independence to satisfy their greedy desires; they advocate fairness to pursue their private ends through denunciation; and they exalt outlandish, extreme displays of integrity to give free rein to their malicious efforts to undermine and entrap others. These, too, are great pests of learning, and those who embellish their reputations aggravate its abuses. Alas! Is it merely that their learning is false? It stems from the impurity of their hearts and intentions. This is what privately troubles you, sir. What, then, should one do to rectify their learning? First rectify their hearts—that is all. Confucius said: “A minister serves his ruler with loyalty.” Loyalty is nothing other than purity of heart: acting without an ulterior purpose.

Thus, there are people who use the public character of their undertakings to serve the private interests in their hearts. Their hearts are set on private advantage and are not pure. If a loyal minister can benefit the altars of soil and grain, how could he spare a thought for his private interests? Only after eliminating every selfish thought can one be said to possess a pure heart. There are those who accomplish affairs of the realm but wish to enjoy the resulting renown. Their hearts are set on fame and are not pure. A loyal minister serves solely to repay his sovereign; what concern has he for fame? Only after dispelling the desire to seek fame can one be said to possess a pure heart. Those who exhaust themselves pursuing what the ruler can know and see have their hearts set on receiving his notice; they, too, are impure. A loyal minister is single-minded in his sincerity and never divided: what distinction does he make between what is hidden and what is manifest? Only after extinguishing the wish to be noticed can one be said to possess a pure heart.

When the heart is pure, one's learning must be correct; when the heart has mixed motives, one's learning must be perverse. It rests only with those above to distinguish between them early. As for a precious mirror in relation to beauty and ugliness…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
而一照莫逃非妍媸之莫逃也以寶鏡之
空自不能逃也離婁之於曲直而一視罔
遺非曲直之罔遺也以離婁之明自不能
遺也故考學術於心術則學術無疑考心
術於事爲則心術不爽愚故曰心者學之
本也唯於心而辨之則所用者皆純心正
學之君子而所建者皆光明俊偉之事功
由此以媲美伊傅周吕以共成三代盛治
無難也然則察心術以稽學術身世道者
可不加之意哉執事以爲何如
===
第四問
劉應球
同考試官教諭周　批〔營田水利二者皆東省急務子能指陳利弊若燭照數計蓍蔡可見諸實用矣於纂重得兗爲知要識時務之俊傑舍子其誰耶〕
考試官教諭余　批〔區畫墾田治水之方酌古宜時明如指掌是留心經濟者〕
考試官教授李　批〔時務民情處置明悉有用之文也〕
天下猶一家也司牧者貴有以體其情而
punctuated:
而一照莫逃，非妍媸之莫逃也，以寶鏡之空，自不能逃也。離婁之於曲直，而一視罔遺，非曲直之罔遺也，以離婁之明，自不能遺也。故考學術於心術，則學術無疑；考心術於事爲，則心術不爽。愚故曰：心者，學之本也。唯於心而辨之，則所用者皆純心正學之君子，而所建者皆光明俊偉之事功。由此以媲美伊傅周吕，以共成三代盛治，無難也。然則察心術以稽學術，身世道者可不加之意哉？執事以爲何如？

第四問
劉應球
同考試官教諭周　批〔營田水利二者皆東省急務，子能指陳利弊，若燭照數計，蓍蔡可見諸實用矣。於纂重得兗，爲知要識時務之俊傑，舍子其誰耶？〕
考試官教諭余　批〔區畫墾田治水之方，酌古宜時，明如指掌，是留心經濟者。〕
考試官教授李　批〔時務民情，處置明悉，有用之文也。〕

天下猶一家也，司牧者貴有以體其情而
translation_en:
…and nothing escapes a single reflection. This is not because beauty and ugliness cannot escape of themselves, but because the precious mirror’s emptiness leaves them no escape. When Li Lou looks at what is crooked or straight, nothing eludes a single glance. This is not because crookedness and straightness cannot elude him of themselves, but because his keen sight leaves nothing unobserved. Thus, examining a person’s learning through the disposition of his heart leaves no doubt about his learning; examining the disposition of his heart through his deeds leaves no error about that disposition. Hence I humbly say: the heart is the root of learning. If discrimination is made on the basis of the heart, those employed will all be gentlemen of pure hearts and orthodox learning, and their achievements will all be illustrious and outstanding. It will then be no difficult matter to rival Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Lü Shang, and together bring about the flourishing government of the Three Dynasties. Should not those who bear responsibility for the moral order of the age [?] give careful attention to examining the disposition of the heart in order to assess learning? What is your judgment, honored examiners?

Fourth Policy Question
Liu Yingqiu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Agricultural development and water conservancy are both urgent concerns in Shandong. You identify their benefits and drawbacks as clearly as illuminating them with a candle or calculating them numerically. Your divinatory insight can be put to practical use. The passage “於纂重得兗” is unclear [?]. As an outstanding man who understands essentials and recognizes the needs of the times, who could take your place?〕

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: 〔Your plans for reclaiming farmland and controlling water weigh ancient precedents and suit present circumstances; they are as clear as the palm of one’s hand. Here is someone who attends closely to statecraft.〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: 〔Your treatment of current affairs and the people’s circumstances is clear and informed. This is an essay of practical use.〕

All under Heaven is like a single household. Those charged with shepherding the people should above all be able to understand their circumstances and…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
達天下之政天下猶一身也治農者貴有
以審其勢而成天下之能蓋吾之民其子
也而牧其慈母也無知之子能舍慈母而
他依哉亦惟于情焉體之而已矣水之流
其氣也而源其喉咽也不息之氣能舍喉
咽而他出哉亦惟于勢焉審之而已矣今
民之利不興而水之害不已是視天下之
民未必若家而視天下之水未能若身也
執事以營田水利爲問噫此誠切慈母之
===
懷而惻喉咽之患者乎愚嘗博觀古今之
故錯綜利弊之原而知其萬一矣且屯田
以兵吾嘗聞其說矣而營田之制何昉乎
蓋主于撫不耕之民而墾不毛之地者也
漢唐屯營之參制而兵民絡繹焉自塞下
之募先零坐困河中之倡衆庶勸耕善于
經裕者充國于儀其選矣其間寓滑水而
民安增佃許准而資富强襄陽十年之儲
度支十萬之省代亦享其利也而夷考其
punctuated:
達天下之政。天下猶一身也，治農者貴有以審其勢而成天下之能。蓋吾之民，其子也，而牧其慈母也。無知之子能舍慈母而他依哉？亦惟于情焉體之而已矣。水之流，其氣也，而源其喉咽也。不息之氣能舍喉咽而他出哉？亦惟于勢焉審之而已矣。今民之利不興，而水之害不已，是視天下之民未必若家，而視天下之水未能若身也。執事以營田水利爲問，噫！此誠切慈母之懷而惻喉咽之患者乎！愚嘗博觀古今之故，錯綜利弊之原，而知其萬一矣。
且屯田以兵，吾嘗聞其說矣，而營田之制何昉乎？蓋主于撫不耕之民，而墾不毛之地者也。漢唐屯營之參制，而兵民絡繹焉。自塞下之募，先零坐困；河中之倡，衆庶勸耕。善于經裕者，充國、于儀，其選矣。其間寓滑水而民安，增佃許准而資富，强襄陽十年之儲，度支十萬之省，代亦享其利也。而夷考其
translation_en:
…and carry through the governance of All-under-Heaven. All-under-Heaven is also like a single body: those who administer agriculture must carefully assess its circumstances and thereby realize its productive capacities. Our people are its children, and their governor is their loving mother. Can an unknowing child abandon its loving mother and depend on someone else? One need only understand their feelings sympathetically. Flowing water is its vital breath, and the source is its throat. Can the ceaseless vital breath leave by some other route, abandoning the throat? One need only examine its configuration carefully. Now benefits for the people remain undeveloped, while the damage caused by water never ceases. This means that the people of All-under-Heaven are not truly regarded as a family, nor its waters as a body. You, sir, have asked about agricultural settlements and water management. Ah! Does this not indeed touch the loving mother’s heart and stir concern over an affliction of the throat? I have studied events past and present extensively and considered the interwoven causes of benefits and harms, and have gained some slight understanding of them.
As for establishing agricultural colonies with soldiers, I have heard the explanations; but where did the system of agricultural settlements originate? Its principal purpose was to provide for people who did not farm and to reclaim uncultivated land. Under the Han and Tang, military colonies and agricultural settlements were administered in combination, with soldiers and civilians participating in succession. Recruitment along the frontier left the Xianling in distress without battle; the initiative in Hezhong encouraged the populace to cultivate the land. Among those skilled at planning for abundance, Chongguo and Yu Yi [?] were outstanding. There were also settlements at Huashui [?] that brought peace to the people, and increased tenant cultivation at Xu and Zhun [?] that enriched resources; Xiangyang was strengthened by reserves sufficient for ten years, and the state finances saved a hundred thousand [?]. Successive ages also enjoyed these benefits. Yet, examining its …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
宋之剏於唐鄧襄之州置屯務以司其營
於河北東西之路置營使以督其屯度地
勢辨方宜驅游民以闢曠土不踰時而地
有餘利民有餘粟焉陳恕承矩之議有不
可採而用之乎漕河以運亦嘗聞其槩矣
而水利之制何始乎蓋主於酌瀦洩之時
而資田疇之利者也大禹疏鑿之成功遺
蹟可稽焉自朕□之穿而繁田獲潤滑渠
之灌而關內稱收善于開濟者文翁鄭當
===
時其最矣厥後鑿六輔於高田導涇水於
陽堰疏雷坡而源以畜引黃河而地以滋
世亦需其□地而追考于宋之時許氏之
修堰踵相國之規趙氏之築堤輯信臣之
址芟蘆葦變沮洳時耕作以成膏腴迄于
今而民不改聚地不改闢焉景山尚寛之
法有不可倣而行之乎夫井牧廢而先王
兵寓于農之意荒矣此家給人足之風不
可望於今日也阡陌開而先王經界溝洫
punctuated: 宋之剏於唐、鄧、襄之州，置屯務以司其營，於河北東西之路，置營使以督其屯，度地勢，辨方宜，驅游民以闢曠土，不踰時而地有餘利，民有餘粟焉。陳恕、承矩之議，有不可採而用之乎？漕河以運，亦嘗聞其槩矣。而水利之制何始乎？蓋主於酌瀦洩之時，而資田疇之利者也。大禹疏鑿之成功，遺蹟可稽焉。自朕□之穿而繁田獲潤，滑渠之灌而關內稱收，善于開濟者，文翁、鄭當時其最矣。厥後鑿六輔於高田，導涇水於陽堰，疏雷坡而源以畜，引黃河而地以滋，世亦需其□地。而追考于宋之時，許氏之修堰，踵相國之規；趙氏之築堤，輯信臣之址。芟蘆葦，變沮洳，時耕作以成膏腴，迄于今而民不改聚，地不改闢焉。景山、尚寛之法，有不可倣而行之乎？夫井牧廢而先王兵寓于農之意荒矣，此家給人足之風不可望於今日也。阡陌開而先王經界溝洫
translation_en:
…under the Song, agricultural colonies were established in the prefectures of Tang, Deng, and Xiang, with colony offices to administer their cultivation. In the eastern and western circuits of Hebei, commissioners for agricultural colonies were appointed to supervise them. They surveyed the terrain, determined what suited each locality, and directed people without settled occupations to reclaim vacant land. Before long, the land yielded a surplus and the people had grain to spare. Could the proposals of Chen Shu and Chengju not be adopted and put to use?

I have also heard the broad outlines of using the grain-transport canals for shipping. But where did the system of water management begin? Its principal purpose was to judge the proper times for storing and releasing water, thereby benefiting the fields. The surviving traces of the Great Yu’s successful dredging and excavation can still be examined. With the excavation of Zhen □ [?], the fields of Fan received water; with irrigation from the Hua Canal [?], the region within the passes was said to enjoy good harvests. Among those skilled in opening waterways to benefit the people, Wen Weng and Zheng Dangshi were foremost. Later, the Six Auxiliary Canals were excavated to serve elevated fields, the waters of the Jing were led to the Yang Weir, Leipo [?] was dredged so that its waters could be stored, and the Yellow River was diverted to irrigate the land. Successive generations also depended on these □ lands [?].

Looking back to Song times, Master Xu repaired weirs, following the plans of the Chief Minister; Master Zhao built embankments, restoring the remains of Xinchen’s works. They cleared reeds, transformed marshland, and cultivated it in season to make fertile fields. Down to the present, people have continued to settle there and the land has remained under cultivation. Could the methods of Jingshan and Shangkuan not be emulated and put into practice?

Now that the well-field and pastoral divisions have been abolished, the former kings’ intention of incorporating soldiers within the farming population has fallen into neglect. Thus, we cannot hope today for a state in which every household has sufficient supplies and every person has enough. With the opening of paths and boundaries between fields, the former kings’ regulations for land boundaries and irrigation ditches…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之規壞矣此旱乾水溢之患不能免於今
日也時殊政易三代之所以善治者既非
後世之所能因而與時變通漢唐宋之可
以宜民者要在今日之所必講也今山東
以營政言之土多磽瘠地當上衝賦役百
出于閭閻供應多方于孔道公家告匱切
剪爪及膚之艱民罄夂懸率捉襟露肘之
態矧不登屢歲待哺空嗷宿課未償而新
輸繼集使羸稚轉於溝壑妻孥携于道路
===
幸偷一日之生奚懷故土稍免目前之急
寧畏重遷邪斯時也得其人以區處之投
其所至願不强其所不堪一招徠之下而
民之渙者萃矣執事乃曰司牧者其秦越
之心乎噫民罔常懷懷於有仁使牧而不
為之所也是猶惡漏卮者而不思所以塞
其隙焉耳烏乎可哉以水道言之會通受
派于黄河支流合泉于汶泗遥滂夂而魚
臺曹單之防必潰衛河漲而館陶清源之
punctuated:
之規壞矣，此旱乾水溢之患不能免於今日也。時殊政易，三代之所以善治者，既非後世之所能因，而與時變通，漢唐宋之可以宜民者，要在今日之所必講也。

今山東，以營政言之，土多磽瘠，地當上衝，賦役百出于閭閻，供應多方于孔道。公家告匱，切剪爪及膚之艱；民罄夂懸，率捉襟露肘之態。矧不登屢歲，待哺空嗷，宿課未償，而新輸繼集，使羸稚轉於溝壑，妻孥携于道路。幸偷一日之生，奚懷故土？稍免目前之急，寧畏重遷邪？斯時也，得其人以區處之，投其所至願，不强其所不堪，一招徠之下，而民之渙者萃矣。執事乃曰：「司牧者其秦越之心乎？」噫！民罔常懷，懷於有仁。使牧而不為之所也，是猶惡漏卮者，而不思所以塞其隙焉耳，烏乎可哉？

以水道言之，會通受派于黄河，支流合泉于汶泗，遥滂夂而魚臺曹單之防必潰，衛河漲而館陶清源之
translation_en:
…the arrangements have been ruined; hence the calamities of drought and flooding cannot be avoided today. Times differ and policies change. The means by which the Three Dynasties governed well cannot simply be carried on by later ages. Yet adapting to changing times and examining those measures of the Han, Tang, and Song that could benefit the people are essential tasks today.

As for administrative affairs in Shandong today, much of the soil is stony and infertile, and the region lies on major thoroughfares [?]. Taxes and labor services descend upon village households in a hundred forms, while demands for supplies along the main routes are manifold. Public resources are reported exhausted: the distress is as acute as clipping nails into the flesh. The people’s resources are depleted, and their distress persists [?]; everywhere they resemble someone whose elbows are exposed when he pulls his lapels together. Moreover, harvests have failed for successive years. Those awaiting food cry out in vain. Old tax obligations remain unpaid, while new demands for payment arrive in succession, leaving the weak and young to perish in ditches and ravines, and wives and children to be led along the roads. Hoping merely to eke out another day of life, how could they cherish their native soil? If they could gain some relief from their immediate distress, would they shrink from the hardship of moving? At such a time, if suitable men were found to make arrangements for them, meeting their deepest wishes without forcing upon them what they could not bear, a single summons to return and settle would gather the scattered people together. Yet you say: “Can those who shepherd the people have hearts as estranged as Qin and Yue?” Alas! The people have no constant object of attachment; they attach themselves to those who possess benevolence. To shepherd them without providing them a place is like disliking a leaking cup without considering how to plug its cracks. How could this be acceptable?

As for the waterways, the Huitong Canal receives a branch of the Yellow River, and its tributaries join the springs of the Wen and Si rivers. When prolonged flooding occurs [?], the embankments at Yutai, Cao, and Shan inevitably collapse; when the Wei River rises, Guantao and Qingyuan’s…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
害孔殷環二郡千里之間戍奔突四出之
勢且大清之入海肇平陰而會諸淯小清
之入海自趵突而沿諸漯特其河流久塞
故道悉湮決鄒長清漸之泊漫浮苑博匯
麻姑諸水之衝漸圮齊城斯時也得其人
而疏築之防其所害而導其所歸一經畫
之間而水之危者安矣執事乃曰司農者
其鄰壑之謀乎噫善治水者不與水爭利
使水而坐觀其變也是猶欲止沸者而不
===
知所以去其薪焉耳奚可得哉雖然循胥
胥之簿書而不切百姓之痌瘝者於治奚
補是不仁而不可爲也校瑣瑣之尋尺而
不慮百年之遠大者於害奚除是不智而
不可爲也明問所及而豈徒哉昔三晉磽
鹵有耕之人鮮其地關中饒廣有耕之地
鮮其人秦誘三晉之人利其力而俾世復
焉卒之富强甲于天下不可謂均民無術
也今平原廣隰亘千餘里皆齊曾舊封卑
punctuated:
害孔殷，環二郡千里之間，戍奔突四出之勢。且大清之入海，肇平陰而會諸淯；小清之入海，自趵突而沿諸漯。特其河流久塞，故道悉湮，決鄒長清漸之泊，漫浮苑博，匯麻姑諸水之衝，漸圮齊城。斯時也，得其人而疏築之，防其所害而導其所歸，一經畫之間，而水之危者安矣。執事乃曰：「司農者，其鄰壑之謀乎？」噫！善治水者，不與水爭利。使水而坐觀其變也，是猶欲止沸者而不知所以去其薪焉耳，奚可得哉？
雖然，循胥胥之簿書而不切百姓之痌瘝者，於治奚補？是不仁而不可爲也。校瑣瑣之尋尺而不慮百年之遠大者，於害奚除？是不智而不可爲也。明問所及，而豈徒哉？昔三晉磽鹵，有耕之人，鮮其地；關中饒廣，有耕之地，鮮其人。秦誘三晉之人，利其力而俾世復焉，卒之富强甲于天下，不可謂均民無術也。今平原廣隰，亘千餘里，皆齊曾舊封，卑
translation_en:
…the damage is exceedingly grave. Throughout the thousand li surrounding the two prefectures, the waters rush violently outward in every direction [?]. Moreover, the Daqing River’s course to the sea begins at Pingyin and joins the Yu [?]; the Xiaoqing River’s course to the sea begins at Baotu Spring and follows the Luo. But their channels have long been blocked, and their former courses entirely silted up. They breach at Zou and Changqing and inundate the lakes [?], spread across Yuan and Bo [?], converge with the rushing waters of Magu and other streams, and gradually undermine the walls of Qi. At such a time, if suitable men were obtained to dredge channels and build embankments, preventing the waters from causing harm and guiding them toward their proper destination, a single concerted undertaking would turn dangerous waters into safe ones. Yet you ask: “Are those responsible for agriculture planning to make their neighbors’ land a drainage ditch?” Alas! Those skilled in controlling water do not contend with it for advantage. To sit and watch as the waters change is like wishing to stop a pot from boiling without knowing to remove its firewood. How could that succeed?
Nevertheless, what contribution to government is made by those who merely follow clerks’ registers and documents [?], without taking the people’s suffering to heart? Such conduct is inhumane and must not be practiced. What harm is removed by those who quibble over petty measurements in fathoms and feet, without considering the far-reaching interests of a hundred years? Such conduct is unwise and must not be practiced. Surely the matters raised in your discerning question are no idle concerns! Formerly, the lands of the Three Jin were barren and saline: there were people to cultivate them, but little cultivable land. Guanzhong was fertile and extensive: there was land to cultivate, but few people. Qin attracted people from the Three Jin, benefited from their labor, and granted them hereditary exemption from taxes and service. In the end, its wealth and strength ranked first under Heaven. One cannot say that there are no methods for distributing the population more evenly. Today, level plains and broad lowlands extend for over a thousand li, all within the former domains of Qi and Zeng [?], low-lying [?]…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
稱雄覇者而乃蕭條極目一望成墟遷徙
無恒流離殆盡得非司牧者所當加之意
乎蓋不必別立一規制也以愛民之實心
行撫民之實政通古今之變求民俗之同
相可耕之地而制畝焉量能耕之人而均
力焉給所耕之器而備資焉豫宜耕之時
而瀦洩焉俯仰有賴恤其私也徭役有貸
裕其本也惰勤有令作其氣也豪譎有懲
屏其蠧也又必聯繹於保甲而固結之志
===
堅視成於三年而高下之額定漸征於五
年而生息之道蕃凡可以體其情者罔不
至矣如是則恒產以植恒心自存三年耕
必有一年之食也九年耕必有三年之食
也胥將愛戴之如慈母而寧忍于去之者
乎監司者於此而需其久任課其殿最焉
無田不稅無農不耕內以實壯勇於什伍
之外而神氣益振外以實儲積于常數之
餘而元氣益充雖趙郭之經裕不是過也
punctuated: 稱雄覇者，而乃蕭條極目，一望成墟，遷徙無恒，流離殆盡，得非司牧者所當加之意乎？蓋不必別立一規制也。以愛民之實心，行撫民之實政，通古今之變，求民俗之同。相可耕之地而制畝焉，量能耕之人而均力焉，給所耕之器而備資焉，豫宜耕之時而瀦洩焉。俯仰有賴，恤其私也；徭役有貸，裕其本也；惰勤有令，作其氣也；豪譎有懲，屏其蠧也。又必聯繹於保甲而固結之志堅，視成於三年而高下之額定，漸征於五年而生息之道蕃。凡可以體其情者，罔不至矣。如是則恒產以植，恒心自存。三年耕，必有一年之食也；九年耕，必有三年之食也。胥將愛戴之如慈母，而寧忍于去之者乎？監司者於此而需其久任，課其殿最焉。無田不稅，無農不耕，內以實壯勇於什伍之外而神氣益振，外以實儲積于常數之餘而元氣益充。雖趙郭之經裕，不是過也。
translation_en:
…which once claimed supremacy, yet now desolation stretches as far as the eye can see, and all is ruin at a glance. People move from place to place without permanence; almost all have scattered and become displaced. Surely this demands particular attention from those charged with shepherding the people?

There is no need to establish an entirely new system. With a sincere heart that loves the people, carry out substantive measures to care for them; comprehend changing circumstances across past and present, and seek what popular customs have in common. Survey cultivable land and lay out its allotments; assess those capable of cultivating it and distribute the labor equitably; supply farming implements and provide the necessary resources; prepare for the proper farming seasons by storing and draining water. Give them the means to support parents and children, thus attending to their household needs; grant relief from labor service, thus strengthening the foundation of their livelihood; issue directives concerning indolence and diligence, thus stirring their spirit; punish the powerful and deceitful, thus removing those who prey upon them.

Moreover, link them together [?] through the baojia household organization, so that their resolve to remain united becomes firm. Assess results after three years, so that higher and lower quotas can be fixed; introduce taxation gradually over five years, so that the means of sustaining life and increasing prosperity may flourish. Leave nothing undone that accords with their circumstances. In this way, stable livelihoods will be established, and constancy of heart will naturally endure. Three years of cultivation will assuredly yield a year's food in reserve; nine years of cultivation will assuredly yield three years' food in reserve. All will cherish and honor their officials as loving mothers: how could they bear to leave them?

The surveillance officials should accordingly ensure that these local officials remain long in office and assess their performance as inferior or superior. No field will go untaxed, and no farmer will fail to cultivate. Internally, this will strengthen the supply of able-bodied, courageous men beyond those organized into units of ten and five, further invigorating morale; externally, it will fill reserves beyond their customary amounts, further replenishing the fundamental vitality of the realm. Even the administrative accomplishments of Zhao and Guo could not surpass this.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
豈特如陳恕家矩之議而已哉昔先儒謂
禹之治水只從低處下手下面之水旣殺
則上面之水必洩又謂禹不惜數百里之
地而疏之爲九河以殺其勢是卽所謂行
其所無事也今會通淸河遡源九曲皆神
禹平成疏鑿遺矩者而乃鯨波漲天墊溺
奚禦黿拆遍野焚膜曷援得毋治農者所
當豫其策乎蓋不必別有所謂輸運也因
其性之本下順其勢之必趨功求其必濟
===
利求其必興兗郡之屬會通之上流也黃
之怒濤震撼而非人力可遏若濰沮雷夏
之疏而漸殺其威焉可也濟東之屬會通
之下流也衛之湍溢迅發而非人謀可加
循故河枯河之址而盆捍其決焉可也小
淸之淤旣所當濬則全漯之水必不能容
也分其半而俾隄之高且固焉則孝婦岔
烏之諸河有所受而爲地中之行有所洩
而無旁潰之患矣齊東之城旣在必移雖
punctuated: 豈特如陳恕家矩之議而已哉！昔先儒謂：「禹之治水，只從低處下手，下面之水旣殺，則上面之水必洩。」又謂：「禹不惜數百里之地，而疏之爲九河，以殺其勢。」是卽所謂行其所無事也。今會通淸河，遡源九曲，皆神禹平成疏鑿遺矩者，而乃鯨波漲天，墊溺奚禦？黿拆遍野，焚膜曷援？得毋治農者所當豫其策乎？蓋不必別有所謂輸運也，因其性之本下，順其勢之必趨，功求其必濟，利求其必興。兗郡之屬，會通之上流也。黃之怒濤震撼，而非人力可遏，若濰沮雷夏之疏，而漸殺其威焉，可也。濟東之屬，會通之下流也。衛之湍溢迅發，而非人謀可加，循故河枯河之址，而盆捍其決焉，可也。小淸之淤，旣所當濬，則全漯之水必不能容也。分其半，而俾隄之高且固焉，則孝婦岔烏之諸河有所受而爲地中之行，有所洩而無旁潰之患矣。齊東之城旣在必移，雖
translation_en:
…Could this amount merely to something like Chen Shu’s proposal concerning household rules [?]? A Confucian scholar of former times said: “In controlling the waters, Yu began only at the lower places. Once the water below had diminished, the water above would necessarily drain away.” He also said: “Yu did not begrudge several hundred li of land, but opened channels through it to form the Nine Rivers, thereby diminishing the force of the waters.” This is precisely what is meant by proceeding without imposing artificial interference. Today, tracing the Huitong Canal and the Qing River upstream through their many bends, one finds everywhere the methods bequeathed by divine Yu’s dredging and excavation, through which he brought the land and waters into order. Yet enormous waves rise to the heavens: how can inundation and drowning be prevented? The fields everywhere are cracked [?]: how can those scorched by drought be rescued [?]? Surely those responsible for agriculture ought to prepare measures against these dangers? There need be no separate undertaking called “transport” [?]. Follow water’s inherent tendency to descend and accommodate the direction in which its force must carry it; ensure that the works succeed and that their benefits are realized.

The territories of Yanzhou lie upstream along the Huitong Canal. The furious waves of the Yellow River shake the land, and human strength cannot restrain them. It would be practicable to dredge channels, as with the Wei and Ju rivers and Leixia Marsh, gradually diminishing their force. The territories of Jidong lie downstream along the Huitong Canal. The Wei River’s turbulent overflow surges forth swiftly, beyond what human planning can master. It would be practicable to follow the courses of the old and dried-up rivers and contain breaches [?]. The silt in the Little Qing River certainly ought to be dredged, but the river could not accommodate the entire flow of the Ta River. Divide off half of that flow and make the embankments high and strong. Then the Xiaofu, Cha, and Wu rivers [?] would have channels to receive their waters and carry them within the earth, and outlets through which to discharge them, without the danger of their bursting out sideways. Since the town of Qidong must in any case be relocated, even though…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
分潩之水亦無所妨也導其流而俾溝之
深且廣焉則由柳塘陳愷而下直抵于大
清而無有滯隔會歸于大海而無有泛濫
矣夫明于支派而達自然之宜參于舊址
而察已然之故時于濬築而豫未然之防
凡可以審其勢者罔不周矣如是則旱澇
無虞居食胥賴
京師之襟帶無壅也省會之脉絡分明也誠
有如一氣之流通于喉咽而寧復有虞之
===
者乎監司者于此不計功于旦夕不撓議
于道旁廓永頼之洪猷闢無前之美利上
以奠千百年
國儲之計下以貽億兆姓生靈之休雖文鄭
之開濟不多讓也豈止于景山尚寛之法
而已哉嗟夫營田水利之法猶之朝饔而
夕餐也夏葛而冬裘也其誰不知利害之
重且切乎其誰不知利害之興且去乎而
慮後瞻前者徒掩目而竊嘆踵常襲故者
punctuated:
分潩之水，亦無所妨也。導其流而俾溝之深且廣焉，則由柳塘、陳愷而下，直抵于大清而無有滯隔，會歸于大海而無有泛濫矣。夫明于支派而達自然之宜，參于舊址而察已然之故，時于濬築而豫未然之防，凡可以審其勢者，罔不周矣。如是，則旱澇無虞，居食胥賴，京師之襟帶無壅也，省會之脉絡分明也，誠有如一氣之流通于喉咽，而寧復有虞之者乎？監司者于此，不計功于旦夕，不撓議于道旁，廓永頼之洪猷，闢無前之美利，上以奠千百年國儲之計，下以貽億兆姓生靈之休，雖文鄭之開濟，不多讓也，豈止于景山、尚寛之法而已哉！
嗟夫！營田水利之法，猶之朝饔而夕餐也，夏葛而冬裘也。其誰不知利害之重且切乎？其誰不知利害之興且去乎？而慮後瞻前者，徒掩目而竊嘆；踵常襲故者，
translation_en:
…diverting the waters of the Yi would likewise present no impediment. Guide its flow and make the channels deep and broad: then the water will descend through Liutang and Chenkai [?], reaching the Daqing directly without obstruction, and converge in the sea without overflowing.
