Understand the branching waterways and grasp what their natural configuration requires; consult the old courses and investigate the causes of past events; dredge and build embankments at the proper times, taking precautions against troubles yet to come. Leave nothing unexamined in assessing the configuration of the waters. In this way, there will be no anxiety over drought or flooding, and both habitation and sustenance will be secured. The waterways girding the capital will be unobstructed, and the arteries of the provincial capital will be clearly ordered. It will truly be like the free passage of breath through the throat: what further cause for anxiety could there be? In this undertaking, the surveillance commissioners must not reckon achievement by the day or allow roadside criticism to shake their deliberations. They should enlarge their grand plans for lasting security and create benefits without precedent, thereby securing the state's reserves for hundreds and thousands of years above, and bequeathing well-being to the countless common people below. Their achievements would scarcely yield even to the pioneering and sustaining accomplishments of Wen and Zheng [?]. How could they amount merely to the methods of Jingshan and Shangkuan [?]?
Alas! The methods of agricultural development and water management are like eating meals morning and evening, or wearing hemp in summer and furs in winter. Who does not know how weighty and urgent their benefits and harms are? Who does not know that benefits must be promoted and harms removed? Yet those who fret over what lies behind and peer anxiously ahead merely cover their eyes and sigh in private; those who follow established practice and cling to precedent…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
竟袖手而旁觀間有志之銳而武怵于通
方猶皷瑟而膠柱有任之勇而或泥于欲
速猶計程而裹糧此大學理財之章必歸
之用人良有以也使有當世之豪傑者在
焉小功勿圖也而澤及生民者則慨然爲
之近利勿謀也而功在萬世者則毅然任
之察上下之情達變通之勢以天地之利
生天地之民以
國家之財裕
===
國家之治叢文莊之議雖西北之牧苑坊監
莫非可墾之地也據單鍔之言雖東南之
淮徐震澤莫非要害之水也舉而行之謂
非
今日之要務哉此固明問所未及而愚生未敢
悉陳也倘與其進焉尚有調停綜理之術
又安長治之猷爲執事者獻也
第五問
謝思聰
punctuated:
竟袖手而旁觀。間有志之銳而武怵于通方，猶皷瑟而膠柱；有任之勇而或泥于欲速，猶計程而裹糧。此《大學》理財之章必歸之用人，良有以也。使有當世之豪傑者在焉，小功勿圖也，而澤及生民者則慨然爲之；近利勿謀也，而功在萬世者則毅然任之。察上下之情，達變通之勢，以天地之利生天地之民，以國家之財裕國家之治。叢文莊之議，雖西北之牧苑坊監，莫非可墾之地也；據單鍔之言，雖東南之淮徐震澤，莫非要害之水也。舉而行之，謂非今日之要務哉？此固明問所未及，而愚生未敢悉陳也。倘與其進焉，尚有調停綜理之術，又安長治之猷，爲執事者獻也。

第五問
謝思聰
translation_en:
…in the end stand by with folded arms. Occasionally there are men keen in purpose yet daunted by the need for adaptable methods [?], like someone who glues down the bridges of a zither before playing it; others courageously undertake responsibility but become fixated on quick results, like someone who measures the journey and packs provisions accordingly. There is good reason why the Great Learning’s discussion of managing wealth ultimately comes back to employing the right people. Were there outstanding men of our age engaged in this work, they would seek no petty achievements, but would generously undertake whatever benefited the people; they would pursue no immediate gains, but would resolutely assume responsibility for whatever brought benefits lasting ten thousand generations. They would examine the circumstances of those above and below, comprehend the opportunities for adaptation, use the bounty of Heaven and Earth to sustain the people of Heaven and Earth, and use the state’s wealth to enrich its governance.

Following Wen Zhuang’s proposal [?], even the pastures and horse-breeding establishments of the northwest are all land that could be brought under cultivation. According to Shan E, even the waterways of Huai and Xu and Lake Zhenze in the southeast are all waters of critical importance. Could putting these proposals into practice be said not to be an urgent task today? These matters indeed lie beyond your illuminating question, and I, an unlearned student, have not ventured to set them forth in full. Should I be permitted to develop them further, I still have methods of coordination and comprehensive management, and plans for security and lasting good government [?], to offer you, honored examiners.

Fifth Policy Question
Xie Sicong

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正劉　批〔條答荒政甚悉以經權立說雅虜碩畫且文勢起伏詞意曲折如江河順流波瀾不竭非淺學所能到宜錄之以傳不朽云〕
考試官教諭余　批〔推極民隱而預防拯救歷陳良法先憂之志溢于言表非凡士也〕
考試官教授李　批〔籌畫荒政剴切詳盡取之〕
善為國者有經世之大法有濟時之大權
何謂經務本節用豫立於未事之先使天
下晏然自裕其休者是已何謂權審機達
變推行於有事之日使天下帖然不知其
===
患者是已惟經定於豫則不必天下之無
患而恃吾有素定之猷權達於時則不必
其患之先弭而恃吾有濟艱之策以是圖
治裕如矣執事策士時務而以備荒下詢
誠經國遠慮也謹拾所聞以對夫天道能
鼓化以阜物不能使氣運之無愆王者能
奉天以利民不能使地產之恒足是故水
旱為災堯湯憂之而卒不能為民病者以
有荒政耳然昔人謂救荒無上策非謂荒
punctuated:
同考試官學正劉，批〔條答荒政甚悉，以經權立說，雅虜碩畫，且文勢起伏，詞意曲折，如江河順流，波瀾不竭，非淺學所能到，宜錄之以傳不朽云〕。
考試官教諭余，批〔推極民隱，而預防拯救，歷陳良法，先憂之志溢于言表，非凡士也〕。
考試官教授李，批〔籌畫荒政，剴切詳盡，取之〕。
善為國者，有經世之大法，有濟時之大權。何謂經？務本節用，豫立於未事之先，使天下晏然自裕其休者，是已。何謂權？審機達變，推行於有事之日，使天下帖然不知其患者，是已。惟經定於豫，則不必天下之無患，而恃吾有素定之猷；權達於時，則不必其患之先弭，而恃吾有濟艱之策。以是圖治，裕如矣。執事策士時務，而以備荒下詢，誠經國遠慮也。謹拾所聞以對。
夫天道能鼓化以阜物，不能使氣運之無愆；王者能奉天以利民，不能使地產之恒足。是故水旱為災，堯湯憂之，而卒不能為民病者，以有荒政耳。然昔人謂救荒無上策，非謂荒
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, a School Instructor, comments: 〔The itemized response treats famine administration very thoroughly. It develops its argument through constant principles and discretionary measures, offering substantial plans [the preceding wording 雅虜 is doubtful: ?]. Moreover, the prose rises and falls, its wording and ideas turn and unfold, like great rivers flowing onward with waves that never cease. This is beyond the attainment of shallow learning. It should be recorded and transmitted to posterity.〕
Examiner Yu, a County School Instructor, comments: 〔He probes the people's hidden sufferings to their depths and sets out, one by one, sound methods of prevention and relief. His resolve to take thought for troubles before others do overflows his words. He is no ordinary scholar.〕
Examiner Li, a Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔His planning for famine administration is pertinent, thorough, and exhaustive. Accept this answer.〕
Those skilled in governing a state possess both great enduring methods for ordering the world and great discretionary measures for meeting the needs of the times. What are enduring principles? They consist in attending to the foundations and restraining expenditure, making preparations before trouble arises, so that all under Heaven may peacefully enjoy increasing well-being. What are discretionary measures? They consist in assessing circumstances and responding to change, putting measures into practice when trouble arises, so that all under Heaven remain at ease, unaware of their afflictions. When enduring principles are established beforehand, we need not depend on the world being free of trouble: we can rely on plans long since settled. When discretionary measures are aptly applied to the times, we need not depend on troubles having been quelled in advance: we can rely on strategies for overcoming difficulties. With these means, the pursuit of good government has ample resources. You, honored examiners, test scholars on contemporary affairs and graciously inquire about preparations against famine. This indeed shows farsighted concern for governing the state. I respectfully gather what I have heard to offer a reply.
The Way of Heaven can impel transformation and make things abundant, but cannot ensure that the cycles of vital forces never go awry. A true king can serve Heaven and benefit the people, but cannot ensure that the earth's produce is always sufficient. Thus floods and droughts became disasters, causing Yao and Tang concern; yet in the end they could not afflict the people, simply because measures for famine administration were in place. However, when men of old said that famine relief offered no best strategy, they did not mean that famine…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
不可救也蓋以備荒爲上救荒則已後時
矣以周言之遺人掌邦之委積以待施惠
鄉里之委積以恤艱阨縣都之委積以待
凶荒所以備於未荒也廩人掌九穀之數
以歲之上下數邦用以論年之豐凶所以
慮其將荒也大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民
始於散利而終於除盜賊所以救於已荒
也濟天時之不常補地利之不足經權並
用有非後世所可及者由周而後臧文仲
===
有無相濟以備旱敬仲輕重相通以計國
耿壽昌之立常平李悝之作平糴戴胄之
建義倉長孫平朱元晦之建社倉此未荒
而先備也汲黯矯制發粟富弼以糜活民
盧坦平價宣歙畢仲游賑鄜糴州此適荒
而救之也蔡文忠之弛鹽禁韓魏公之蠲
租稅趙清獻之募入粟此既荒而救之也
書取有備爲政在人其以是夫
國家創制立法監於周禮天下郡縣有預備
punctuated:
不可救也，蓋以備荒爲上，救荒則已後時矣。以周言之，遺人掌邦之委積，以待施惠；鄉里之委積，以恤艱阨；縣都之委積，以待凶荒，所以備於未荒也。廩人掌九穀之數，以歲之上下數邦用，以論年之豐凶，所以慮其將荒也。大司徒以荒政十二聚萬民，始於散利而終於除盜賊，所以救於已荒也。濟天時之不常，補地利之不足，經權並用，有非後世所可及者。由周而後，臧文仲有無相濟以備旱，敬仲輕重相通以計國，耿壽昌之立常平，李悝之作平糴，戴胄之建義倉，長孫平、朱元晦之建社倉，此未荒而先備也。汲黯矯制發粟，富弼以糜活民，盧坦平價宣歙，畢仲游賑鄜糴州，此適荒而救之也。蔡文忠之弛鹽禁，韓魏公之蠲租稅，趙清獻之募入粟，此既荒而救之也。《書》取有備，爲政在人，其以是夫！

國家創制立法，監於《周禮》，天下郡縣有預備
translation_en:
…cannot be relieved. Rather, preparedness for famine is held to be best; once one must relieve a famine, the proper time has already passed. Taking the Zhou as an example, the Distributor managed the state's accumulated stores to provide beneficent assistance, the stores of townships and villages to relieve hardship, and those of districts and domains to meet crop failures and famine. These were means of preparing before famine arose. The Granary Director managed the quantities of the nine grains, calculating state expenditure according to the quality of the harvest and assessing whether the year was abundant or poor. These were means of anticipating an approaching famine. The Minister of Education brought the people together through twelve famine measures, beginning with distributing resources and ending with suppressing robbers and thieves. These were means of relieving famine once it had arisen. They countered irregularities in the seasons and made up for deficiencies in the land's yield, employing both established principles and measures adapted to circumstances. In some respects, later ages could not match them.

After the Zhou, Zang Wenzhong used the resources of those who had supplies to assist those who lacked them, preparing against drought; Jingzhong managed the state's economy by facilitating exchange between goods of differing values. Geng Shouchang established ever-normal granaries; Li Kui instituted equitable grain purchasing; Dai Zhou established charity granaries; and Zhangsun Ping and Zhu Yuanhui established community granaries. These were preparations made before famine occurred. Ji An issued grain on a falsely claimed imperial authorization; Fu Bi kept the people alive with gruel; Lu Tan stabilized prices in Xuan and She; and Bi Zhongyou provided relief in Fu and Di prefectures [?; the place-name transcription is doubtful]. These were measures to relieve famine as it struck. Cai Wenzhong relaxed the salt restrictions; Han, Duke of Wei, remitted taxes; and Zhao Qingxian solicited contributions of grain. These were measures to provide relief after famine had occurred. The Book of Documents prizes preparedness, and the conduct of government depends on the people entrusted with it. Surely this is why!

In establishing institutions and laws, our dynasty took the Rites of Zhou as its model. Throughout the realm, prefectures and counties have reserve…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
倉鄉有社倉是稟人遺人之制也蠲租有
詔賑貸有詔是散利薄征之制也規畫弘
大節目周詳陋漢唐宋於不足言矣夫何
邇來公私告匱甚為司計之憂往歲南徐
北冀齊魯河洛之間風雨繼災平原成浸
漂沒稼廬米珠薪桂閭閻赤子半為魚鱉
矣當事臣工連章奏請荷蒙
皇上鴻慈睿筭彰念元元特出
帑金遣使周行賑卹仍錫民田租有差於乎
===
雨露一灑枯槁回春厚澤深仁下蟠上際捫
腹之民洋洋然有生氣也大哉
皇謨其周禮荒政之十二乎入春徂夏喘息方
舒水旱繼作
畿輔齊魯之間告災之牒又繁矣復蹙
皇上惻然淵視惕然勤思
睿命煥頒
躬親祈禱布告天下臣工痛自省過於是
馨德昭升
punctuated: 倉，鄉有社倉，是稟人、遺人之制也。蠲租有詔，賑貸有詔，是散利薄征之制也。規畫弘大，節目周詳，陋漢唐宋於不足言矣。夫何邇來公私告匱，甚為司計之憂？往歲南徐、北冀、齊魯、河洛之間，風雨繼災，平原成浸，漂沒稼廬，米珠薪桂，閭閻赤子半為魚鱉矣。當事臣工連章奏請，荷蒙皇上鴻慈睿筭，彰念元元，特出帑金，遣使周行賑卹，仍錫民田租有差。於乎！雨露一灑，枯槁回春，厚澤深仁，下蟠上際，捫腹之民洋洋然有生氣也。大哉皇謨！其《周禮》荒政之十二乎！入春徂夏，喘息方舒，水旱繼作，畿輔、齊魯之間，告災之牒又繁矣，復蹙。皇上惻然淵視，惕然勤思，睿命煥頒，躬親祈禱，布告天下臣工，痛自省過。於是馨德昭升，
translation_en:
…granaries, while villages have community granaries: these embody the institutions of the linren, the granary officials, and the yiren, the relief officials. Edicts provide for tax remissions, and edicts provide for relief loans: these embody the institutions of distributing resources and lightening taxation. The planning is grand in scope, the provisions comprehensive and detailed, making the arrangements of the Han, Tang, and Song seem so meager as to be scarcely worth mentioning. Why, then, have public and private resources lately become exhausted, causing such concern to those responsible for financial administration?

In past years, across Xu in the south, Ji in the north, Qi and Lu, and the region of the Yellow and Luo rivers, wind and rain brought successive disasters. Plains became flooded expanses; crops and dwellings were swept away or submerged. Rice cost as much as pearls, and firewood as much as cassia. Half the common people, those innocent children, became fish and turtles—that is, perished in the floods. The officials responsible submitted successive memorials requesting aid. Through His Majesty’s immense compassion and sagacious planning, he showed his concern for the common people, specially released treasury funds, and dispatched envoys to travel throughout the affected areas distributing relief. He also granted the people varying degrees of land-tax relief.

Ah! Once the rain and dew of imperial favor fell, the withered returned to springtime life. His abundant bounty and profound benevolence spread throughout earth and heaven. The people, stroking their now-filled bellies, brimmed with renewed vitality. Great indeed is the imperial design! Does it not embody the twelve famine-relief measures of the Rites of Zhou?

From spring into summer, just as the people began to breathe freely again, floods and droughts followed one another. Reports of disaster once more multiplied throughout the metropolitan region and Qi and Lu, bringing renewed distress [?]. His Majesty compassionately examined matters in depth and anxiously applied himself to reflection. His sagacious commands were splendidly promulgated. He personally offered prayers and proclaimed to officials throughout the realm that they should earnestly examine their own faults. Then the fragrance of virtue rose radiantly on high…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇天鑒佑災異之運倏然豐稔矣猗歟休哉其
與成湯比隆者乎是故
上帝之昭事日嚴下民之陰隲愈厚我
皇上宵旰之憂誠可紓矣然災異靡常圖之貫
豫及是時修舉荒政非急務哉夫古者三
年耕必有一年之食九年耕必有三年之
食以三十年通計則雖有凶旱水溢民無
菜色是言民積當裕也王制曰國無三年
之蓄曰不足無六年之蓄曰急無九年之
===
蓄曰國非其國是言國積當豐也是故官
爲歛散善矣與其爲管仲未若爲周禮之
委積減價濟民善矣與其爲陳堯佐未若
爲耿壽昌之常平上蹝罷餞善矣與其爲
韓昌平無若爲戴冑之義倉長孫平朱元
脢之社倉蓋積貯者天下之大命無積貯
則無命矣徹桑土於未雨防氷至於履霜
爲國者可無經常之要策哉必不得已則
彷備旱於臧文如省發勸分曾國饑而不
punctuated: 皇天鑒佑，災異之運倏然豐稔矣。猗歟休哉！其與成湯比隆者乎？是故上帝之昭事日嚴，下民之陰隲愈厚，我皇上宵旰之憂誠可紓矣。然災異靡常，圖之貫豫，及是時修舉荒政，非急務哉？夫古者三年耕必有一年之食，九年耕必有三年之食，以三十年通計，則雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。是言民積當裕也。《王制》曰：「國無三年之蓄曰不足，無六年之蓄曰急，無九年之蓄曰國非其國。」是言國積當豐也。是故官爲歛散，善矣；與其爲管仲，未若爲《周禮》之委積。減價濟民，善矣；與其爲陳堯佐，未若爲耿壽昌之常平。上蹝罷餞，善矣；與其爲韓昌平，無若爲戴冑之義倉、長孫平朱元脢之社倉。蓋積貯者，天下之大命；無積貯，則無命矣。徹桑土於未雨，防氷至於履霜，爲國者可無經常之要策哉？必不得已，則彷備旱於臧文，如省發勸分，曾國饑而不
translation_en:
…August Heaven perceived this and bestowed its protection: the course of calamities and anomalies suddenly gave way to abundant harvests. Ah, how splendid! Does this not rival the glory of Cheng Tang? Thus the reverent service rendered to the Lord on High grows daily more solemn, and the unseen protection afforded the common people grows ever more generous. Our Emperor’s anxieties, which keep him occupied from before dawn until late at night, may truly be eased. Yet calamities and anomalies are unpredictable, and provision must be made beforehand [?]. Is it not an urgent task to restore and implement famine relief measures at this time?

In antiquity, three years of cultivation necessarily yielded provisions for one year in reserve, and nine years of cultivation yielded provisions for three years. Reckoned over thirty years, this meant that even when severe droughts or floods occurred, the people showed no signs of starvation. This means that the people’s reserves should be ample. The “Royal Regulations” states: “If a state lacks reserves for three years, this is called insufficiency; if it lacks reserves for six years, this is called urgency; if it lacks reserves for nine years, the state is no longer truly a state.” This means that the state’s reserves should be abundant.

For officials to collect and distribute grain is good; yet rather than follow Guan Zhong, it would be better to establish the stores prescribed in the Rites of Zhou. To reduce prices to relieve the people is good; yet rather than follow Chen Yaozuo, it would be better to establish Geng Shouchang’s ever-normal granaries. The measure transcribed as 上蹝罷餞 [?] is good; yet rather than follow Han Changping [?], it would be better to establish Dai Zhou’s charitable granaries and the community granaries of Zhangsun Ping and Zhu Yuanmei [?]. For stored reserves are the very lifeblood of all under Heaven: without reserves, there is no life. Gather mulberry roots before the rain falls; guard against the coming ice when first treading on frost. Can those who govern a state dispense with essential policies for its enduring needs?

If there is truly no alternative, then emulate Zang Wen in preparing for drought—for example, by inspecting conditions, distributing provisions, and encouraging people to share their resources, so that although the state suffered famine [?], it did not…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
害彷通榷於敬仲如矯制發粟河南困而
不凋彷平價於宣歙如設糜興造捐祿弛
鹽則青州兩浙梓州京東之瘵而未疲此
順變通於蠱極定機宜於一時是亦策之
權也夫經權之策審矣使地有遺利則蕩
無餘稼積散之間何所取焉若齊魯之崇
山巨浸青冀之環山距海埠多草萊濕爲
水壑尤可懼已是故招困離之民通水泉
之利陂塘濬其湮塞斗門時其啓閉墾
===
膽其工力虞集之捍水爲田何承矩之闢
草爲地獨不可取而行之乎然水利墾田
豊荒猶能病之他如錢鈔之法尚所當議
夫採歷山荊山以鑄錢幣堯湯爲之而有
泉布之號織楮成帛鈔之在漢唐宋也擅
皮幣飛錢便錢之名古人致世殷富未有
不須於此今楮幣廢於民用鑄錢滯於官
司銀貴傷農農傷則竭矣握利權以通錢
鈔又非備荒一策乎雖然語有之山木不
punctuated: 害，彷通榷於敬仲，如矯制發粟，河南困而不凋；彷平價於宣歙，如設糜興造、捐祿弛鹽，則青州、兩浙、梓州、京東之瘵而未疲。此順變通於蠱極，定機宜於一時，是亦策之權也。夫經權之策審矣，使地有遺利，則蕩無餘稼，積散之間何所取焉？若齊魯之崇山巨浸，青冀之環山距海，埠多草萊，濕爲水壑，尤可懼已。是故招困離之民，通水泉之利，陂塘濬其湮塞，斗門時其啓閉，墾膽其工力。虞集之捍水爲田，何承矩之闢草爲地，獨不可取而行之乎？然水利墾田，豊荒猶能病之。他如錢鈔之法，尚所當議。夫採歷山、荊山以鑄錢幣，堯湯爲之，而有泉布之號；織楮成帛，鈔之在漢唐宋也，擅皮幣、飛錢、便錢之名。古人致世殷富，未有不須於此。今楮幣廢於民用，鑄錢滯於官司，銀貴傷農，農傷則竭矣。握利權以通錢鈔，又非備荒一策乎？雖然，語有之：山木不
translation_en:
…cause harm; emulate Jingzhong in facilitating trade and managing monopolies, as when grain was distributed under an unauthorized imperial command, so that Henan, though distressed, did not fall into ruin. Emulate the equalization of prices in Xuan and She: establish gruel kitchens, undertake construction projects, contribute official salaries, and relax restrictions on salt. Thus Qingzhou, Liangzhe, Zizhou, and Jingdong, though afflicted, were not exhausted. These measures accommodate change and restore circulation when decay has reached its utmost, determining what is appropriate to the circumstances of the moment. They, too, belong to the expedient use of policy.

Suppose that policies, both regular and expedient, have been carefully considered. If the land still has untapped resources, yet no surplus crops remain at all, what can be drawn upon for storage and distribution? Consider the lofty mountains and vast waters of Qi and Lu, or Qing and Ji, encircled by mountains and bordering the sea: the elevated ground is largely overgrown, while wet ground forms water-filled hollows. This is especially alarming. Accordingly, gather the distressed and displaced people, make the benefits of streams and springs accessible, dredge blocked reservoirs and ponds, and open and close sluice gates at the proper times; apply labor to reclamation [?]. Could we not adopt and implement Yu Ji’s method of keeping back water to make fields, and He Chengju’s method of clearing overgrowth to create farmland?

Yet even with irrigation and land reclamation, fluctuations between abundance and famine can still cause distress. Other measures, such as the system of coin and paper currency, also warrant discussion. Yao and Tang mined Mount Li and Mount Jing to cast money, which bore the name quanbu. Paper mulberry was woven into cloth [?]; under the Han, Tang, and Song, currency bore such names as ‘leather money,’ ‘flying money,’ and ‘convenience money.’ When the ancients brought prosperity to the realm, they invariably relied upon these means. Now paper currency has fallen out of use among the people, while the casting of coins is held up in government offices. Dear silver harms farmers; when farmers are harmed, resources are exhausted. Would taking control of the sources of financial profit to facilitate the circulation of coin and paper currency not also be a policy for preparing against famine? Nevertheless, there is a saying: ‘The trees of the mountains cannot…’

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
能供市斧勺源難以潤尾閭可以喻治也
令冗員汰矣而糜費有十倍於冗員者出
馬敎民節矣而工費有百倍於民用者出
焉獨可無憂乎然則節財足民尤備荒者
不可不講也雖然不可必者時也不可泥
者法也荒政之興廢亦存乎人何如耳誠
使當事者存眞實愛民之心立平易近民
之政一日而思百年之計豐年而慮盈戌
之饑毋避聚斂之名而市恩以干譽毋逼
===
遷陟之期而倍入以取盈飭倉廩以乂收
藏嚴簿書以恒稽察定戶口以便賑貸水
利墾荒期於成功錢法鈔法期於通利荒
政尚亦有賴矣雖然責千將以納屨不若
一鏄之利而騄駬不試以鞚靮者信其能
千里也故漢中歲饑而郡守發粟至以細
過逮及也
太祖嘉之兩淮饑饉而陶令借糧人方以爲危
也
punctuated:
能供市斧，勺源難以潤尾閭，可以喻治也。令冗員汰矣，而糜費有十倍於冗員者出馬；敎民節矣，而工費有百倍於民用者出焉，獨可無憂乎？然則節財足民，尤備荒者不可不講也。雖然，不可必者時也，不可泥者法也。荒政之興廢，亦存乎人何如耳。誠使當事者存眞實愛民之心，立平易近民之政，一日而思百年之計，豐年而慮盈戌之饑，毋避聚斂之名而市恩以干譽，毋逼遷陟之期而倍入以取盈，飭倉廩以乂收藏，嚴簿書以恒稽察，定戶口以便賑貸，水利墾荒期於成功，錢法鈔法期於通利，荒政尚亦有賴矣。

雖然，責千將以納屨，不若一鏄之利；而騄駬不試以鞚靮者，信其能千里也。故漢中歲饑，而郡守發粟，至以細過逮及也，太祖嘉之；兩淮饑饉，而陶令借糧，人方以爲危也。
translation_en:
…supply the axes of the marketplace; a spoonful of spring water can scarcely moisten the ocean’s outlet. These sayings may illustrate the work of government. Suppose redundant officials have been dismissed, yet wasteful expenditure arises amounting to ten times their cost [?]; the people have been taught frugality, yet expenditure on construction arises amounting to a hundred times what the people use. Can this really give no cause for concern? Economizing on expenditure and ensuring the people’s sufficiency are therefore matters that those preparing against famine must especially examine. Nevertheless, the seasons cannot be counted upon, nor should methods be followed rigidly. Whether famine administration flourishes or falls into neglect also depends upon the character of those responsible. If those in charge truly cherish the people and establish straightforward, accessible government; if they consider a century’s needs in a single day and, in abundant years, anticipate famine [?]; if they do not avoid the reputation of being rapacious merely to purchase favor and seek praise, or, as the time for their promotion approaches, double their exactions to fill their quotas; if they put granaries in order to manage receipts and storage, maintain rigorous accounts for regular inspection, and establish household registers to facilitate relief and loans; and if they pursue irrigation and reclamation to completion and make the systems of coinage and paper currency circulate effectively—then famine administration will have something to depend upon.

Nevertheless, requiring the sword Ganjiang [?] to stitch shoes is less effective than using a single awl [?]. The reason one does not test the steed Lü’er by its bridle and reins is that one trusts its ability to travel a thousand li. Thus, when famine struck Hanzhong and the prefect distributed grain, even when he came to be arrested for a minor fault, Taizu praised him. When famine struck the Lianghuai region and Magistrate Tao borrowed grain, people were just then considering his action perilous…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
成祖美之故曰天下之政舉而成之任人天下
之才作而成之在君也雖然猶未也先王
祈天永命尚有所以感通之道焉禮曰用
水火金木惟特合男女頒爵祿必當故邦
無水旱昆虫之災爲政當順五行脩五事
以安百姓朱熹亦嘗言之故禹陳吉凶影
響之謀而曰善政養民皐陶陳聰明明畏
之謨而曰安民則惠必
廟堂敦茅茨之風
===
朝著崇羔羊之節不急之務罷焉無藝之征
緩焉內外協於勤恤
上下一於恭敬則太和洋溢休徵備至歲月日
時無易雨暘寒燠以時洪範所謂百穀用
成家用平康者將在是矣區區備荒之術
似不必講也
punctuated: 成祖美之。故曰：「天下之政，舉而成之任人；天下之才，作而成之在君也。」雖然，猶未也。先王祈天永命，尚有所以感通之道焉。《禮》曰：「用水火金木惟特，合男女，頒爵祿，必當，故邦無水旱昆虫之災。」爲政當順五行，脩五事，以安百姓，朱熹亦嘗言之。故禹陳吉凶影響之謀，而曰：「善政養民。」皐陶陳聰明明畏之謨，而曰：「安民則惠。」必廟堂敦茅茨之風，朝著崇羔羊之節，不急之務罷焉，無藝之征緩焉，內外協於勤恤，上下一於恭敬，則太和洋溢，休徵備至，歲月日時無易，雨暘寒燠以時。《洪範》所謂「百穀用成，家用平康」者，將在是矣。區區備荒之術，似不必講也。
translation_en: …Chengzu praised him for it. Thus it is said: “To undertake and accomplish the government of All-under-Heaven depends on appointing men; to awaken and perfect the talents of All-under-Heaven rests with the ruler.” Yet even this is not enough. In praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate, the former kings also possessed a way to move Heaven and elicit its response. The Book of Rites says: “In employing water, fire, metal, and wood, observe their particular requirements [?]; in joining men and women in marriage and distributing ranks and stipends, everything must be fitting. Thus the state will suffer no disasters from floods, droughts, or insects.” Zhu Xi, too, once said that governing requires following the Five Phases and cultivating the Five Activities, so as to bring peace to the common people. Thus Yu, in presenting his counsel on how good and ill fortune follow conduct like shadows and echoes, said: “Good government nourishes the people.” Gao Yao, in presenting his counsel on Heaven’s perceptiveness and its manifest majesty, said: “Bring peace to the people, and they will be compliant.” The court must cultivate the simplicity of thatched dwellings, and its officials must honor the integrity celebrated in “The Lamb’s Fur.” Nonessential undertakings must be discontinued, and unbounded exactions eased. Officials within and outside the capital must cooperate in diligent care for the people, and those above and below must be united in reverence. Then supreme harmony will overflow, and every auspicious sign will arrive; years, months, days, and seasons will proceed without disruption, and rain, sunshine, cold, and warmth will come at their proper times. What the “Great Plan” calls “the hundred grains ripening, and households enjoying peace and well-being” will then be realized. The petty techniques of preparing for famine would seemingly no longer need discussion.

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
維
皇上御極四載秋八月山東鄉試
士御史周〔詠〕監臨祗悉提調
監試簾內外百執事靡不恭
肅事竣錄士姓名并文以
獻〔登庸〕謹序末簡維多士督學
憲臣所精選三試拔其尤益
精矣行登南宮對
===
大廷爲世用予言之事君先資
其言拜自獻其身以成其信
今多士之文先資之言也種
種備矣請約之夫士任重道
遠非爲有脩齊治平寄與其
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

維皇上御極四載，秋八月，山東鄉試士。御史周〔詠〕監臨，祗悉提調、監試、簾內外百執事，靡不恭肅。事竣，錄士姓名并文以獻。〔登庸〕謹序末簡。

維多士，督學憲臣所精選，三試拔其尤，益精矣。行登南宮，對大廷，爲世用。予言之：事君先資其言，拜自獻其身，以成其信。今多士之文，先資之言也，種種備矣。請約之。夫士任重道遠，非爲有脩齊治平寄與其
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the fourth year of His Majesty’s reign, in the eighth month, in autumn, Shandong held its Provincial Examination for scholars. Censor Zhou Yong 周詠 served as Supervising Official. The Proctors, examination monitors, and all officials serving inside and outside the examination curtain were without exception reverent and solemn [the preceding 祗悉 is unclear]. When the proceedings were completed, the scholars’ names and compositions were recorded for presentation to the throne. I, Dengyong 登庸, respectfully compose this postface on the closing leaves.

These scholars had been carefully selected by the censorial official supervising education. Through three examination sessions, the most outstanding were chosen, making the selection still more exacting. Soon they will proceed to the Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination, answer questions at the Palace Examination, and enter the service of the realm. I say to them: in serving one’s ruler, one first offers one’s words as a basis for appraisal, then bows and offers oneself [?], thereby making good one’s pledge. The compositions these scholars have now submitted are those preliminary words; they cover every sort of subject. Allow me to state their essentials. A scholar’s burden is heavy and his road long. Is this not because the tasks of cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world are entrusted to him [?] …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
遵備載大學一書經夫子言
傳曾子意大聖大賢爲萬世
開太平者也萬世信之宜若
著蔡夷考其論釋治平厥義
維絜矩厥事維用人理財二
者參陳對舉不一而足他無
所及爲政在人是矣財用何
急急也聚人曰財是矣他務
===
何寥寥也蓋懋遷有無化居
烝民乃粒萬邦作乂上世所
謂財也有土有財者也非若
後世斂民之有以貯于國俾
充用度爲府庫財矣廵其稼
穡移用其民以救其時事阜
punctuated: 遵備載《大學》一書，經夫子言，傳曾子意，大聖大賢爲萬世開太平者也。萬世信之，宜若著蔡。夷考其論釋治平，厥義維絜矩，厥事維用人理財，二者參陳對舉，不一而足，他無所及。爲政在人，是矣，財用何急急也？聚人曰財，是矣，他務何寥寥也？蓋懋遷有無，化居，烝民乃粒，萬邦作乂，上世所謂財也。有土有財者也，非若後世斂民之有以貯于國，俾充用度，爲府庫財矣。廵其稼穡，移用其民，以救其時事，阜
translation_en:
… [the opening character 遵 is doubtful] are fully set forth in the single book, the Great Learning. Its classic text contains the words of Confucius; its commentary conveys the meaning of Zengzi. These were the great sage and great worthy who opened the way to peace for all generations. That all generations should trust them ought to be manifest [?]. Yet upon examining its discussion and explanation of governing the state and bringing peace to the world, its guiding principle is that of the measuring square—judging how to treat others by what one would wish for oneself—and its practical concerns are employing people and managing wealth. These two are repeatedly presented together and paired for discussion; nothing else is addressed. That government depends on people is true; but why such urgency about financial resources? That wealth brings people together is true; but why is so little said about other affairs?
For promoting exchanges between those who have goods and those who lack them, putting accumulated goods into circulation, enabling the multitude to eat grain, and bringing the myriad states under good government constituted what antiquity called wealth. This is what is meant by having land and thus having wealth. It was unlike later ages, when what the people possessed was collected and stored by the state to meet its expenditures, becoming wealth held in treasury storehouses. To inspect their sowing and harvesting, to transfer and employ the people so as to meet the needs of the season, and to increase …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
民之財因以足國之用民富
而國益富上世所謂理財也
生衆爲疾者也非若後世量
出以爲入用之不給取之益
多以斂散爲理財矣理財關
係若是乎其重也欲致治平
誰能忽焉財誠理萬民遂生
===
養萬事遂經費王道備矣乃
其理財勞一心以度天下爲
之裁成輔相爲之脩其敎不
易其俗齊其政不易其宜豐
扎合天時淳鹵酌地利好惡
當人心上下四旁均齊方正
是則絜矩也非若後世任一
punctuated:
民之財，因以足國之用，民富而國益富，上世所謂理財也，生衆爲疾者也。非若後世量出以爲入，用之不給，取之益多，以斂散爲理財矣。理財關係若是乎其重也，欲致治平，誰能忽焉？財誠理，萬民遂生養，萬事遂經費，王道備矣。
乃其理財，勞一心以度天下，爲之裁成輔相，爲之脩其敎，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。豐扎合天時，淳鹵酌地利，好惡當人心，上下四旁，均齊方正，是則絜矩也。非若後世任一
translation_en:
…the people’s wealth, thereby providing enough for the state’s needs. When the people are wealthy, the state becomes wealthier still. This is what was called managing wealth in ancient times: having many producers and making production swift. It was unlike later ages, when revenue was determined by expenditure, and when spending exceeded available resources, ever more was extracted, so that collecting and disbursing came to be regarded as managing wealth. Such is the weighty importance of managing wealth! Who seeking orderly government and peace could neglect it? If wealth is indeed properly managed, all the people can secure their livelihood and sustenance, and all undertakings receive the funds they require. The Kingly Way is then complete.
In managing wealth, the ruler taxes his own mind to consider all under Heaven, regulating and assisting its workings. He cultivates instruction without changing local customs, and brings government into order without changing what suits local circumstances. Abundance and calamity [?] are brought into accord with Heaven’s seasons; fertile and saline soils [?] are considered in light of the advantages of the land; likes and dislikes accord with the people’s hearts. Above, below, and on all four sides, everything is balanced, aligned, and square. This is the principle of measuring with the carpenter’s square. It is unlike later ages, when rulers rely on …

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
切法把持推會已矣大學論
釋治平義維絜矩事維用人
理財他無所及豈欺我哉夫
子之教曰吾道一以貫之曾
子曰夫子之道忠恕而已矣
千載而下談者鑿空行者步
影試深思之大學經之一章
===
非夫子之一貫乎傳之十章
非曾子之忠恕乎聖賢授受
心法切近精實若此然則多
士先資宜無出此今海内多
事公私告匱理財爲急乃徵
輸未掃一切法以還
成憲偏苦農家民流田蕪郡邑彫
punctuated: 切法把持推會已矣。《大學》論釋治平，義維絜矩，事維用人、理財，他無所及，豈欺我哉？夫子之教曰：「吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」千載而下，談者鑿空，行者步影。試深思之：《大學》經之一章，非夫子之一貫乎？傳之十章，非曾子之忠恕乎？聖賢授受心法，切近精實若此，然則多士先資，宜無出此。今海内多事，公私告匱，理財爲急，乃徵輸未掃一切法以還成憲，偏苦農家，民流田蕪，郡邑彫
translation_en:
…merely wielding expedient measures to maintain control and contrive adjustments [?]. In expounding the governance of the state and the pacification of the world, the Great Learning treats, in principle, only the measuring-square rule of reciprocity and, in practice, only the employment of men and the management of wealth. It addresses nothing else: could it be misleading us? The Master's teaching says: “My Way has one thread running through it.” Master Zeng said: “The Master's Way is simply loyalty and reciprocity.” A thousand years later, those who discuss it fabricate empty notions, while those who practice it tread upon shadows. Consider it deeply: is not the single chapter of the Great Learning's classic text the Master's one unifying thread? Are not its ten chapters of commentary Master Zeng's loyalty and reciprocity? The teaching of the mind transmitted between sages and worthies is thus accessible, precise, and substantial. Surely, then, the primary resource of you assembled scholars should lie nowhere else.

Now there are many troubles throughout the realm, and both public and private resources are reportedly exhausted. Managing wealth is urgent. Yet in collecting and remitting taxes, expedient measures have still not been swept away to restore the established statutes. The burden falls disproportionately upon farming households; the people flee, the fields lie waste, and prefectures and counties decline…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
〈畋〉元氣索然識者有未能絜
矩嘆且
朝廷德意雨露也江南北生齒
林林總總異俗異宜町畦中
諸種也必町畦治九穀分斯
雨露有養一切法千條萬緒
紐結爲一如鞭然農家如受
===
羈靮然是以
朝廷屢下節省蠲免令惠逮在
官暨逐末也易獨逮農家也
難譬則甘雨清露空施于未
治之田也可勝惜哉儒貴行
道濟時今農困甚矣多士能
胥以絜矩理財先資成信是
punctuated:
〈畋〉，元氣索然，識者有未能絜矩嘆。且朝廷德意，雨露也；江南北生齒，林林總總，異俗異宜，町畦中諸種也。必町畦治、九穀分，斯雨露有養。一切法，千條萬緒，紐結爲一，如鞭然，農家如受羈靮然。
是以朝廷屢下節省蠲免令，惠逮在官暨逐末也易，獨逮農家也難。譬則甘雨清露，空施于未治之田也，可勝惜哉！儒貴行道濟時，今農困甚矣！多士能胥以絜矩理財，先資成信是
translation_en:
…[?], their vital energies utterly depleted. Discerning men lament the failure to apply the principle of the measuring square—judging others’ needs by one’s own. Moreover, the court’s benevolent intentions are like rain and dew. The teeming population north and south of the Yangzi, with differing customs and differing needs, resembles the various crops in cultivated plots. Only when the plots are put in order and the nine grains properly distinguished can rain and dew nourish them. The comprehensive method [?] binds a thousand strands and myriad threads into one, like a whip; farming households feel as though they have been put under bridle and rein.
Thus, although the court has repeatedly issued orders for economies and tax remissions, their benefits readily reach those in official service and those pursuing commerce, but reach farming households only with difficulty. It is as though sweet rain and pure dew were falling fruitlessly upon untended fields. How regrettable! What is prized in Confucian scholars is their ability to put the Way into practice and meet the needs of their age. Today the farmers’ distress is extreme! If you candidates can all administer finances according to the principle of the measuring square, making your initial resources truly effective [?], this…

title: 隆慶四年山東鄉試錄
text:
謂識時務是故先資庶富庶
富臻矣先資文教文教興矣
先資武功武功定矣不然元
氣且索他奚以爲滄溟岱嶽
涵元降神魯壥鄒井力本同
風縱觀多士先資言類崇正
尚實其質布帛其味菽粟知
===
有俊傑者出馳孔曾康莊齊
天下開太平因不自量爲約
之維多士其永念哉
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教
諭余登庸謹序
punctuated:
謂識時務。是故先資庶富，庶富臻矣；先資文教，文教興矣；先資武功，武功定矣。不然，元氣且索，他奚以爲？滄溟岱嶽，涵元降神；魯壥鄒井，力本同風。縱觀多士，先資言類，崇正尚實，其質布帛，其味菽粟。知有俊傑者出，馳孔曾康莊，齊天下，開太平。因不自量，爲約之。維多士其永念哉！
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教諭余登庸謹序。
translation_en:
…is what is meant by understanding the needs of the times. Thus, first furnish the means for a populous and prosperous society, and that condition will be attained; first furnish the means for literary and moral instruction, and such instruction will flourish; first furnish the means for military achievement, and such achievement will be secured. Otherwise, the vital energy will be exhausted: what could anything else accomplish?
The vast sea and Mount Dai embrace primordial energy and send down numinous spirits. In the fields of Lu and the settlements of Zou, people share the custom of devoting themselves to agriculture, the fundamental occupation. Surveying the many candidates, I find that their statements on giving priority to resources [?] generally honor what is correct and esteem what is substantial. Their substance is like cloth and silk; their flavor is like beans and grain. I know that outstanding men will emerge from among them, travel the broad highway of Kongzi and Zengzi, bring order to all under Heaven, and inaugurate an age of great peace. Thus, presumptuous though it may be, I have drawn these points together for them. May you candidates keep them forever in mind!
Preface respectfully written by Yu Dengyong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.
